title: Beeline mints occurrenceID, independent of the field number
description:
Researched 2026-09-09. The standards separate two identifiers and Beeline currently conflates them.

dwc:catalogNumber is the collection's number and may change; dwc:otherCatalogNumbers is defined as 'previous or alternate ... catalog numbers ... for the same Occurrence' and is the mechanism for recording a superseded one. Symbiota enforces catalogNumber unique per collection and offers tagged additional identifiers ('Previous Catalog Number').

dwc:occurrenceID is the persistent global identity. GBIF treats a changed one as a NEW record: fresh gbifID, fresh URL, old one deprecated. Since 2022 GBIF pauses ingestion when more than half the occurrenceIDs in a version differ from the previous one, opens an issue and emails the publisher; an intentional change is migrated by supplying a CSV of old->new so gbifIDs and URLs carry over.

The defect: the reference implementation derives Oregon's occurrenceID FROM the field number (https://osac.oregonstate.edu/OBS/OBA_${fieldNumber}). So the persistent identifier is a function of the mutable one. If a field number can ever change, the derived URI either changes with it (the expensive GBIF case) or fossilises and then lies about which specimen it names - and the corpus shows the second happening 592 times (beeline-1kb.14). Washington's Ecdysis catalogNumber (WSDA_...) is likewise derived, and Symbiota generates its own UUID occurrenceID.

Proposal: Beeline mints occurrenceID once per specimen as its own value, opaque and independent of the field number, at the same moment it mints the field number - and the field number becomes only a catalogNumber-shaped label identifier. Then renumbering costs an otherCatalogNumbers entry rather than a GBIF migration.

Consequence for ADR 0008 worth naming: with an independent occurrenceID, renumbering stops being catastrophic downstream, which weakens one of the arguments that ADR uses against Arthur's account ('every published catalog number is one renumbering away from stale'). The ADR should say so rather than keep an argument this undermines. It does not decide the ADR - a pin bearing two labels is still ambiguous - but the downstream cost was overweighted.

Open: whether OSAC wants to keep issuing the URI form, and what Ecdysis/WSUC expect for Washington.
notes:
MINTING HALF BUILT 2026-09-17 (PR #74): specimen.occurrence_id, a UUID v7 minted at the freeze beside the field number, unique by index (migration 0031), NULL on every imported specimen. The export-side questions — whether OSAC keeps its URI form, whether Ecdysis accepts a supplied occurrenceID, and what to do with the 598 imported duplicates (1kb.14) — remain, in docs/questions.md Printing and mailing 7 and in ADR 0008's open questions; this bead stays open for them.

The three export-side questions are filed as gh-98 (2026-09-25) for Andony: OSAC's URI as the occurrenceID or an alias, Ecdysis accepting a supplied one, and whether the 598 duplicates have been published. ADR 0008 amended in PR #97 to say a URI carrying the field number is admissible if minted once and never re-derived.

title: occurrenceID is not unique in the legacy corpus: 216 URIs on 598 records
description:
Found 2026-09-09 while researching how Ecdysis/GBIF handle relabelling.

dwc:occurrenceID is the identifier GBIF treats as the record's persistent identity; it must be globally unique. In the legacy dump it is not: 216 occurrenceID values appear on more than one record, covering 598 records, with one URI (https://osac.oregonstate.edu/OBS/OBA_25016980) on 51 of them.

The same phenomenon from the other side: 592 records carry an OSAC URI whose embedded number is not the record's own fieldNumber. The reference implementation mints it as .../OBA_${fieldNumber} but only when the field is empty (ObservationsSubtaskHandler.js, the occurrence[occurrenceId] || ... guard), so a URI that has been copied onto another record is never corrected and keeps the number it was born with. Cause not yet established; the sha256-of-mutable-business-data primary key that inserts duplicates on edit is the obvious suspect, as is a CSV round-trip.

Why P1: Oregon publishes to GBIF manually after the embargo (CONTEXT.md), so this is very likely caught BEFORE publication rather than after — which is the cheap moment. If it ever reaches GBIF, records sharing an occurrenceID collapse or are rejected, and untangling them afterwards means the occurrenceID migration process (a publisher supplies GBIF a CSV mapping old to new and GBIF migrates the gbifIDs) rather than an edit.

Not a renumbering fingerprint, which is what the query was originally looking for: a shared URI is a copy, not a specimen that changed number. It says nothing about beeline-1kb.5.

Next: establish the cause, decide whether Beeline mints occurrenceID itself (see beeline-1kb.14), and check whether any of these have already been published.
notes:
CORRECTED 2026-09-09, and the diagnosis is worse than filed.

Figures wrong in the description:
- The worst-case value on 51 records is a BARE number, 7842549, not an OSAC URI. My original report said 'one URI on 51 of them' and conflated two populations.
- Two populations, not one. 139 records carry non-URI occurrenceIDs and share only NINE distinct values between them. The URI population is 273,651 records over 273,399 distinct values, 252 surplus; the widest duplicated URI is .../OBA_25016980 on 29 records.
- catalogNumber in the dump has no WSDA_ values at all (2,906 non-empty, zero prefixed). The prefix is Ecdysis's shape, not the dump's.

The 592 mismatched URIs are NOT stale, which is what the description assumed. Every one of the 592 embeds a field number that belongs to another REAL record, and they fall in contiguous blocks with a constant offset: 214 consecutive field numbers 25056482-25056695 all carry a URI offset by exactly 6,899; 132 at 25056954-25057293 offset 6,772; 46 offset 6,759; and so on, every block inside 25055898-25057412.

That is the fingerprint of a misaligned assignment pass, not of the sha256 primary key I guessed at: two ordered sequences zipped together with a shifted start, which #indexOccurrences could produce if occurrenceIDs were assigned over a differently ordered or differently sized set than the field numbers. It is confined to one narrow band of 2025 numbers, so it looks like a single bad run.

Why this is worse than stale: a stale URI names nobody. These name SOMEBODY ELSE. If published, record A asserts the identity of record B, and GBIF would see two records claiming one occurrenceID while the specimen those numbers actually describe is a different bee. Untangling that after publication is the occurrenceID migration process, not an edit.

Still true: Oregon publishes manually after the embargo, so this is very likely pre-publication. Next step is to confirm the band against print-run dates and check whether anything in it has shipped.

Whether any of the 598 has been published is question 3 on gh-98 (2026-09-25), filed for Andony.
PUBLICATION CHECKED 2026-10-01: none of it has shipped. OSAC publishes Oregon to GBIF from its own IPT (Oregon Bee Atlas, GBIF 1fa69ff3-3e40-465f-927f-12b1484d3731, archive https://osac.oregonstate.edu/ipt/archive.do?r=osac-oba). The 2026-07-28 release holds 64,913 records, nothing after the 2024 season, no identifier twice. Against the corpus fetched 2026-09-28 (now 204 duplicated identifiers on 574 records: 438 OR 2025 records on 198 OSAC URIs, 136 2024 records in OR/ID/WA on six bare numbers), none of the 204 and none of the 592 misembedded URIs are in it. The bare numbers appear on GBIF only as unrelated publishers' records (7842549 is an Estonian woodcock). Deadline: the 2025 season goes out at OSAC's next annual update. Separate finding filed as beeline-1kb.22 (4,636 published Oregon records whose GBIF occurrenceID differs from the corpus's).

title: The backup token expires 2026-12-01, in cutover month, and fails quietly
description:
The scheduled backup on maderas authenticates to Fly with an SSH-scoped token minted 2026-09-02 with a 90-day expiry (`fly tokens create ssh --app beeline --expiry 2160h`). It expires **1 December 2026**. When it does, scripts/backup-authored-files.sh stops being able to reach the volume and the nightly copy of the authored history stops.

Two things make this worse than a routine rotation.

**The date collides with cutover.** The roadmap puts cutover in December 2026: the blow-away era ends, minted field numbers become permanent, and backups stop being optional. The token lapses in the same weeks the backup first genuinely matters, and while everyone's attention is on the cutover itself.

**The failure is quiet.** /healthz/jobs (beeline-6td) watches the app's in-process scheduler; this cron runs on maderas and is invisible to it. The run exits non-zero and writes to stderr, so cron mails — but only into the local spool unless the host has a working MTA and a MAILTO that reaches somebody, neither of which is established. The mail-independent signal documented in the runbook is the age of the newest archive:

    find ~/beeline-backups -name 'beeline-authored-*.tar.gz' -mtime -2 | head -1   # silence = stale

Nobody runs that on a schedule.

Options, roughly in order of how much they fix:

- Re-mint now with an expiry that does not land in cutover month — cheapest, and turns a collision into an ordinary rotation. Trades a longer-lived credential for not having this fail during the week it matters most.
- Have something watch the backup the way /healthz/jobs watches the app: a check that the newest archive is younger than two days, run somewhere that can shout. It would cover far more than the token — a full disk, a broken flyctl, a revoked credential, maderas being down.
- Fold both into beeline-8w6.1's Sentry work if that lands first, which is the tidier home.

Related: beeline-6td covered exactly this class of silent failure inside the app and deliberately stopped at the app boundary.
close_reason: Merged in #52; token rotated (expires 2027-03-09), age check in maderas cron, poll line fixed. Mail-path decision carried in the bead's last comment.

comments.author: Peter Abrahamsen
comments.text: Rotated 2026-09-10: new SSH-scoped token (180 days, expires 2027-03-09) installed on maderas in ~/.config/beeline/backup-env with BEELINE_FLY_TOKEN_EXPIRES beside it; proven with a live backup; the 1 December token is revoked. PR #52 adds the two-week expiry warning, a loud flyctl failure, and scripts/check-backup-age.sh for cron. Two findings that outlive this bead: (1) the /healthz/jobs poll cron line never ran — crontab treats % as newline, printf "%s" broke it; fixed to echo in the live crontab and runbook; (2) cron mail on maderas does not reach anyone: no MAILTO, exim4 internet-mode with no smarthost, and a test to Gmail timed out on SMTP over IPv6 (Linode port 25?). Every alarm lands in ~/Maildir on maderas. Decision needed on a mail relay or another channel (beeline-8w6.1 Sentry is the tidier home). After merge: git pull on maderas and add the check-backup-age cron line. Close when merged.

title: A failing nightly is visible only to an admin who opens /jobs
description:
The nightly pipeline failed on every run for about half a day (2026-09-02, DuckDB OOM at the configured memory_limit) and nothing said so. job_run records it and /jobs displays it, but only to an admin who goes looking. It was caught by accident, while reading the boot log to confirm an unrelated migration had applied.

The gap matters more than the incident: ingestion is how observations become samples, so a silent stall means volunteers' records stop arriving while the site looks entirely healthy. /healthz answers 200 throughout — it proves HTTP, and beeline-2c3.17 would make it prove the store is readable, but neither would notice a job that has not run.

Two things are wanted and they are separable. A run that fails should reach somebody who is not already looking. And a job that has not succeeded within its expected interval should be distinguishable from one that has never been scheduled — the failure mode here ended with the scheduler giving up after four retries, which looks identical to quiet from the outside.

Cheap options worth weighing before building anything: the /jobs page could carry a staleness marker rather than only a history; the app could log at a level a Fly alert can match; or beeline-8w6.1's Sentry integration could take it, which is the tidier home if that lands first.

Found while deploying #40.
notes: 2026-09-10: PR #41 built /healthz/jobs (staleness per registered job, non-200 when any is wrong) and docs/runbooks/deploy-fly.md carries the external poll line. What remains is confirming the poll is installed on a checker host; nothing in the repo can show that. Close once it is.

title: Shutdown does not wait for a running job, and can skip the checkpoint
description:
src/app/main.ts's signal handler calls scheduler.stop(), which is clearIntervals only, then server.close(cb) whose callback does jobConn.closeSync() and await close(). Two problems, both worst at 2am.

A night-window job (the nightly pipeline, the Sunday sweep) may be mid-transaction on jobConn when the signal arrives. Nothing waits for it and nothing interrupts it: closeSync() is called on a busy connection.

The callback is async, so if closeSync() throws on that busy connection the rejection is unhandled, Node exits without reaching await close(), and DuckDB is never checkpointed. That is the uncheckpointed-WAL state that DuckDB <= 1.5.5 can fail to replay, leaving the store unopenable (beeline-c1b).

Pre-existing, not introduced by the Fly work, but the Fly move raises the odds: host maintenance restarts a machine with little warning and can land inside the 2am window. Found by adversarial review of PR #35.

Wanted: shutdown that interrupts or awaits the in-flight job before closing, and that cannot lose the checkpoint to a throw in the close path.
close_reason: Merged in #52 (ca3062d) and deployed to Fly 2026-09-10.

comments.author: Peter Abrahamsen
comments.text: PR #52 (branch shutdown-and-backup-token). scheduler.stop() now awaits the running job: 60s grace, then the JobContext signal aborts (step() refuses at boundaries; syncINat checks before every page) and conn.interrupt() cancels a running query so the transaction rolls back. main.ts checkpoints both catalogs explicitly and closes on a path reached whatever threw. Verified live: SIGTERM 1s into a three-project sweep on a fresh store, exit 0, no WAL, store reopens with all loads. Close when merged.

title: qc_finding scans cost 1.1s: a regex read from a view is recompiled per row
description:
beeline-oyq gave the street-suffix word list one home — a one-row view read as
`(SELECT pattern FROM locality_street_suffix_pattern)` — and in doing so took
qc_rule_locality_format from 16 ms back to 1.1 s over the dev store's 67,304
localities. The whole qc_finding union went with it: 1,120 ms against the 25 ms
ADR 0001 records, and every QC read in the app goes through that union (the QC
home, both listings, printability, both record pages).

CAUSE: DuckDB compiles a regex once when the pattern argument is a literal and
once PER ROW when it is anything else. A scalar subquery is anything else —
even `(SELECT '<literal>')` measures 1.1 s. Pattern length matters too, because
what is repeated is the compile: beeline-4dt's longer pattern took the same
query to 1.7 s.

MEASURED on the dev store (2026-08-29), same store, same predicate:

  (SELECT pattern FROM the view)   1,077 ms
  macro / inline literal              18 ms

FIXED in beeline-4dt: locality_street_suffix_pattern becomes a MACRO, which the
binder expands to a literal, keeping the one home and giving the compiler its
constant back. qc_finding is 34 ms again. ADR 0001's third named exception —
a threshold in a one-row view (elevation_derivation_limit) costs nothing,
because nothing is compiled; a pattern is different in kind.

Filed for the record rather than as open work: found and fixed in the same
change, because that change made it worse and touched the same line.
close_reason: Landed in #27 (squashed as dd950f8).

title: Samples have no change history: every writer overwrites silently
description:
Peter, 2026-08-29: "half of the point of this entire rewrite is to get
auditable history of changes and overrides on samples."

ADR 0007 settled the shape for PEOPLE and the first instance shipped
(beeline-o22, data/person-change.csv). Samples have nothing. Every writer
overwrites in place and leaves no trace but the code that did it, which is
word for word the failure ADR 0007 was written about:

  "Legacy promotion mints people and binds accounts wholesale;
   ingest/promote-observations.sql rewrites inat_account.login whenever
   iNaturalist renames an account. Both used to leave no trace but the code
   that did it - which is exactly the class of change that silently bound
   three people to the wrong iNat account."

THE WRITERS, all silent today:
- ingest/promote-observations.sql:49 rewrites sample_location's coordinates,
  uncertainty AND source unconditionally, every night.
- ingest/mint-samples.sql creates samples and free-links observations
  (beeline-oyq), and fills descriptive fields.
- ingest/promote-legacy.sql creates every legacy sample.
- src/app/sample-edit.ts writes data/corrections.csv - keyed by staging Mongo
  _id, which is a replay overlay under ADR 0004, not a history, and covers
  only non-iNat samples.
- The staff override screen (beeline-oyq, blocked on beeline-6e9) will be the
  next one.

MEASURED, and this is what prompted it. Comparing every sample whose
coordinates came from iNaturalist against the pair the legacy dump staged for
the same observation (56,736 comparable): the staged values carry exactly four
decimal places so the export can only explain ~6 m, and yet

  under 1 m        3,202     export rounding
  1-20 m          29,940     rounding, mostly
  20-200 m        23,284     REAL movement, far too many to look at
  200 m - 2 km       130
  2-50 km            145
  over 50 km          35

Roughly 23,600 samples - a third of the linked corpus - hold coordinates that
differ from what the import recorded, and promotion resolved every one of them
silently. Those imported coordinates are the ones already printed on labels
(CONTEXT.md), so a label and a record can disagree with nothing recording
that they ever did. The extreme is a SIGN FLIP: sample 68866 staged at
-120.701 and now carrying +120.701, Oregon against central Asia.

SHIPPED AS A STOPGAP, not the answer: legacy_location_conflict
(ingest/promote-legacy.sql) names the 310 samples over 200 m, of which 6 are
in the open season. It describes a symptom, and it can only do so while the
staging that holds the original is still here - which is to say, until
cutover, which is exactly when this stops being recoverable.

THE REFERENCE, settled 2026-08-29. An earlier draft of this bead claimed a
sample has no stable reference and called that the hard part. WRONG, and Peter
cut through it in one line: "You're already looking up existing samples on
fetch and updating them, right?" Promotion re-identifies a sample on every run
- collector, sample number, observed date inside the sample's range
(schema/108, sample_mint_match) - with no stored key at all. That reconcile IS
the reference, and it survives a rebuild for exactly the reason person_ref
does: the store and the log both derive it from the same upstream facts rather
than from a surrogate the rebuild redraws.

MEASURED on the dev store, with the collector named the way the overlay names
a person (inat:<user_id>, else name:<display_name>, never entity_id):

  samples                                67,887
  distinct (person_ref, number, date)    67,887
  collisions                                  0
  samples that cannot be keyed                0

So it is unique and total, which none of the alternatives are:
- entity_id: a per-store sequence draw a rebuild redraws (beeline-ten).
- inat_observation_id: null on 6,367 samples, and NOT UNIQUE - 150
  observations are cited by two or more samples, since nothing constrains it.
  (Worth its own look; sample_multi_observation names the opposite case.)
- legacy staging _id: only legacy-staged samples, and it dies at cutover.

THE ONE REAL WRINKLE, and it is a solved shape rather than an open problem:
when a change moves the reference itself - a staff correction to the sample
number or the date, which is precisely a change the log wants to record - the
log has to follow it. ADR 0007 already specifies how, for the person case
where a rename moves person_ref: forward only, in file order, and never onto a
reference the log already knows somebody by, because treating a move as
evidence that two references ARE one record merges two of them the moment
their keys swap. Port that, do not reinvent it. 633 samples currently have an
observation disputing their number or date
(sample_observation_number_mismatch), which is the population that would
exercise it.

Worth carrying over wholesale from ADR 0007 once the reference is settled:
entries are DIFFERENCES computed by comparing the store against what the log
last said, through one function reading one query, so a writer that forgets is
caught by the next pass and attributed to that pass; state rather than
instructions; append-only in a file until cutover, then a table; read
leniently, written strictly.

ALSO WORTH DECIDING HERE, since it is the same question: whether promotion
should stop overwriting a materially different coordinate at all, rather than
recording that it did. Related, and blocked on the same engine problem:
beeline-6e9 (a sample's collector and atlas cannot be updated in DuckDB at
all), and beeline-oyq's note that a staff coordinate override currently
survives until the next nightly run and then vanishes, with sample_location's
'staff_entry' source - already in the CHECK vocabulary, written by nothing -
as the intended hook.
notes: The 'no stable reference' framing in the first draft of this bead was mine and it was wrong (2026-08-29). I went looking for a stored surrogate and concluded none existed, when the project's own answer - and the one already running in promotion's reconcile - is a reference DERIVED from the same upstream facts. Measured after the correction: (person_ref, sample_number, date_start) is unique across all 67,887 samples with zero unkeyable. The description now carries that; what remains is a reference that MOVES when somebody corrects a number or a date, which ADR 0007 already solved for renames and which should be ported rather than redesigned.
close_reason: Landed as #32: src/sample-change.ts, ADR 0007's second instance with the snapshot-baseline variation written into the ADR addendum. Every writer covered — legacy promotion, observation promotion (the nightly), boot, and the edit screen's narrowed authored pass — with history on /samples/:id. Reference is the derived triple; moves follow the observation link first; collisions and unreferenceable samples record nothing, are counted, and their snapshot rows are carried so resolution reconnects instead of re-arriving (CodeRabbit's catch). Measured: baseline 1.1s/11.2MB/0 entries; steady pass ~2s; 30 moves + 2 renumbers = exactly 32 entries. Overwrite policy split out as beeline-942. Baseline corpus deliberately has empty histories — the empty-state copy says the sample predates the log rather than that nothing happened (Peter: the copy is enough).

title: A sample's atlas and collector cannot be changed: DuckDB refuses to update an indexed column on a referenced row
description:
Found while building beeline-oyq's minting step, which tripped over it in a
statement the real corpus could not exercise.

DuckDB 1.5.5 will not UPDATE an INDEXED column on a row that an incoming
foreign key references. The update becomes a delete-and-insert, and the delete
trips the inbound check:

  Constraint Error: Violates foreign key constraint because key
  "sample_id: 8" is still referenced by a foreign key in a different table.

Every sample has a sample_collector row pointing at it, so for `sample` this
means:

  UPDATE sample SET locality = ...      OK   (unindexed column)
  UPDATE sample SET country = ...       OK   (unindexed column)
  UPDATE sample SET atlas_id = ...      FAILS (foreign key => indexed)
  UPDATE sample SET collector_id = ...  FAILS (foreign key => indexed)

THE RULE AS THE REPO CURRENTLY STATES IT IS TOO BROAD, and the sharper version
is worth having because it is the difference between "no descriptive refresh
is possible" and "all of them are". schema/010:56 and
migrations/0020:166 both say DuckDB "refuses to update a row an incoming
foreign key references". That is not what happens - `UPDATE atlas SET name`
succeeds on a row atlas_region references. What fails is
`UPDATE atlas SET inat_place_id`, and inat_place_id is BIGINT UNIQUE. So the
discriminator is an index on the column being written (PRIMARY KEY, UNIQUE, or
FOREIGN KEY), not the presence of an inbound reference alone. Both comments
should be corrected; they are currently used to justify not writing
atlas.inat_place_id, and that justification happens to still hold.

WHY IT MATTERS BEYOND TIDINESS. beeline-oyq's staff override screen exists
mainly to fix collector attribution: Emily Carlson's 254 records under
amelathopoulos, and the household logins where the account names the wrong
human about half the time. Reassigning a collector is exactly
`UPDATE sample SET collector_id`, which cannot be done. Same for moving a
sample between atlases, which beeline-2c3.20 and the border cases will want.

WHAT MINTING DID ABOUT IT, for now: nothing that helps the general case. The
atlas is set in the INSERT and never afterwards, and sample_atlas_unfilled
(schema/108) names the population that would need repairing - empty on the dev
store, and the reseed recipe fetches places before promoting to keep it that
way.

OPTIONS. MEASURED 2026-08-29 — SEE THE NOTE BELOW, which corrects two of these
and adds two the list did not have:
- Delete the child rows, update, reinsert, inside the transaction. DOES NOT
  WORK: the foreign key check reads committed state, so a child deleted in the
  transaction still counts as referencing. Succeeds only across separate
  autocommit statements, where a crash leaves a sample with no collectors.
- Drop the foreign key from sample_collector.sample_id and keep the invariant
  as a view, which the project already does for things the engine cannot hold
  (sample_primary_collector_mismatch, schema/116). NOT ENOUGH ON ITS OWN:
  sample_location, specimen and sample_promotion_finding reference sample too.
- Wait for DuckDB. Worth re-testing whenever it moves past 1.5.x, the same
  note migration 0007 leaves for ALTER TABLE RENAME COLUMN (beeline-c1b).

A test that pins the current behaviour would be worth having either way, so
that the day it changes is a day something tells us.
notes:
FIX UP AS PR #31 (branch the-sample-columns-that-could-not-change), 2026-08-30 — the structural option from the 2026-08-29 measurement, chosen by Peter over the cheap FK-drop:

- sample.collector_id dropped; primary collector IS sample_collector position 1, read through the new sample_primary_collector view (schema/100). schema/116 becomes sample_primary_collector_invalid (headless list, or two heads). Reassigning a collector is UPDATE sample_collector SET person_id, which works.
- atlas moves to sample_atlas (sample_id PK, atlas_id, assigned_by; CHECK atlas_id IS NOT NULL OR assigned_by IS NOT NULL — NULL atlas only as a human's "belongs to none"). The fill-only refresh drains sample_atlas_unfilled every promotion, so fetch-places-first ordering is no longer load-bearing.
- Reseed-only per ADR 0006; migrations 0001-0023 declared the pre-reseed epoch in migrations/README.md; the migration-walk test replaced by a drift-report pin.
- Control experiment: reseed+promote under old and new code — identical findings rule-for-rule, identical pending_print (1,117), all 67,887 samples' collector and atlas identical row by row.

Close when #31 merges and the sandbox reseed completes. Upstream duckdb/duckdb#20246 stays pinned by test on a scratch pair.
close_reason: Fixed structurally by #31 (1c46eea): sample.collector_id dropped — primary collector IS sample_collector position 1, read via the sample_primary_collector view (schema/100), with schema/116 slimmed to sample_primary_collector_invalid; atlas moved to the writable sample_atlas satellite, whose fill-only refresh drains sample_atlas_unfilled every promotion. Reassignment works both ways and is pinned by test: SET person_id for someone new, SET position (swap) to promote a listed co-collector. Reseed-only (ADR 0006); migrations 0001-0023 declared the pre-reseed epoch. Sandbox reseeded and swapped 2026-08-30, counts identical to the old store row for row, all alarms empty, healthz ok. Unblocks beeline-ewl and the staff override screen. Upstream duckdb/duckdb#20246 stays pinned on a scratch pair for the day it changes.

title: qc_rule_locality_format calls St Helens a street address
description:
qc_rule_locality_format (schema/120) tells 168 samples their locality "looks
like a street address" when it says "St Helens" or "St. Helens" — a town in
Columbia County, Oregon, and a perfectly good locality.

The street-suffix list carries `st` as the abbreviation for Street, and the
predicate matches it as a whole word between spaces. "St Helens" normalises to
" st helens " and hits. So does any Saint: St Paul, St Johns, Ste Genevieve.

MEASURED on the dev store (2026-08-29): 222 of the 4,100 locality_format
findings have a locality beginning "St " or "St. ". Of those, 168 are the bare
town name in two spellings:

  St Helens                                    121
  St. Helens                                    47

The remaining ~54 do contain a real street ("St. Helens Saulser Rd",
"St. Helens, Conibear Rd.") and are correctly flagged for that reason, not
this one — so the fix must not simply exempt anything starting with "St".

WHY IT MATTERS more than 168 rows: this is a self-service instruction. The
volunteer is told to fix something that is not wrong, and the only way to
satisfy the rule is to write the locality incorrectly. It is the one kind of QC
finding that actively damages data.

The rule is inherited: docs/reference-implementation.md records the same
seventeen words in OBP-Server, so the live system has the same false positive
and has had it for years. Whatever is decided here should be true of both.

WORTH CONSIDERING rather than prescribing:
- `st` is the only entry in the list that collides with a common word. `dr`
  (Drive vs Doctor) is the next nearest and does not appear in the corpus.
- A Saint is followed by a capitalised proper noun, where a Street is preceded
  by one — "St Helens" vs "Helens St". Requiring the suffix to be the LAST
  token, or at least not the first, would fix this class without a word list.
  That is worth measuring against the corpus before adopting: the rule's whole
  point is that a locality is a place name, not an address, and it is doing
  real work on the other 3,878 findings.

Found while measuring locality quality for beeline-oyq, which needs to know
how many minted samples get a usable locality. It is a live defect independent
of that work.
close_reason: Landed in #27 (squashed as dd950f8).

title: Read the 2018 sample-id and collection-method OFVs, and cache iNat places
description:
Minting samples from observations (beeline-oyq) needs three things the store
cannot do today, and all three are useful on their own. Split out so each is
reviewable, and so observation_place can be verified against the real corpus
before anything writes samples from it.

1. THE 2018 SAMPLE-NUMBER FIELD. `sampleId` is the 2019+ observation field.
   2018 used one literally named `sample id` — 1,636 observations, used by
   pandg, molfamily, ellenwatrous, tom_julie, patwheeler and ~40 others.
   It is not junk: 1,054 of its 1,532 usable values match an existing legacy
   sample on (collector, number, date). Nothing in Beeline or in the reference
   implementation reads it, which is part of why 2018 is thin.

   Extend `observation_current_fields.sample_number_raw` to coalesce the two,
   the same shape the count OFV already uses for `numberOfSpecimens` /
   `Number of bees collected`.

   Two things measured that the coalesce must NOT paper over:
   - 31 observations carry both fields and 14 of them DISAGREE. A view must
     name that rather than silently preferring one.
   - it is not purely 2018 (1,608 of 1,636 are; 20 are 2019-2026, 1 is 2017),
     and 72 of 296 distinct values are non-numeric and would print verbatim:
     `dto3`..`dto68`, `4/2`, `LD3`, `A1`, `block 134`,
     `NC. 6.   May 23, 2018`.

2. COLLECTION METHOD. `OBA Collection Method` covers 10,178 observations with
   a genuinely controlled four-value vocabulary: `net` (9,921), `pan trap`
   (149), `vane trap` (67), `nest block` (17). New column
   `collection_method_raw` on the view and on `observation_field`.

   It is also evidence owed to docs/questions.md, Trap sampling q3 (for
   Lincoln Best / Olivia Messinger-Carrill / Karen Wright): the project
   already runs a controlled protocol vocabulary on the iNat side, with no
   effort smuggled into the string, which is the failure mode that question
   names ("6 Vane Traps").

   NOT in scope, and measured to be useless for it: `Trap Installed` /
   `Trap Removed` (4,118 / 4,089 observations) hold a bare TIME OF DAY
   ("15:30", "4:31pm"), not a date. They give no trap date range.

   CAREFUL — `refreshObservationFields` does a POSITIONAL
   `INSERT INTO observation_field SELECT * FROM observation_current_fields`,
   and `observation_field_stale` compares with `EXCEPT` over `SELECT *`,
   which is also positional. A new TEXT column added anywhere but last swaps
   silently with `sample_number_raw` or `specimen_count_raw`, and the alarm
   built for exactly this cannot see it. New column goes LAST in both.

3. PLACES. A sample minted from an observation has no country/state/county,
   and `atlas_region` is a text lookup on the two-letter code. `place_guess`
   is free text ("Leach Botanical Garden", "Parkrose community orchard") and
   unparseable. `place_ids` is already whitelisted and stored: 2,556 distinct
   across the corpus. Verified against the live API — iNat places carry
   `admin_level` 0=country, 10=state, 20=county (Oregon=10, Benton County=20).

   - `inat_place` cache table (id, name, admin_level, ancestor_place_ids,
     fetched_at). Not an entity per ADR 0002 — nothing anchors on a place.
   - `src/fetch-places.ts` + `pnpm inat:fetch-places`: batched
     `GET /v1/places/{ids}`, unauthenticated, ~86 requests cold.
   - `observation_place` view resolving each observation to country / state /
     county by admin_level.
   - `atlas_region` gains a place id for all ~63 rows. NOTE
     `atlas.inat_place_id BIGINT UNIQUE` already exists (schema/010:43,
     Washington = 46) and covers only the six atlases; the other 57 regions
     need one too. Use BIGINT to match, and pin the six to agree by test.

   MUST NOT REPEAT beeline-oyq's near-miss: `inat_place` has to be added to
   `CARRIED_TABLES` in src/reseed-store.ts and `inat:fetch-places` to the
   reseed instructions, or every reseed silently loses the cache.

Also covered here, being documentation drift found while measuring: two stale
cross-references to a numbering docs/questions.md no longer uses —
schema/030_samples_specimens.sql:38 (`sample.protocol` → "T3") and :39
(`sample.sampling_effort` → "T6"). Both are Trap sampling q3 and q6.

DONE WHEN: `observation_place` reproduces the country/state/county of a
sample of real linked samples whose legacy geography is already known — that
comparison is the point of splitting this out, and it can be made before
anything mints.

Per ADR 0006 this needs migrations for the view, the new column, the new
table, `atlas_region`'s new column AND its ~63-row seed as UPDATEs (schema/010
seeds by INSERT; a deployed store already holds the rows). `src/model.ts`
follows the SQL by hand. `COMMENT ON` for every new table and column.
notes:
PR https://github.com/rainhead/beeline/pull/19 (2026-08-29). Landed the projection change (2018 'sample id' + OBA Collection Method), the inat_place cache with pnpm inat:fetch-places, observation_place/observation_place_ambiguous/inat_place_uncached, atlas_region.inat_place_id for all 64 regions, migration 0020, and 20 tests.

DONE-WHEN MET: observation_place agrees with the legacy import's state on 57,241 of 57,278 linked samples; every observation carrying any place ids resolves to a state (the 82 that do not carry none at all, 60 because geoprivacy is private); observation_place_ambiguous is empty on the real corpus.

Three findings worth carrying into beeline-oyq:
- 37 disagreements with the legacy import, and at least one is LEGACY being wrong: two Utah samples carrying CAN, exactly what qc_rule_place_unrecognised's comment predicted. Four more are WA/OR border cases where iNat reads coordinates and legacy was typed. A QC rule comparing a sample's stated geography against its observation's is now possible and is not filed.
- 3 place ids (59614, 117476, 186423) are named by observations and no longer resolve upstream - merged or deleted. Reported by the fetcher, never cached as a guess.
- Migration 0017's 'INSERT ... SELECT *' broke the moment the view grew a column, because a migration reads the view as the schema defines it TODAY. Both migrations now name their columns. Any future migration that fills a table from a view must do the same.
CodeRabbit round 1 (PR #19, 2026-08-29). Both findings real, both confirmed against the corpus, both fixed in b13e66c.

1. A BLANK sampleId swallowed the 2018 value. coalesce falls through on SQL NULL only, so a present-but-empty 'sampleId' won, projected as '', and took the real 'sample id' with it - silently, since the conflict view drops blanks too. 119 observations carry a blank sampleId; two (13342107, 13339586) carry sample numbers 187 and 181 that were being discarded. Guard went in the WHERE, not around the value, so the column stays verbatim as documented. Applied to the specimen-count arms too (349 blanks, none masking a value today - same rule, spelled the same way).

2. CARRIED_TABLES IS DECORATIVE. It is exported and read by nothing; carryStaging copies per-table by hand because three tables need ids or their sync_run reference rewritten. Adding inat_place to the list carried nothing, and the cache would have been dropped on every reseed - the exact failure the comment beside it claimed to prevent. GENERAL LESSON: a list that looks authoritative and is not. A test now asserts every name in CARRIED_TABLES arrives in a reseeded store, so the next table added cannot be forgotten in the copy.

Also: PR bodies in this repo are soft-wrapped (200-530 char lines); #19 shipped hard-wrapped at ~76 because the body was written in the same heredoc pass as the commit message. Rewritten unwrapped, and every cited document linked pinned to the commit SHA per the new CLAUDE.md rule, all 15 URLs verified 200.
close_reason: Merged as 8352034 (PR #19). The 2018 'sample id' and 'OBA Collection Method' OFVs are read; inat_place caches iNaturalist places with pnpm inat:fetch-places; observation_place resolves country/state/county and the two-letter code; atlas_region carries a verified place id for all 64 regions. Verified against the real corpus: derived state agrees with the legacy import on 57,241 of 57,278 linked samples, every observation with any place ids resolves to a state, observation_place_ambiguous empty. beeline-oyq is unblocked.

title: iNaturalist observations never create samples (roadmap phase 3 gap)
description:
Sync brings observations in; nothing turns one into a sample. Samples exist
only because LEGACY promotion minted them from the Mongo dump, and
ingest/promote-observations.sql starts every join from a sample that already
exists:

  CREATE OR REPLACE TEMP TABLE observer_collector_pair AS
  SELECT ... FROM sample s
  JOIN observation_field f ON f.inat_id = s.inat_observation_id

So observation promotion is a provenance UPGRADE on records the legacy dump
already supplied — believed-true coordinates, geoprivacy, observer→collector
account linkage — and never a source of records. An observation with no
matching legacy row is synced, shredded into observation_field, and stops
there.

MEASURED on the dev store, 2026-08-28 (a full reseed of the production dump
plus current sync):

  observations synced                                63,280
  linked to a sample                                 57,278
  linked to nothing                                   6,134
  ...of those, carrying BOTH a sampleId OFV and a
     'Number of bees collected' OFV — collection
     records by the project's own definition           4,453
  distinct observers among those                        458
  observers with no inat_account in the store           128

The newest are five days old (2026-08-23): ltauzer sample 2, mrthorn sample 4,
annebulger sample 2 / 12 bees. Some observers are people we know perfectly
well — their recent collecting produces nothing simply because the frozen dump
predates it.

WHY THIS IS P1 RATHER THAN A PHASE-3 TIDY-UP: docs/roadmap.md's deferred
section already states that "iNat and the legacy import are the only data
entry points", and at cutover (phase 8) the legacy import is frozen. From that
moment iNat is the ONLY entry point, and today it enters nothing. Everything
downstream — QC findings, printability, field numbers — is keyed to a sample,
so a season collected after the freeze would be invisible end to end rather
than visibly broken.

Not the same thing as beeline-v0j (the observer is not always the collector),
which assumes the sample exists and asks who to attribute it to.

DESIGN QUESTIONS THIS OPENS, none of them settled:
- Which observations are samples? sampleId + specimen count present is the
  obvious test, and 1,681 of the 6,134 unlinked ones lack one or both.
- What mints the sample number series for a collector who has no legacy rows?
- How does a sample created from an observation interact with the correction
  overlay (ADR 0004), which was designed for upstream data that moves?
- Deletion: observation_seen already proves presence (beeline-3hj) — does an
  observation disappearing retire its sample, or flag it?
- The unknown-observer case is its own decision: see the blocking bead.
design:
SETTLED DESIGN as of 2026-08-29. The Notes below are the working record —
five rounds of decisions, measurements and corrections, several of which
SUPERSEDE each other. Read this field for what to build; read the notes for
why, and for the numbers behind each claim.

## What exists already (beeline-2yt, merged, both stores current)

- observation_field.sample_number_raw coalesces 'sampleId' (2019+) with
  'sample id' (2018), blank treated as absent.
- observation_field.collection_method_raw carries 'OBA Collection Method'.
- inat_place caches iNaturalist places; pnpm inat:fetch-places fills it.
- observation_place resolves country / state / county / the two-letter code,
  preferring private_place_ids. observation_place_ambiguous is its alarm.
- atlas_region.inat_place_id is seeded for all 64 regions.

## The step

ingest/mint-samples.sql, called from promoteObservations INSIDE its existing
transaction. Pure function of observation_field + inat_place + the model;
idempotent; re-runnable, like the rest of that file.

PLACEMENT IS OPEN AND MATTERS: minting resolves the observer through
inat_account, which promote-observations.sql WRITES at its tail, and
inat:backfill-accounts writes again after promotion in the reseed recipe. Mint
at the head and each pass mints more, so "promotion twice mints the same
count" is not a property of the design. Either mint after the account harvest
(and re-run the location/geoprivacy statements over the new rows), or accept
the one-pass lag and test THAT.

## Which observations are samples

One view, shared with beeline-e85's unclaimed screen so both agree:

  non-blank sample_number_raw
  AND try_cast(specimen_count_raw AS INTEGER) > 0
  AND observed_on IS NOT NULL

Count zero is the project's own signal that nothing was collected — the
reference implementation's fan-out yields zero rows for those too.

## Reconcile, in this order

1. Resolve observer -> person via inat_account. Unresolvable: DO NOT MINT.
   sample.collector_id is NOT NULL and beeline-e85 argues for staging over a
   placeholder person. Name them in a view; e85's screen reads it.
2. Candidate whose inat_id already appears in sample.inat_observation_id:
   SKIP. Once linked, the link IS the identity — this is what stops an
   upstream sampleId edit minting a second sample, which is the reference
   implementation's sha256-primary-key bug.
3. Group the remainder by (person_id, sample_number, observed_on).
4. THE KEY IS A DATE RANGE, NOT date_start:
     observed_on BETWEEN sample.date_start AND sample.date_end
   A trap sample spans a range and its observation is dated on the END.
   Keying on date_start misses 20 samples that cite no observation — free
   links turned into duplicate collecting events, invisible because
   qc_rule_duplicate_sample_number also groups on date_start.
   - matched, sample has no inat_observation_id -> set it (free link; lowest
     inat_id where the group holds several, as legacy_sample_map's arg_min does)
   - matched, sample cites another observation -> do nothing
   - never touch an existing sample's number, date or count
5. No match -> mint one sample per group.

## What a minted sample carries

- collector_id: the resolved person; sample_collector position 1 the same
  person, so sample_primary_collector_mismatch stays empty. Taking the
  observer as collector is SETTLED: the household risk is 98% historical
  (2026: 9 household-login samples, 2 partner duplicates), and collectors are
  being moved to individual iNaturalist accounts.
- sample_number: the OFV verbatim, trimmed. Beeline never mints one.
- date_start = date_end = observed_on.
- specimen_count: SUM over the group. Caution: qc_rule_count_mismatch
  compares against the ONE linked member, so all 33 multi-observation groups
  are born flagged with both sides right. Decide before shipping.
- kind = 'net', protocol = 'aerial net', both CONSTANT. 56,937 of 57,278
  iNat-backed samples carry 'aerial net' whatever collection_method_raw says,
  and that field disagrees with the record about a third of the time where
  non-net. Do not derive either from it.
- country / state_province / county from observation_place; atlas_id from
  atlas_region on the two-letter code.
- locality: the first comma-separated component of place_guess that reads
  like a place name — 2 to 18 chars, no street suffix, not a bare state code
  or country, no postcode. 92% of 2026 samples get one. NOT the reference's
  exactly-three-parts rule, which manages 68% and refuses good data.
  PREREQUISITE: extract private_place_guess into observation_current_fields
  (the reference prefers it, as the coordinate rule prefers private_geojson).
  New column goes LAST — the refresh inserts positionally.
  BLOCKED ON beeline-4dt: the street-suffix list contains 'st', so "St
  Helens" reads as a street address. Fix that first or minting inherits it.
- host_inat_taxon_id / host_name_as_observed from the observation's taxon.
- geoprivacy and sample_location are left to the statements already in
  promote-observations.sql — they key on inat_observation_id, which step 5
  has just set. No new location or elevation-clearing code (beeline-x5c).

## Schema stance

sample.inat_observation_id stays scalar. No sample.origin, no
sample_observation list — so minting never rewrites an existing sample, which
is also what protects a staff edit to any field minting writes.

DESCRIPTIVE FIELDS ARE THE EXCEPTION and this is not yet designed: geography
must be an idempotent refresh keyed on inat_observation_id, or a reseed mints
1,441 samples with null geography that no later fetch can repair, because
minting never rewrites. Write-once is right for number/date/count and wrong
for everything descriptive.

## The editor

In scope, STAFF-GATED (not collector-gated — that is the volunteer path).
Its purpose is staff OVERRIDE where iNaturalist is wrong or silent and no
upstream edit helps: Emily Carlson's 254 records under amelathopoulos, the
household logins, anything the record must say that the observation does not.
Staff also fix things a volunteer could fix, on grounds of unreachability or
economy. Volunteer-facing findings still point upstream to iNaturalist.

MUST FIX WITH IT: ingest/promote-observations.sql:49 rewrites sample_location
unconditionally every run, including `source`, so it silently erases a staff
coordinate override. sample_location.source already carries 'staff_entry'
with nothing writing it — that is the hook. Open question: does an override
then win forever, including after the volunteer fixes the coordinates?

## Views to add

- the candidate predicate (above), shared with beeline-e85
- unminted: a candidate whose observer cannot be resolved
- unusable: has a sample number but zero/unparseable count or no date
- sample_observation_number_mismatch: a sample whose observation now reports a
  different number or date — the cost of never rewriting, made visible

Deletion needs no new rule: qc_rule_observation_missing_upstream covers it. A
minted sample is never retired when its observation disappears; minting is
additive only.

## Do not forget

src/model.ts by hand; migrations per ADR 0006 for every view and column;
COMMENT ON everything (pinned by test/schema.test.ts); volunteer-facing copy
in src/app/messages/, never literal in a view; pending_print_sample becomes
non-empty for the first time (schema/150 says so) and the QC home reads it;
sample_elevation_pending gains ~1,435 rows and the DEM tiles for them;
CLAUDE.md's promotion paragraph still says observation promotion is never a
source of records.

Ordering is unstated and unenforced: promote-legacy.sql does an unconditional
INSERT INTO sample with no anti-join, so inat:promote before legacy:promote on
a fresh store lets legacy re-insert what minting made.
notes:
MINTING MERGED to main as 2de8ed8 (PR #23, 2026-08-29), and applied to the dev store: pnpm db:migrate then pnpm inat:fetch-places then pnpm inat:promote against beeline.duckdb. 1,594 samples minted (up from the 1,421 measured before the day's sync brought 265 new observations), 1,111 free links, 3 ambiguous refused, 357 unresolvable observers, pending_print_sample 0 -> 1,134. A backup of the pre-mint store is outside the repo.

THE SOP LOOP WAS EXERCISED END TO END on a real record rather than a fixture, and it holds. Peter's observation 394571724 (2026-08-25, sample 1, 10 bees) arrived in the day's sync with place_guess 'Snohomish County, US-WA, US' - county-only, correctly refused, so the sample minted with locality NULL and blocked as missing_required_field. He edited it upstream to 'Verlot, WA, US'; the re-sync fetched 56 and stored 1 new load with 55 unchanged, i.e. exactly his edit; promotion then reported samplesMinted 0 and freeLinks 0, the sample count did not move, and locality went NULL -> 'Verlot' with every finding cleared. Three decisions from the PR proved out at once: the fill-only refresh wrote the gap and touched nothing else, the link stayed the identity so a changed observation did not mint a second sample, and 'the volunteer fixes it upstream and the next sync collects it' is now a thing that happened rather than an argument in a comment.

STILL OPEN ON THIS BEAD: the staff override screen, blocked on beeline-6e9 (a sample's collector cannot be reassigned - DuckDB refuses to update an indexed column on a referenced row), and with it the ingest/promote-observations.sql fix so a staff coordinate override survives the nightly run.

Also noted while there: the 1,594 new samples are in sample_elevation_pending with no elevation, and elevation:fetch is DEM-tile downloading that belongs on maderas rather than a home connection.
close_reason: Shipped in PR #23 (ingest/mint-samples.sql): observations become samples; documented in AGENTS.md. Bead was left open.

title: attachPrivateStore cannot create a table against a file-backed store: USE memory fails
description:
src/app/db.ts attachPrivateStore applies missing private DDL through apply(),
which runs `USE private`, the CREATE TABLE, then `USE memory`. That last
statement only exists when the MAIN database is in-memory. Open a file-backed
store and the default catalog is named after the file:

  duckdb_databases() -> ['beeline', 'system', 'temp']
  USE memory -> Catalog Error: SET schema: No catalog + schema named "memory" found.

CONFIRMED IN THE SANDBOX, 2026-08-28 12:57:54 during a deploy that first
shipped schema/private/030_activity.sql to that host:

  12:57:51 Started beeline.service
  12:57:54 [Error: Catalog Error: SET schema: No catalog + schema named "memory"]
  12:57:54 Main process exited, code=exited, status=1/FAILURE
  12:57:59 Scheduled restart job, restart counter is at 1
  12:57:59 Started beeline.service          <- and stayed up

So it is self-healing, which is why it has gone unnoticed: apply() runs the
CREATE TABLE successfully and only then throws from the `USE memory` in its
finally, so the table IS created before the process dies. The restart finds it
present, skips it, and boots. The cost is one crash-and-restart per newly
added private table — plus whatever a crash immediately after DDL does to that
store's WAL, which is the beeline-vyi hazard the runbook warns about and the
reason this is not merely cosmetic.

Fix is small: restore the catalog that was current rather than assuming
'memory'. Read it once (SELECT current_database()) before the USE, or qualify
the DDL to the private catalog by name so no USE is needed at all. The column
patches below it already qualify their target (ALTER TABLE private.
inat_oauth_token ...) and are unaffected — which is why only the create path
breaks.

Found while smoke-testing beeline-o22; unrelated to it.
notes:
FIXED in PR https://github.com/rainhead/beeline/pull/24 (2026-08-29), branch fix-private-store-catalog-restore. Read current_database() before the USE and restore that, rather than assuming 'memory'.

Three regression tests in test/auth.test.ts, all of which fail without the fix. They open the MAIN database as a file, which no existing test did - every one of them paired a file-backed private store with an in-memory main, and that is the single combination in which the bug is invisible, because then the default catalog really is called 'memory'. The third asserts the property the fix turns on directly: attachPrivateStore leaves the caller in the catalog it found them in, since everything after it reads unqualified names and a connection left pointing at 'private' resolves them against the wrong store.

Verified end to end: restored the dev store's private file to the exact shape that had crashed twice, booted, HTTP 200 first try.

WORTH CHECKING ON THE SANDBOX before the next deploy: which shape its private.session is in. If it still carries person_id it has been restart-looping rather than running, and this is what lets it come up.
close_reason: Merged as 3c37e4c (PR #24). attachPrivateStore reads current_database() before the USE and restores that, rather than assuming 'memory'. Three regression tests open the MAIN database as a file — the combination no existing test used, and the only one in which the bug is visible — and all three fail without the fix. Verified end to end: restored the dev store's private file to the exact shape that had crashed twice, booted, HTTP 200 first try. Worth checking on the sandbox before the next deploy: which shape its private.session is in — if it still carries person_id it has been restart-looping rather than running.

title: Reseeding the sandbox locked every bootstrap admin out
description:
Peter, 2026-08-28: 'I am no longer an admin' on the sandbox, after a few reseeds and after adding Nora (which is what introduced the admin-grant mechanism).

CAUSE. seedAdmins applied config.adminLogins only when person_admin was empty AND the overlay recorded no admin decision at all. db:reseed does not carry person_admin — CARRIED_TABLES is staging, and its comment says the rest is 'a pure function of these, and promotion recomputes it', which is true of everything except this: promotion recomputes person_admin from the OVERLAY alone. The only admin decision ever written was name:Nora Jacobi,admin,yes. So a reseeded store came back holding exactly her, which satisfied both guards at once and permanently disabled the bootstrap for the five people who had only ever been in it. Nobody was revoked; they were never re-granted, and could not grant themselves because granting requires being an admin.

THIRD SYMPTOM, found while fixing: clankford (Caleb Lankford, person 577) has an inat_account but no person_admin row on the dev store. His account was backfilled after the seed ran, and 'don't top up a non-empty roster' meant he has never been an admin at all.

FIX (committed). The question is asked per person: grant to anyone on the list who holds no row and whom the overlay has not revoked. Only a revocation of THIS person suppresses their seed — that is the property the guard was reaching for ('a revocation sticks across a restart'); someone else's grant is none of their business, and already holding a row is not a reason to skip the rest of the list. Refs are matched the two ways personRef writes them (name:<display_name>, inat:<user_id>); a curated name: row written against a since-renamed display name errs toward re-granting rather than toward locking out, which is the safe direction for a bootstrap. main.ts now merges BOTH overlays before asking, since half the decisions are curated in git — reading only the app-written half asked a different question than it looked like.

RECOVERY. Deploying is the unlock: at boot the five are re-granted (Caleb makes six), Nora keeps hers. No manual DB surgery, no service-stopped INSERT.

STILL OPEN, deliberately not fixed here: a bootstrap-seeded admin is invisible to a rebuild, because the seed writes no overlay row. That is by design — it is a seed, not a decision, and writing rows would make removing someone from ADMIN_LOGINS impossible — but it does mean the roster after a reseed is 'whatever the overlay says, plus whatever the checked-in list says at boot', and those two lists are maintained in different places. Worth a look when the admin allowlist becomes a per-atlas role.
close_reason: Fixed and committed. Deploying is the unlock — at boot the six on the checked-in list are granted (including Caleb, who had never had it) and Nora keeps hers. 390 tests pass; two new ones reproduce the reseed lockout and the backfilled-account case directly.

title: One iNaturalist login, two humans: the partner cannot sign in
description:
Found by Peter on /people, 2026-08-24: person 722436 on the sandbox is
'Robert Pederson', but the iNat account his records use — pandg — is titled
'Pete & Gretchen Pederson'. A household shares one login.

inat_account.inat_user_id is UNIQUE, so one iNaturalist account belongs to
exactly one person by construction. Promotion binds it to whoever files most
under it (beeline-eft's weighted rule), and the partner gets nothing. Robert
has 1,087 samples and no way to sign in and see a single one of them.

MEASURED on the sandbox (2026-08-24): 161 people with samples have no
account, 5,170 samples between them. 17 of those, holding 2,329 samples, have
records pointing at an account somebody else holds:

  Robert Pederson  1087  pandg           held by Gretchen Pederson
  Steve Sheehy      420  smalaby         held by Sarah Malaby
  Julie Biddle      363  tom_julie       held by Tom Robertson
  Emily Carlson     254  amelathopoulos  held by Andony Melathopoulos
  Jane Pope          31  pandg           held by Gretchen Pederson
  ...and Shaw Steinmetz, Brendan McGarry, Edward Lisowski, Barrett Barrett,
  Juan Benitez, Cort Gardner, Amy Greenwalt

That list is TWO problems wearing one shape, and the second is already
handled. The tail — Steinmetz, McGarry, Lisowski, Barrett, Benitez, Gardner,
Greenwalt — are duplicate person records, and every one of them disappears
when data/collector-duplicate-worksheet.csv is filled in and becomes alias
lines (beeline-eyk). There is no partner to give an account to; there is one
human spelled twice.

What is left is genuinely two humans under one login: the Pedersons (with
Jane Pope somehow also filing under pandg), Sheehy/Malaby, Robertson/Biddle.
Plus Emily Carlson, which is a third thing again — Andony typed her records
in, so she needs HER OWN account resolved from iNat, not a share of his.

OPTIONS, none obviously right:

(a) Let several people share one account — drop the UNIQUE. Sign-in then
resolves to more than one person and has to ask which; every "my samples"
query has to decide whether it means the person or the household.

(b) An account grants access to a SET of people. Signing in as pandg shows
both Pedersons' QC lists. Closest to what actually happens at that kitchen
table, and it keeps attribution per-person, which determinations and labels
need. Costs a new table and a session that carries more than one person.

(c) Leave it: staff act on the partner's behalf. 2,329 samples whose QC has
no owner who can act on it — and after cutover, no way for that person to
see their own field numbers.

Not urgent before the worksheet is done, because that shrinks the list to
about four. Urgent before cutover, because (c) becomes permanent.

MEANWHILE (done, beeline-eyk): /people no longer shows these people as a
blank. The row reads "No account — Their records use pandg, which is Gretchen
Pederson's", and the person page says it at length and names it as a shared
login only one person can hold. That squares the display; it does not square
the model.
close_reason: Duplicate of beeline-oyl, which was filed the same day and covers it better — it has the near-even-split analysis and the reference implementation's hand-patched 'pandg after 2021 resolves by sampleId > 100'. My measurements moved to beeline-oyl.

title: People roster: who is in the store, and the evidence for each iNat binding
description:
Admin screen at /people (beeline-eft follow-on; delivers the person_home_atlas satellite from beeline-2c3.11).

Read: paged roster of every person with their iNat binding AND the evidence for it — records backing the bound account, the runners-up, and a verdict (backed / check this / unattested / no account / no legacy records). Weighed on inat_user_id, not the login string, so an upstream rename reads as backed rather than as four false alarms; falls back to the login where legacy recorded no id at all.

Write, all five: rebind/unbind an account, grant/revoke admin, set home atlas, edit name parts, merge two people. Every write lands in data/person-overlay.csv first and is applied from there, so promotion replays it onto a rebuilt store (ADR 0004 shape, git-curated counterpart ingest/person-overlay.csv). The overlay names people by name:<display_name> or inat:<user_id>, never entity_id.

New: schema/010 person_home_atlas + person_admin (migration 0009); src/person-overlay.ts, src/apply-person-overlay.ts, src/app/roster.ts, src/app/views/roster.tsx. The admin roster moved into person_admin; config.adminLogins is the bootstrap seed applied at boot only when that table is empty, so a revocation is not undone by the next restart.
close_reason: Shipped and deployed to the sandbox; admin seed confirmed live for all six.

title: Legacy account linking picks the rarest login, not the right one
description:
ingest/promote-legacy.sql:328 binds person -> inat_account by a login-to-name test that consults name uniqueness but never record counts: GROUP BY login HAVING count(DISTINCT (fn,ln)) = 1, then QUALIFY row_number() OVER (PARTITION BY person_id ORDER BY c.login) = 1 — alphabetical.

A login used for data entry on someone else's records spans two people and is discarded as ambiguous; a one-off typo login survives and wins by default. The busy, correct login loses BECAUSE it is busy.

Two confirmed mislinks in the dev store (sandbox has the same rows):

• Andony Melathopoulos -> 'andonymelathopoulos' (iNat 1542612: no display name, 2 observations, created 2019) on the strength of ONE legacy record. The correct account is 'amelathopoulos' (iNat 429964, name 'Andony Melathopoulos', ~1900 obs, iNat 'app owner'), carrying 3042 of his records — discarded because it also sits on Emily Carlson's 151 records, which is just Andony entering her data.
• Pat Wheeler -> 'hexapod' (iNat 12665) on 4 records. That account is DAMION COE, 530 observations — a different, active person. The correct 'patwheeler' (iNat 793138) carries 990.

Impact, given auth is real now (src/app/auth.tsx:145 gates on inat_account):
• Andony cannot sign in at all — 'amelathopoulos' has no inat_account row, so he gets the pending-approval 403. He is the program lead and production sync is meant to run as him (see the token-policy memory).
• The lookalike 1542612 would receive Andony's person record and 515 samples.
• Damion Coe, who is not a person in this store, would receive Pat Wheeler's person record and 763 samples.

The reference implementation had no exposure here: userLogin is a typed string behind one shared password (docs/reference-implementation.md:39), so there was no account binding to get wrong. This risk is new with real OAuth identity.

Note what is NOT broken: 'mrthorn', 'ben_diehl', 'cbick', 'jadethegem' also differ from their legacy top login, but each resolves to a profile matching the person and each legacy login 404s on iNat — correctly-followed renames. A fix must keep those.

Directions: prefer the login backing the most records for that person; treat a login spanning several people as a data-entry account rather than a disqualifier; and require corroboration (profile name, or an inat_user_id seen in live observation data) before binding a login that backs only a handful of records. src/backfill-inat-accounts.ts already has the profile-name check — it just never runs on these people because promote-legacy claimed them first, and it would not have caught 1542612 anyway since that profile has no name at all.
close_reason: Rule rewritten to weigh records in both directions; three mislinks corrected on the sandbox by migration 0008 and verified live. Follow-up for the 19 newly-bindable people: beeline-2gw.

title: Refuse to derive elevation above a coordinate-uncertainty threshold
description:
A derived elevation is a statement about where the bee was collected. When the coordinate is only known to within hundreds of kilometres, the DEM lookup still returns a confident-looking integer — and that integer gets printed on a physical label, which is immutable fact once printed (CONTEXT.md).

The store currently does exactly this. Measured 2026-08-24 on the dev store, sample_location by stated coordinate_uncertainty_m:

  <=100 m   47375 locations   (all with elevation)
  <=1 km     1071
  <=5 km      307
  <=20 km     125
  <=100 km     26
  >100 km      30   (29 of them have a derived elevation)
  unstated  17358

Worst offenders, all inat_public: 2979 km uncertainty -> 260 m derived; 1378 km -> 1651 m; 1204 km -> 109 m. These numbers constrain nothing and should not exist.

Proposal: refuse derivation when coordinate_uncertainty_m IS STATED and exceeds a threshold; leave it NULL. Suggested threshold 10 km — below ~1 km the elevation error from horizontal uncertainty is smaller than the label needs even in mountains, and by 10 km the plausible elevation range in Oregon terrain routinely spans over 1000 m, so the number stops meaning anything. That affects on the order of 100-180 of 66k locations (~0.2%), the same order as beeline-zjd itself. Peter to confirm the number.

Deliberately NOT refusing the 17358 'unstated' rows: legacy records carry no uncertainty, and treating absent as unbounded is a much larger and different decision.

Design notes:
- Guard goes in the gap query's WHERE in deriveElevations, but those rows must not then be counted as perpetual gaps in the nightly log — add a 'refused' counter beside gaps/filled/voids so the job line reads honestly.
- The ~29 already-derived values above the threshold need clearing; derive only touches NULLs, so it will not undo them by itself. That is a migration for the sandbox (ADR 0006).
- Threshold as a named, commented constant.
- Complements rather than duplicates the existing coordinate_uncertainty QC rule: that rule tells the volunteer their coordinate is vague; this stops Beeline manufacturing a fact from it.

Raised by Peter on reading beeline-zjd's one remaining NULL (a record at -7.08,-121.58, 1196 km uncertainty, open Pacific) — that one is NULL only because no DEM covers ocean, not because anything refused it.
notes: 2026-08-27: beeline-x5c is the other half of elevation trustworthiness — this bead is about deriving an elevation the coordinate does not support; that one is about keeping an elevation the coordinate no longer supports (nothing records which coordinates an elevation was derived from). Whatever columns x5c adds, the threshold rule here should be applied on re-derivation too.
close_reason: elevation_derivation_limit states the threshold once (100 m, Peter 2026-08-27); sample_elevation_pending drops coordinates above it so they are never a standing backlog; deriveElevations reports a 'refused' count and the nightly job line carries it, so shrinkage is not read as progress. An unstated uncertainty still derives — treating absent as unbounded stays the larger decision this bead declined. sample_elevation_unsupportable names what is already present and removes nothing: 1,558 rows on the dev store, 744 under the 250 m printing limit and so on records that still print, and 1,546 from iNaturalist rather than the legacy import. Note the threshold is tighter than the 250 m at which qc_rule_coordinate_uncertainty blocks printing, deliberately — an elevation is a stricter claim than a locality string. Migration 0016. Follow-up worth a decision: whether to clear the 1,558.

title: QC home took 10s: printability's correlated OR never decorrelated
description: Found right after the 2026-08-23 rebuild put a full 66k-sample store back under the dev app: GET / took 9.5-10s, every load, against a 1s interactive budget (ADR 0005). printable_sample tested sample-keyed and specimen-keyed blocking findings with an OR inside a correlated NOT EXISTS, which DuckDB cannot decorrelate — it degrades to scanning qc_finding once per sample (11.7s for a bare count over the view; qc_finding itself is 0.67s). pending_print_sample inherits it, so the QC home paid it twice. Fixed by splitting the two routes into a blocking_sample UNION view that the planner hash-anti-joins. Same membership, and the QC rule and printability tests cover it.
acceptance_criteria: GET / and the pending-print reads are well inside the one-second interactive budget on a full store; printable_sample membership is unchanged.
close_reason: printable_sample rewritten as a blocking_sample UNION anti-join; QC home 9.5s -> 1.2s on the full store. Residual cost is qc_finding itself, filed separately.

title: Production does not require BEELINE_ORIGIN; missed env silently drops Secure cookie flag
description: config hard-fails on missing BEELINE_PRIVATE_DB_KEY outside development but defaults origin to http://localhost, which drops the Secure flag and breaks the CSRF origin comparison behind TLS termination. Require BEELINE_ORIGIN outside development.
close_reason: Closed

title: POST /jobs/run/:name has no admin tier
description: Any approved volunteer can trigger any job including the nightly sync (API-quota burn, races with interactive edits). /jobs is documented as an admin screen but the session model has no role. Gate /jobs behind an admin allowlist (e.g. BEELINE_ADMIN_LOGINS).
close_reason: Closed

title: OAuth callback 500s on token-exchange failure and is an unauthenticated iNat amplifier
description: exchangeCode errors propagate to Hono's default 500 instead of m.signIn.failed; anyone can mint a state cookie and loop the callback, making the server POST to iNat's token endpoint without limit. Wrap in try/catch → friendly failure page; consider rate limiting.
close_reason: Closed

title: Crash-orphaned job_run rows consume the schedule slot; no retry in window
description: lastStarts uses max(started_at) with no outcome filter and nothing at boot marks completed_at IS NULL rows failed, so a crash at 2:01am means no sync that day (a crashed Sunday sweep stales deletion detection a week). A single transient failure likewise costs the whole period. Reconcile orphans at boot and let dailyLA retry within the night window after a failure.
close_reason: Closed

title: Sync watermark can be advanced by windowed sweeps, permanently skipping edits
description: lastSyncStart takes max(started_at) over any completed sync_run, but a windowed sweep does not subsume 'everything updated since the last nightly'. A manual daytime sweep advances the watermark past edits to observations outside its window; those edits are never fetched. Derive the watermark only from runs that carried updated_since (or the first covering sweep).
close_reason: Closed

title: Two-tab sample edit silently reverts the other tab's save
description: The edit form posts every field and applySampleEdit diffs against the row as-of-POST, so a stale tab's prefilled values register as deliberate edits and clobber a newer save in both the DB and the permanent CSV. Carry the form's base values in hidden fields and treat submitted==form-base as untouched.
close_reason: Closed

title: Reverting a sample edit leaves the stale correction event standing
description: applySampleEdit skips events where base === newValue, so an X→Z→X revert never replaces the X→Z row in corrections.csv; the live row says X but every rebuild restores Z. Fix per ADR 0004: write the identity event and let the merge classify it retired.
close_reason: Closed

title: Volunteer determination entry UX: self-explanatory, mistake-resistant
description: Peter (2026-08-21, beeline-fmg session): cutover is instantaneous, so the volunteer determination flow must be better than status quo from day one — a low bar on function, but the screens must be self-explanatory and hard to make mistakes on. Ties to the CONTEXT.md open question: momentary data-entry mistakes must not become permanent history, suggesting a draft/commit boundary where only deliberate assertions become append-only determination events. Design levers: constrained affordances (taxon picker over free text, sex/caste as explicit choices), visible review-before-commit, easy same-session retraction of a slip vs the formal correction path for committed events. Also interacts with i18n: mistake-resistance via structured inputs translates cheaply; mistake-resistance via explanatory prose multiplies the en/es/fr-CA translation surface.
design: Wireframe canvas (rev 2026-08-22): https://claude.ai/code/artifact/cb7324e7-6f94-4817-bece-1a18a0991128 — My determinations (prefilled outstanding rows, row states, jump-to-number), Filling down (two-pass coarse→fine bulk apply), Taxon picker (any-rank curated search, bees-default + bycatch toggle), Expert mode (their-determination column, leave-as-is state, cross-collector). Model: spreadsheet-semantics rows, freeze-on-consumption, corrections after freeze.
notes:
Design inputs (Peter, 2026-08-21/22):

ENTRY REALITY — varies by volunteer. Minority: determine as labels arrive (genus or higher). Majority: big winter batches; boxes physically sorted by taxon first, some chronological.

STATUS QUO TO BEAT — official 2025 flow is a copied Google Sheet (OBA Number, Sex/Caste, Family, Genus, Species; taxonomy-tab dropdowns; NO number validation; manual transcription into reference DB). Its strength to preserve: apply 'Bombus' to N rows, refine to species in smaller batches. Example: https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1N1ObAb2rZgPWcdgPqK_yr-L6NSzzCV7-O7fAnHErsPg

ONE GRID, TWO MECHANICS (2026-08-22, replaces separate batch screen): (1) rows PREFILLED for every outstanding specimen — numbers never typed; 'jump to number' still validates. (2) FILL-DOWN: select N rows, apply taxon+sex; coarse→fine overwriting is the normal workflow.

SAMPLE CONTEXT ON ROWS (2026-08-22) — each row shows its sample (number · date · place hyperlinked to the iNat observation); heavier rule at sample boundaries so a selection run doesn't spill into the next sample.

COMMIT SEMANTICS — no ceremony; mutable rows freeze into append-only events on downstream consumption (export/review/print); post-freeze = correction path. CONFIRM WITH ANDONY.

PICKER — curated taxonomy, family/tribe/genus/species; bees default, anyone may widen to bycatch. Junior-synonym support (B. californicus → B. fervidus) filed as beeline-2ae.

EXPERT MODE (provisional) — experts DO see the collector's determination; leave-as-is when right or nobody knows better (volunteer det stays determination of record; expert row only to correct/improve — endorsement by omission). Read-only collector column + sample link, cross-collector, same fill-down mechanics, auto-granted to staff. PROVISIONAL: taxonomist workflows unknown; pros may prefer spreadsheet/Ecdysis round-trips; this UI may mostly serve staff/semi-experts, and a validated spreadsheet-upload path may suit some volunteers — discovery filed as beeline-r33.

VOLUNTEER SIDE ANTI-ANCHORING — expert dets hidden during volunteer entry (Journey credit). Worth socializing.

MISTAKE MINING — approved; caveat: manual transcription step is invisible, so mined disagreements conflate volunteer and transcription slips.

DELIVERABLE — wireframes + design doc (no UI build yet). English-only okay; strings structural.

STILL OPEN — (a) Andony on freeze semantics; (b) socialize volunteer-side expert-det withholding; (c) Drive spreadsheets for mistake mining; (d) beeline-r33 expert-workflow discovery.
Peter, 2026-09-14: typically only taxonomists will enter determinations, in batches and sometimes through Ecdysis, not volunteers. This bead's premise, that the volunteer determination flow has to beat the status quo from the first day after cutover, needs revisiting against that. The priority (P1) was set on that premise.
CORRECTION (Peter, 2026-09-14): my note above was wrong. It is COMMON, though not universal, for volunteers to enter determinations. Taxonomists are typically the ones entering names ITIS lacks. This bead's premise, a volunteer determination flow that has to be good from the first day after cutover, STANDS, and so does its P1 priority. Relevant to the design: volunteers pick from ITIS names (beeline-45v).
