title: Design discussion: volunteer onboarding
description: Peter wants a dedicated session on volunteer onboarding. Context to load first: GitHub issue #1 (per-collector OAuth hybrid — onboarding is its rollout half), beeline-fvx (decisions: non-expiring iNat tokens, shared accounts out of scope, hybrid agreed), beeline-gju (person↔account mapping), CONTEXT.md Collector definition (collectors become real users who sign in via iNat OAuth). Likely threads: what login unlocks (trusted coordinates for their records, self-service QC, label status), what if anything gates on onboarding (printing?), rollout by season start vs opportunistic, the first-login claim flow (matching an OAuth identity to an existing legacy person — display-name/login match with staff fallback), i18n (en/es/fr-CA) from day one, pronouns self-fill on first login.
notes: DECIDED (Peter, 2026-08-20/21): (1) Two onboardings — atlas-membership funnel (promo, approval, trainings, inactivity drop) is future & out of scope; this session is Beeline sign-in only. No auto-created person on unknown login. (2) PENDING-STATE DESIGN AND WORK DEFERRED (Peter 2026-08-21): no pending record, no staff approval queue, no self-claim UI, no stranger tokens stored. Unknown login → static page: 'we don't recognize this account; if you're a volunteer, contact your coordinator' (they already know whom to email). Staff fixes register/inat_account mapping by hand; next login silently matches. Can revisit if legit volunteers hit this often. (3) Token retention despite non-expiry: purge after ~6mo login inactivity and on membership drop; re-mint is one OAuth click. Tokens keyed by inat_user_id, only stored for recognized people. (4) Private store: separate encrypted DuckDB file (private.duckdb, native AES-256, key outside both files) for private satellites — tokens, mailing_address, email_address. Main file copy-safe by construction. Backups include addresses; tokens TTL-bounded. → ADR 0003. (5) Data catalog/handling policy later → beeline-bla. (6) Email: OAuth does NOT hand us email — reference system HAS emails (weekly-email CSV workflow) but our import doesn't load them yet (email_address sketched only). Load with legacy import when the satellite's phase arrives; confirm/edit on welcome screen; new people supply it there. (7) Instantaneous cutover: determination flow must beat status quo day one — screens self-explanatory and hard to make mistakes on → beeline-bcq (P1). (8) ES AUDIENCE RESOLVED: Juan Manuel Benitez Alvarez (inaturalist.org/people/juanmbeniteza), Washington volunteer from El Salvador, very little English → es is DAY-ONE FULL SURFACE at cutover (QC finding texts, determination flow, welcome screen, front door), not chrome-only. Locale = person-level preference: front-door language switcher (pre-login), welcome interstitial adds language field (browser default, skippable), preference drives notifications too. Juan Manuel is the concrete acceptance test for beeline-bcq's bar (structural safety, not prose). (9) ES TRANSLATION REVIEWER: Juan Manuel — formally trained, expert in stingless bees (Meliponini; not locally occurring) — reviews es translations and the domain-term glossary; native speaker with scientific Spanish. (10) LANGUAGE PRINCIPLE: languages earn day-one status by having actual current users, not by map geography. fr-CA AUDIENCE UNCONFIRMED (Peter 2026-08-21): not certain any native French speakers exist among volunteers — needs investigation (ask BC roster / Bonnie Zand). If none current, fr-CA drops from cutover scope; externalized-strings architecture makes later addition translation-only work. UX SHAPE (discussed, broadly agreed): front door = one 'what is Beeline' paragraph + Continue-with-iNaturalist + one consent-honesty sentence (login lets Beeline see your obs as you see them, incl. hidden coords). Recognized first login → single skippable welcome interstitial ('You're X (atlas) — right?' catches bad register links; pronouns; mailing address + email confirm; language) → IMMEDIATE per-user sync so obscured→printable payoff lands same-session (needs graceful 'still fetching' degrade, never a hanging spinner). STILL OPEN: investigate fr-CA audience; pre-March push to close beeline-gju register gaps (now the entire recognition mechanism); rollout timing confirmation (opportunistic from cutover + March conference push); does anything gate on onboarding (proposed: no policy gate, obscured→printable is the organic carrot).
close_reason: Design discussion held 2026-08-20/21; ten decisions recorded in notes (membership out of scope, pending state deferred, token retention/keying, private encrypted store → ADR 0003, email via legacy import, determination-flow bar → beeline-bcq, es day-one full surface with Juan Manuel as reviewer and acceptance test, language principle, fr-CA investigation → beeline-1a7). Spin-offs: beeline-bla (data catalog), beeline-bcq (determination UX), beeline-2u8 (sandbox banner), beeline-1a7 (fr-CA). Rollout timing and onboarding-gating remain open questions on GitHub issue #1.

title: Several iNaturalist observations claiming one sample number is collector error; Beeline merges them silently
description:
Peter, 2026-10-04: "if multiple inaturalist observations claim the same sample number, that is collector error." A sample is one observation.

Beeline assumes the opposite. Minting groups every observation sharing a collector, sample number and date into one sample (sample_mint_group), and schema/108's sample_multi_observation describes the result as "a sample whose collecting event iNaturalist records in several observations", explaining away the count_mismatch it causes. Legacy promotion does the same with legacy rows, keyed on (collector, sampleId, date). Nothing tells the volunteer: duplicate_sample_number fires only when two separate Beeline samples share a number.

On the sandbox (copy of 2026-10-04), split by season:

| | Open season | Settled |
|---|---|---|
| Samples several observations claim | 228 of 12,711 | 388 of 55,687 |
| of which already printed | 224 | 366 |

They are found two ways, which overlap: legacy records of one sample naming several observation URLs, and sample_multi_observation. Of the open season's legacy-merged ones, 24 span more than 10 km (Fanny Bay and Lundbom Grassland, 304 km, under one number and date) and 41 sit within 1 km of each other: by Peter's rule all are errors, not only the far ones. Two habits show: one volunteer numbering a day's outing as one sample (7 samples, Vancouver with Steigerwald NWR and others), and a later observation given an earlier sample's number and date (73954, 55458, 50682; 66657 and 67931 cross over).

What follows, none of it decided:
1. Tell the volunteer. duplicate_sample_number, or a sibling rule, fires when more than one observation claims a sample's number on its date, with the same instruction: renumber one of the observations. Blocking for an unprinted sample. Nearly all current cases are printed already, where it can only say the record is wrong.
2. Stop merging at minting, so the error stays visible as two samples with one number instead of one sample hiding a second observation. That changes the reconcile key minting and free-linking share, and what happens when the volunteer renumbers (minting never rewrites a number or count), so it needs design, not a patch.
3. Decide what a printed merged sample becomes: the pins carry each observation's own place, so splitting it would match the labels.
4. Correct the premise where it is written: schema/108's comments on sample_multi_observation and the minting paragraph in AGENTS.md.
5. The parallel-run comparison's sample_disagreement label (beeline-en7i) then has an answer: the collector's error, which both systems carry.
close_reason: #133 (a4b7af4) deployed and the sandbox reseeded 2026-10-04: one sample per observation, legacy merges split (3,277 records across 434 groups), unprinted numbers follow, printed duplicates named not flagged. On the reseeded sandbox: 8 open-season and 36 settled samples blocked until renumbered, none still holding several legacy observations, none counting another observation's specimens.

comments.author: Peter Abrahamsen
comments.text: Peter, 2026-10-04: duplicate sample numbers were called out as a needed QC rule from the beginning. The rule exists (qc_rule_duplicate_sample_number, schema/120, since a9bc5e7 on 2026-08-20, blocking, shown on the volunteer dashboard) and has never fired: 0 findings on the sandbox in either season. It counts SAMPLES sharing (primary collector, date_start, number), and both legacy promotion and minting merge on that same key first, so by construction the duplicate it was written for cannot reach it. Its own comment says it catches 'an identity collision the reference implementation silently merged'; Beeline merges it the same way. Fix: count observations claiming a sample's number, not samples. Open decision: 224 of the 228 affected open-season samples are already printed, and telling a volunteer to renumber an observation after its label printed would make the record disagree with the pin (the beeline-4dt kind of finding).

title: Worksheet load overrode identifications volunteers had entered directly in the old system
description:
Found by the parallel-run comparison on the sandbox, 2026-10-04 (beeline-en7i).

The old system has a Determinations page (OBP-Server client/src/pages/determinations/) where a volunteer enters family, genus, species, sex and caste for their own specimens. OccurrencesController.uploadOccurrences saves those five columns in place, with no date and no sign-in required. So a volunteer could identify the same specimen twice: once on a Drive worksheet, once directly in the old system. Peter, 2026-10-04: "some volunteers probably entered data on a worksheet as well as directly into the reference system".

The worksheet loader (beeline-pbk) holds a row when two worksheet copies disagree, but not when a worksheet disagrees with the old system's own volunteer identification by the same person. Both get recorded, and the worksheet becomes current only because it was loaded later. On the sandbox, 52 specimens this season are affected, almost all from one volunteer's two 2026 sheets: 24 where the worksheet says less (a bare family where the old record has a genus), 15 that contradict it (Augochlorella against Augochloropsis), and 13 where the sex flips. Another 73 are refinements (worksheet more specific) and are fine.

Which is newer cannot be read from the data. The old values appear in none of the 34 Drive revisions of either sheet, from the first in June to the last on 30 July, so they were not transcribed from the sheets: they were typed into the old system separately, at an unknown time. They are mostly the more specific of the two.

Undecided, Peter's call:
- Hold these rows (load nothing that coarsens or contradicts the old record by the same person) and leave the old record current.
- Or record both and let the volunteer settle it on /determinations, which would need the screen to show a conflict.
- Or accept the worksheet as current, which is what happened.

Measure the same on the settled seasons before choosing: 1 contradiction and 1 coarsening there.
close_reason: Held as old_system_disagrees in #130 (62fbe1d): a worksheet row that contradicts, says less than, or changes the sex of the determiner's old-system identification no longer loads. Rows already loaded on the sandbox stay until its next reseed.

comments.author: Peter Abrahamsen
comments.text: Peter, 2026-10-04: hold. Implemented in PR #130: a worksheet row that would contradict the determiner's old-system identification, say less than it, or change its sex is held as old_system_disagrees and listed in held.csv with the old value; a refinement loads. Rows already loaded on the sandbox stay until its next reseed. Close when #130 merges.

title: Old system printed 583 specimens twice or more this season under different field numbers
description:
Found by the parallel-run comparison (beeline-en7i, PR #128) on the dev store against the 2026-09-28 pull.

Legacy promotion's `duplicate_specimen` finding (ingest/promote-legacy.sql, `legacy_ranked`) refuses a staged record when another record names the same specimen — same collector, date, sample number and specimen number — under a different fieldNumber, keeping the latest print. Its comment calls this "the hash-id bug" as if historical. It is not: 614 records from the 2026 season are refused this way, 583 specimens each printed under two or more field numbers, 448 of them twice on the same print day (commonest days 6 Jul, 20 Jul, 13 May, 26 May 2026). None has an unprinted member.

So there are physical pins, or at least printed labels, carrying field numbers Beeline does not hold. Why it matters:

- A taxonomist or Ecdysis record that cites the losing number finds no specimen in Beeline.
- The minting floor and `minted_field_number_collision` read the imported corpus; check that the losing numbers count towards it, or Beeline could reissue one at cutover.
- The old system is presumably still doing this, so the count grows until it freezes.

Not decided, and not ours alone: whether the extra labels were discarded or pinned, which needs staff; and whether Beeline should keep the losing numbers as aliases of the winning specimen. Read docs/reference-implementation.md on the hash id first, and look at OBP-Server's print path for why one specimen is printed twice in one day.

comments.author: Peter Abrahamsen
comments.text: Sandbox, 2026-10-04, against the 2026-09-28 pull (395,045 staged rows): 701 open-season records refused as duplicate prints, against 614 on the dev store's earlier pull (383,032 rows). So it is still growing between pulls, as expected while the old system prints. Also in the 09-28 pull, unrelated but adjacent: 177 empty records (no collector, sample, date or print date) carrying field numbers 25100000-25100088, two records per number. They are not promoted and sit in the 2025 block below anything Beeline mints, so they cannot collide; noted in case staff know what made them.

comments.text: Mostly not reprints: 2,467 of the 2,902 refusals on the 2026-10-04 corpus were distinct specimens on observations sharing a sample number, each observation numbering its own specimens from 1 (field numbers 26075301 and 26075302 are both specimen 1 of sample 1 that day, from two observations). PR #135 keys the reprint ranking on the observation in those groups. Left: 435 refusals, all from before 2025, which are what this bead's question about extra labels now covers. The minting floor reads specimen only, but every one of the 435 is below the 2026 ceiling.

title: Parallel run: a discrepancy relation against the reference export, with rulings
description:
Source: https://github.com/rainhead/beeline/issues/127 (an agent's proposal, reshaped here; the issue is now the question to Andony about whether and how he would use rulings).

## Why

README's plan for 2026 is to run Beeline in parallel with OBP-Server and compare outputs. Today the comparison is `pnpm legacy:compare-export` (`src/compare-legacy-export.ts`): every one of the 63 exported columns compared per record matched on `fieldNumber`, split by season, with the commonest value pairs named per column. It is a report of counts. Nothing records that a difference has been explained, so the same one is re-investigated on every run, by us and by Andony, whose R comparison joins the same file on the same key.

## What

Build on `compare-legacy-export.ts`; do not start over. Plain SQL where it can be (ADR 0001).

1. **A per-(fieldNumber, column) relation.** One row per difference: both values, which kind of difference it is, when first and last seen, and the reference file's hash and date. Persisted outside the blow-away path like `data/sample-state.csv`, since the store is rebuilt at will and first/last seen only mean something across builds. `fieldNumber` is the key because it is the only one both systems share and it is not PII, so the file can live in git. Compare normalised values (dates, decimals, whitespace), not bytes.
2. **Kinds, not predicates.** Classify differences in SQL into a fixed set of named kinds: Roman-numeral month, case (`Male`/`male`), whitespace, higher taxonomy filled where the old record was blank, country/state code vocabulary, staff edit applied, Ecdysis determination newer than the register's, and so on. The compare tool's "commonest pairs" output is most of this classifier already. A ruling names a kind or a record, never a SQL predicate: SQL in a CSV is not a ruling anyone but a developer can read or write.
3. **Rulings**, `data/rulings.csv`, hand-maintained, loaded, never auto-written: `(field_number | column+kind), outcome, reason, source, by, date`, outcome in {reference-wrong, beeline-wrong, known-gap, expected}. `source` points at the issue or email where the call was made. A `beeline-wrong` ruling stays visible until the discrepancy disappears, then reads as retired (ADR 0004's auto-retire, applied to an explanation rather than a value), so a fixed bug never hides behind a stale ruling. A reason must not carry a volunteer's name: the repo is public.
4. **The report**: unexplained differences, count and list, open season against settled (every check count splits by season), and the trend since the last reference file. A CLI first. It becomes a nightly job only once the reference file reaches the sandbox nightly, which today it does not: a developer fetches it over SSH from production. That is the open operational question, and it gates the "make it a gate" step, not the rest.
5. **Provenance per column** is a static map from exported column to the view or SQL in `src/legacy-export.ts` that produces it, printed on the row. It is a column→source table, not per-row lineage, and should be described as such.

## Acceptance

- Re-running against the same reference file (same hash) yields the same rows.
- Adding a ruling removes exactly the rows it names from the unexplained report and nothing else.
- A `beeline-wrong` ruling whose discrepancy has disappeared is reported as retired, not silently dropped.
- Every row names its kind and the column's source.
- Counts split by season.

## Not this

- No automatic fixes, no merging, no replacement for issues.
- The issue's "Later" section (label governance by content hash) is already built another way: `printed_label` keeps the rendered strings and the values they came from, and beeline-1kb.17 is the comparison of a later iNaturalist edit against what printed. Nothing to do here.

title: Open-season samples sharing one observation: staff review
description:
sample_shared_observation (beeline-15k, #123) on the dev store, 2026-10-03: 306 samples share an observation with another sample. 24 of them are in the open season: 18 same_date (one collector and day, different numbers) and 6 same_number (one number, different dates). So the legacy path is still producing this, not just carrying old residue. Every promotion gives each sample in a group that one observation's coordinates, geoprivacy, host and count comparison, so at least one sample per group is described by another collecting event's evidence.

Work the 24 first, while they can still be fixed at the source:
- same_number: most likely an observation URL pasted onto the wrong sample. Find the right observation, or clear the link.
- same_date: either one link is wrong, or one collecting event was split into two samples. That needs a person's judgment, not a volunteer-facing flag.

Then decide whether the 282 settled samples (214 same_date, 52 same_number, 14 other, 2 different_collectors) get a curation pass before cutover, which beeline-15k left open.

List them with:
  SELECT v.*, s.sample_number, s.date_start FROM sample_shared_observation v JOIN sample s ON s.entity_id = v.sample_id LEFT JOIN settled_sample st ON st.sample_id = v.sample_id WHERE st.sample_id IS NULL ORDER BY v.inat_observation_id, s.sample_number;

A dashboard QC warning was considered and deferred: on same_date it could push a volunteer to 'fix' a split that is really one event.

title: Oregon exports carry the corpus occurrenceID where OSAC published a different one
description:
For 4,636 Oregon specimens, the occurrenceID in the legacy corpus is not the one GBIF holds. Worked example: field number 1900026 is published by OSAC as https://osac.oregonstate.edu/SP/OSAC_0001252110 (catalogNumber OSAC_0001252110) and sits in the legacy corpus as https://osac.oregonstate.edu/OBS/OBA_1900026. The legacy-format export (src/legacy-export.ts, orStaged("occurrenceID", …)) and anything else that carries the staged value verbatim would hand GBIF these specimens under new identities, which GBIF reads as new records beside the existing ones.

Measured 2026-10-01: OSAC's IPT archive for the Oregon Bee Atlas dataset (https://osac.oregonstate.edu/ipt/archive.do?r=osac-oba, GBIF 1fa69ff3-3e40-465f-927f-12b1484d3731, release 2026-07-28, 64,913 records) joined to the legacy corpus fetched 2026-09-28 by fieldNumber. 59,842 published identifiers appear verbatim in the corpus (http/https folded). Of the rest, 4,636 match a corpus record by field number but carry a different identifier — overwhelmingly OSAC's SP/OSAC_<catalog> and OBS/OSAC_<catalog> forms where the corpus has OBS/OBA_<field number> — and 66 match a record whose corpus occurrenceID is empty. All 2017–2024, settled seasons; nothing from the open season is published. About 370 published records match nothing in the corpus by either key; not investigated.

The SP/OSAC_ form looks like OSAC's catalog number for specimens accessioned into the collection, with OBS/OBA_ for the ones still at the Melittology Lab — an inference from the URI paths and from https://osac.oregonstate.edu/OBS/OBA_<anything>, which serves one static "OBA observations" page for any number. Not confirmed with OSAC.

Decide: does Beeline adopt OSAC's published identifier for these specimens (an import of the IPT archive, keyed by field number), or does it stop emitting occurrenceID for imported Oregon specimens and leave the column to OSAC? Either way the published value is OSAC's to state. Related: ADR 0008 open question 1 (beeline-1kb.15), beeline-1kb.14.

title: Load BC Bee Atlas determinations from Ecdysis collection 196
description: BC keeps its specimens in Ecdysis as collection 196 (Native Bee Society of BC Bee Atlas Collection, NBSBC:BCBA). Catalog numbers are the Beeline field number under the prefix BCBA_, the same shape as Washington's WSDA_, so ecdysis:load --prefix BCBA_ should take it unchanged. Measured 2026-09-27 over the v2 API: 8,585 records; the 2025 season has 3,692, of which 3,524 carry a determination by the atlas's own determiner, and the old system's export holds no determination of any kind for BC 2025 specimens. So this is the only route by which BC's 2025 determinations reach Beeline. Unlike Washington there is no public dataset, so the Darwin Core archive (identifications=1) must be scoped by collection (db=196) rather than datasetid, which beeatlas's download does not do; it needs a logged-in Ecdysis session. BC volunteer determinations are NOT in Ecdysis: 50 of 50 records sampled that the old system says a volunteer determined show only the expert determination and no history on their public record pages (GitHub #102 asks where volunteers' 2025 determinations went). Ecdysis's TLS certificate expired around 2026-09-24; fetches currently need verification off.

title: Fill-only refresh never fills host_inat_taxon_id on an imported sample

Seen on the 2026-09-27 sandbox reseed with a fresh legacy dump: samples the old store held as iNat-minted (host '57934 Ericameria nauseosa') came back as imported ('Ericameria nauseosa'), and the boot pass recorded ~3,600 host changes of exactly that shape plus 7 hosts emptied. No label changes, since labels print the name; what is lost is the plant taxon reference any export (associatedTaxa) would read. Likely fix: add host_inat_taxon_id to the fill-only UPDATE, guarded so it fills only where the observation's host name agrees with host_name_as_observed, since the legacy name was typed separately and may name a different plant.

title: A canceled run's specimens read as never numbered, and the burned number is invisible
description:
A specimen whose run was canceled reads as if it had never been numbered. On the sandbox, /specimens/771472 (specimen 1 of sample 293, dated 2026-09-20) was minted 26080016 in print run 771318, which was canceled 33 seconds after it was prepared. The cancel cleared `specimen.field_number` and burned the number (`minted_field_number` row with `specimen_id` NULL), as designed. But the listing shows the cell as "not numbered", and the record page says "Not numbered — this specimen's label predates field numbering", which is the legacy explanation and false here: the specimen was numbered on 2026-09-21 and had the number taken back, and the next unscoped freeze will re-adopt it with a fresh number. Peter read the page and the listing as contradicting each other (2026-09-23).

All 902 specimens in that canceled run are in this state; none in the two open runs are.

Two fixes, both copy and one column:

1. A third case beside "numbered" and "predates field numbering": a specimen with a label row and a NULL field number is waiting for the next run. The record page already fetches its label rows for the Labels block, so it can tell; the listing would need `specimen_label` joined, or an EXISTS, to say something other than the legacy phrase (and its catalog comment on `noFieldNumber` should stop claiming the legacy meaning).

2. The Labels table on the specimen page shows run, state, sheet and cell but not `number_text`. Put the number in the row, so a proof sheet from a canceled run can be matched to its specimen and the reader can see that 26080016 was this specimen and is now dead. The proofing-lookup half of this block (a number matching twice shows each specimen's labels beside their runs) already assumes the number is visible.
close_reason: Merged as #96: a canceled run's specimen reads 'awaiting a number' on the listing and sample page, names the burned number on its own page, and the Labels table carries the number.

title: Quick links: the program's and the person's atlas's resources, in the menu
description:
Idea (Peter, 2026-09-21): give volunteers one place to find the resources they reach for outside Beeline.

Program-wide links (every signed-in person):
- Ideal Logic, https://apps.ideal-logic.com/osuextension: access to Canvas, which covers Master Melittologist progress tracking, equipment checkout, educational material, the Master Melittologist directory, and recording service hours. The link label should say what it is for, since "Ideal Logic" alone means nothing to most volunteers.
- Request supplies: https://forms.gle/FUv1vR16eCDV3w5z9
- Order educational outreach materials: https://forms.gle/FHFTdaeTr49yVha66
- Order taxonomic keys: https://forms.gle/nkKtwS8esv5SX2eL7
- Donate: https://extension.oregonstate.edu/master-melittologist/donate

Per-atlas links, chosen by the person's `person_membership`:
- The iNaturalist project their atlas uses, and any other links the atlas wants.
- This is reference data, e.g. an `atlas_link` satellite table (atlas, label, url, order) seeded like the other atlas rows, because it varies by atlas and will grow.
- A person with program-only membership or no membership sees only the program links. With acting-for or impersonation on, show the signed-in person's own atlas, not the other person's.

Placement, recommended: a separate group in the existing menu left of the brand (`MoreLinks`, src/app/views/layout.tsx). That menu is by design where everything a person can open lives, grouped by what it is for (beeline-45v.5), and on a phone it is already the only nav. Mark external links as leaving Beeline. A footer was considered and rejected: the app has none, the listings are long enough that a footer is rarely seen, and it would be a second place to look.

Copy goes through the message catalog. URLs are config or data, not copy.

Open: which iNat project each atlas uses (several sync; see BEELINE_SYNC_PROJECTS), and whether the Google Forms are the same for every atlas or only for OBA.

comments.author: Peter Abrahamsen
comments.text: Answered (Peter, 2026-09-21): the three Google Forms are program-wide for now. iNaturalist projects: Oregon (OBA) uses 18521 'Oregon Bee Atlas (Plant Images/SampleID)', Washington (WaBA) uses 166376 'Washington Bee Atlas (WaBA): Plant images/Sample IDs', and every other atlas (BC, ID, NM, OK), plus people with program-only or no membership, uses 99706 'Master Melittologist (outside of Oregon)'. Link by id (https://www.inaturalist.org/projects/<id>), not slug, since the WaBA slug carries a UUID. Because most atlases share a project, the link resolves as the atlas's own project, else 99706. That fallback is a stated default, not one row per atlas: a new atlas gets the umbrella project until it says otherwise. Forms being program-wide 'currently' means an atlas could later override one, and the atlas_link table allows for that.

title: A sample number left in the notes never becomes a sample, and nothing says so
description:
Some versions of the iNaturalist app cannot set observation fields, so a collector in the field writes the sample id into the observation's notes and is expected to copy it into the sampleId field later, at a computer (Peter, 2026-09-18). The notes are a staging area and the copy is the second half of the workflow.

When the copy does not happen, the record falls out of the pipeline silently. With no sampleId the observation is not observation_sample_candidate (schema/108), so minting never considers it AND the volunteer's front page never shows it — the placeholder row there exists for precisely this shape of thing, an observation numbered in the field and left unfinished, but it is keyed on having a sample number, which is the very thing missing.

MEASURED on the dev store after the full sync that brought notes in (beeline-hza), split by season as the convention requires:

  64,321 observations
     133 carry no sample-number field at all
      11 of those have a digit in the notes
       8 of those never became samples

  OPEN SEASON, 3 — all vinciau, 2026-05-23, notes '2', '1', '1C red cuckoo'
  settled, 5 — peter_maxwell 'Sample 2 - ground' (2025-07-19); michelesims
  'Sample 3 mesquite' and 'Sample 2' (2025-04-20); brianalindh 'Placeholder
  for collection number 768' (2020-07-01); laustin '$8 Mt' (2019-05-09,
  count 0, and probably not a sample number at all)

Six of the eight set NO observation field whatever — no count, no collection method — which is the app-limitation signature rather than someone forgetting one box. It also means that even with the number copied across most of them would still lack a count, so they would land as the dashboard's existing 0-specimen placeholder rather than as printable samples. That is the right destination: a thing the volunteer is asked to finish.

DO NOT PARSE THE NUMBER OUT AND MINT FROM IT. '1C red cuckoo' and '$8 Mt' are why: a guess here creates a collecting event that nobody recorded, and field numbers are permanent. The record already says the number in the collector's own words; what is missing is a prompt to the person who can confirm it.

SHAPE: a view naming observations that look like a collection record whose number is only in the notes — no sampleId, a digit in the notes, an observer who resolves to a person — and a row on that volunteer's front page asking them to copy it across on iNaturalist, in the same voice as the existing placeholder. The population is small, which is an argument for surfacing rather than automating.

Worth asking Andony/Arthur how common the affected app versions still are before sizing it: 3 live records is either the whole problem or the visible part of one.

title: A write landing on a row promotion rewrites fails the whole nightly promotion; nothing retries it
description: Found by bench/contention.ts (the synthetic '+ overlap' phase). DuckDB has no row locks, so when another connection commits an UPDATE to a sample row that the promotion transaction then tries to rewrite (the unprinted-locality follow in ingest/mint-samples.sql, the coordinate writes in promote-observations.sql), promotion fails with 'TransactionContext Error: Conflict on update!' and rolls back. Measured: the promotion lost every time — 5 of 5 passes on the workstation, 4 of 4 on the sandbox, zero completed — and the small writer never lost. No screen can do this today: an iNat-linked sample is not editable in the app, and edits to non-iNat samples never collided (0 conflicts across every real phase). It becomes real the day the staff override screen can write an iNat-linked sample, or a print freeze and the nightly touch the same rows. Before then: retry promoteObservations on a conflict (it is one idempotent transaction, so a retry is safe), a bounded number of times, and record the retry in job_run. The interactive side should get the same wrapper so a save that loses is retried rather than shown as an error.
close_reason: Fixed in #121

title: Saving a sample edit takes 2.6 s on the sandbox (1.4 s on a workstation)
description: Found by bench/pages.ts ('save a sample edit', bench/results/pages-sandbox-2026-09-18.json): POST /samples/:id/edit p50 2,596 ms on the sandbox and 1,424 ms on a workstation, with nothing else running — ten times a listing. Beside four readers it is 3.5 s, and beside the nightly 8.2 s (contention result, same date), partly because recordSampleChanges queues passes per snapshot, so an edit's narrowed pass waits behind the nightly's full one. Not yet profiled: the suspects are the narrowed recordSampleChanges pass restating the whole 10 MB sample-state.csv for one sample, and applySampleEdit's staging lookup. Profile first; the benchmark is the acceptance test.

title: Render label sheets off the main thread: a big run's PDF blocks every other request
description: Seen during the first demo (2026-09-18): Fly's health check failed at 21:33 UTC, mid-demo and not at a deploy, while a 5,000-label run's sheets were rendering. renderLabelsPdf (src/label-pdf.ts) is CPU-bound and runs on the app's one Node thread, so for its duration nothing else is served; the freeze's TypeScript half (composing and sorting labels) is the same shape. PR #79 cut the render from 7.2 s to 2.9 s on a workstation, which on the sandbox's two shared threads is still long enough to matter. Options: a worker_thread for the render (input is plain rows, output is bytes — an easy boundary), or render at approve time as a job rather than on first download. The cache means it only happens once per run either way.
notes: PR #82 (https://github.com/rainhead/beeline/pull/82), 2026-09-18. Worker thread (src/label-pdf-worker.ts), spawner and body in one file. Measured on the production shape (node --import tsx, 5,000 labels, 2.6 MB), polling /healthz throughout: in process 2 probes answered with a worst response of 3,996 ms; on a worker 47 probes with a worst of 36 ms, which is the app's idle latency in the same harness. Costs ~7% wall clock (4,186 -> 4,461 ms). runPdf now coalesces concurrent requests for one run. A worker needs its own TypeScript loader stated: production is already node --import tsx and inherits it, vitest is not. The freeze's TypeScript half stays on the main thread — it runs inside the freeze's transaction.
close_reason: Closed

comments.author: Peter Abrahamsen
comments.text: Peter shared the table diagram of Olivia's Access database on 2026-09-17 (rows still wanted). DayPlace(Day, Month, Year, LocID, MetaID) is OUR collecting event; CollectionEvent(EventID, DayPlaceID, CollMethID, StartTime, StopTime, CollectorID1-3, ProjectID, NumberOfBees, Temperature, Cloudiness, WindSpeed) is OUR sample — the words are swapped. BeeSpecimens(BarcodeID, EventID, SpeciesID, PlantID): keyed by barcode, one species with no determination history, and the floral host is per SPECIMEN, where Beeline has one per sample. Locations is a reusable site (LocationID, description, lat/lon in degrees and UTM, elevation m and ft, habitat, CountyID, LocationShorthand — possibly the BLM code), which is how visits to one place are tied across years. PlotFloralMetadata(MetaID, PlantID, Abundance) hangs the plot's plants off the day-place. Plants are the USDA PLANTS database (symbols), not iNaturalist taxa. Collectors carries email, institution and phone. Project(name, abbreviation, contact person, years active) is what we have been calling a program. CollectionMethod is a lookup, so protocol is already a controlled vocabulary for her. BeeSpeciesTraits is trait data and out of scope. Weather sits on the sample, not the day.

title: A program governs its own records: what that means for who sees what and what leaves
description: The program, not its funder, governs the data and specimens collected through it. BLM wants access and not ownership, and has no view yet on how. The same idea sits under every per-atlas policy already in CONTEXT.md: Washington's review before Ecdysis, Oregon's embargo, the per-atlas geoprivacy question. Peter wants it explored generally. Includes which program a sample was collected for, which cannot be read off geography the way an atlas can and so has to be stated.

title: Taking part in a program generalises atlas membership: signing up, volunteers and contractors
description: person_membership says a person belongs to an atlas, or to Master Melittology with no atlas. The BLM surveys are a program that is neither, people sign up to it as volunteers or BLM contractors, and other programs like it are expected; each needs to know who is and is not taking part. A person can plainly take part in more than one, which the current one-row-per-person table cannot say. How people sign up is an open question for Olivia.

title: People list: filter by active in the last 12 months (collected or signed in), or the complement
description: Peter, reviewing the sandbox with Nora (2026-09-16): /people needs a filter for who is still active — collected a sample or signed in within the last 12 months — and its complement, the people who have gone quiet. The two dates already on the roster ('Last sample' from sample_collector, 'Last seen' from the private store's person_activity, sign-in as the weaker fallback) are the inputs; active is either within 12 months. A store opened without the private store has no 'Last seen', so the filter degrades to last sample alone and should say so. Query-string filter like the listings, so a filtered roster is a shareable URL.
close_reason: Shipped in #68: the People page filters to active or not active in the last 12 calendar months, by a sample collected or a visit here, from the Last sample column's menu.

title: Review the QC rules: do they still make sense, and are they raised in the right places
description: Peter, reviewing the volunteer dashboard with Nora (2026-09-16): go through every qc_rule and ask whether it is still a rule, whether it belongs on the volunteer dashboard or on a staff surface, and whether its copy tells a volunteer what to do in the domain's words. Decisions already taken in that session: count_mismatch goes away once an iNat-linked sample's specimen count follows its observation; count_below_printed is a note for staff, not a dashboard item (the volunteer just gets extra labels and discards them); a zero-count observation is a placeholder the volunteer has yet to fill in and belongs on the dashboard even though it is not a sample; 'sync' is not a word volunteers know. Dashboard columns the rules map onto: sample number (duplicate_sample_number), place, coordinates, host plant, specimens; missing_required_field, missing_recommended_field, within_sample_disagreement and observation_missing_upstream have no natural column — decide whether each is a volunteer's problem at all.

title: Dashboard: a 'sync my samples now' button
description: Peter and Nora, reviewing the volunteer dashboard on the sandbox (2026-09-16): a volunteer who has just fixed an observation on iNaturalist should not have to wait for the 2am nightly to see the flag clear. Add a button on the dashboard that runs an interactive-window sync scoped to the signed-in person's observations (their iNat user id, the trailing window), then promotes, so the page reflects the fix on reload. Scoped to one observer so it stays inside the interactive SLA; rate-limit per person (once every few minutes) so it cannot be hammered. Acting-for should sync the person being acted for. Nothing on the page should say 'sync' to a volunteer — the copy is 'Check iNaturalist now' or similar.

title: A curated rename erases the name the source wrote, where verbatim_identification is NULL
description:
ingest/taxon-aliases.csv (and the coming curation layer) change the (rank, name) a determination resolves to, via legacy_expert_target / legacy_volunteer_target (ingest/promote-determinations.sql:68,94). Where determination.verbatim_identification is NULL — which it is for every row whose name arrived in parted columns rather than as a scientificName string — nothing then records what the source actually spelled.

Confirmed on the dev store 2026-09-15: the volunteer determination behind the Osmia rubiflorus -> Osmia ribifloris alias (#64) now resolves to Osmia ribifloris with verbatim_identification NULL. The written spelling is gone. promote-determinations.sql:120 says verbatim is the only record of what the determiner wrote once staging freezes at cutover, so this is exactly the guarantee being lost.

Blast radius for the ITIS adoption decided on beeline-45v.1: 496 determinations adopt a new name and 408 of them have NULL verbatim today.

Fix: where a curated decision (alias or adoption) changes the resolved name, record the overruled spelling as verbatim_identification when it would otherwise be NULL. That is not inventing a name — it is keeping what the parted columns spelled at the moment the program overrules it.
notes: PR #65 (https://github.com/rainhead/beeline/pull/65). Close when it merges. Verified by reseed 2026-09-15: volunteer verbatim 0 -> 8 (Agopostemon x2, Peponapsis x2, Ericrosis, Lassioglossum, Osmia rubiflorus, Protoxaea glorioso), expert unchanged at 30,492/187,011, tree and records identical. Known gap kept deliberately: a subgenus spelling spans two columns, so the five '(Peponapis)' rows record nothing rather than a half-name.
close_reason: Closed

title: A genus known only from volunteer determinations never gets a family, and lands under Insecta
description:
ingest/seed-animals.sql builds its genus list from legacy_det_taxa AND legacy_vol_det_taxa, but legacy_genus_family resolves the family from legacy_det_taxa only. A genus nobody but a volunteer determined is therefore minted with no family and falls through to its order, or to Insecta when the order is unstated too.

Measured on the dev store after the 2026-09-15 reseed: 12 genera sit directly under Insecta, and 11 of them have a family in the volunteer columns and none in the expert ones — Centris, Melitta, Peponapis, Protoxaea, Exomalopsis, Lithurgus, Ericrocis, Townsendiella, Pseudopanurgus, Caupolicana, Leiopodus (Apidae, Andrenidae, Melittidae, Megachilidae, Colletidae; every one correct). Protohalonia is the real unknown: two expert rows, no family stated anywhere in the source, so it stays where it is.

Fix: the family fallback reads the volunteer view after the expert one, so the staff list still wins, then expert co-occurrence, then volunteer. legacy_taxon_uncurated does not catch this — it only asks whether a name is in the staff bee list.
notes: PR #64. Review (CodeRabbit) found the fallback could select a family with no node; the volunteer arm now requires the family to exist, rather than minting volunteer family nodes, since that insert defaults an unstated order to Hymenoptera and would misfile a non-bee family. Verified 2026-09-15 by reseed: same tree, Protohalonia alone under Insecta.
close_reason: Closed

title: Taxonomy page anyone signed in can read, and a menu beside the brand for everything beyond the records
description:
Expose the curated insect taxonomy (animal) on the website as a drill-down: /taxonomy/:rank/:name shows a node's lineage, its ITIS standing (animal_itis), and its children with specimen counts by determination of record; a name search and an ITIS-standing filter switch to a flat paged list, which is the worklist curation later grows into. Readable by everyone signed in, like the glossary, so its copy goes through the message catalog.

Peter, 2026-09-15: the growing set of administrative, curational and reference destinations is grouped by purpose rather than audience, in the account menu. The header nav keeps only Samples and Specimens; Glossary, Taxonomy, People, Jobs and Design move into the account menu, each still shown only to whoever may open it.
notes: PR #63 (https://github.com/rainhead/beeline/pull/63). Close when it merges. Decisions (Peter, 2026-09-15): taxonomy readable by everyone like the glossary; the menu is scoped by purpose rather than audience. REVISED the same day: that menu is the hamburger LEFT OF THE BRAND, shown at every width (on a phone the records collapse into it too), not the account menu. The account menu is for the person signed in and their own things: sign in/out, acting for someone, later their mailing address. Who may curate stays with beeline-45v.1.
close_reason: Closed

title: Each animal node carries its ITIS TSN, matched from a carried ITIS extract
description: The first work item on beeline-45v: store each animal node's ITIS TSN beside it, so a name can be checked against ITIS and, later, followed through its changes. ITIS reference data lives in an itis_taxon table filled by a fetch on maderas and a load into the store, carried by db:reseed like inat_place because it comes from the network; animal.itis_tsn is matched on (rank, name) within Insecta whenever the table is loaded and after every legacy promotion. Views name what matched as valid, what ITIS treats as a synonym, what ITIS does not have, and any homonym the match cannot decide. Survey on beeline-45v: 3,360 of 3,567 nodes valid, 38 synonyms, 169 absent. Not here: the volunteer name picker (roadmap phase 6) and the curation layer (beeline-45v.1).
notes:
Built 2026-09-15. Extract of the 2026-08-26 release: 337,419 insect names at admitted ranks (the Animalia-Arthropoda-Insecta chain included) and 92,892 synonym links, 87 outdated names linking to more than one current name; two CSVs, 27 MB, extracted in under 4 s from the 925 MB database. Trial on a copy of the dev store (migrations 0027-0029, then pnpm itis:load, 3 s): 3,357 nodes valid, 37 synonym, 4 homonym (Hoplitis truncata, Hoplitis semirubra, Ceratina punctigena, and Coelioxys octodentata, which ITIS has as two outdated names), 169 absent; animal_itis_stale empty. DuckDB 1.5.5 accepts deleting and reinserting the same TSNs in one transaction, which the reload relies on and a test exercises.
PR #62: https://github.com/rainhead/beeline/pull/62. The extract is in data/itis/ on maderas (fetched end to end with pnpm itis:fetch, 24 s), ready to upload to Fly once the PR is merged and deployed.
Loaded on Fly 2026-09-15 06:16 UTC (release v11, migration 0029 at boot; pnpm itis:load in a two-minute maintenance window): 337,419 taxa, 92,892 synonym links, ITIS as of 2026-08-26. The Fly store's 3,547 taxa stand 3,357 valid, 38 synonym, 4 homonym, 148 absent. It differs from the dev-store trial (37 synonym, 169 absent) because Fly was rebuilt with #59's name rules: 20 misspelt or mis-bracketed taxa merged away, and 'Xenoglossa (Peponapis) pruinosa' became 'Xenoglossa pruinosa', which ITIS lists as an outdated name.
close_reason: Merged in #62

title: Require the verbatim name on every determination channel except legacy import
description: A determination's verbatim_identification is the name as the determiner wrote it, and the decision recorded on beeline-45v is that it is always kept, because not every name will resolve to an ITIS taxon. Nothing enforces that: the column is nullable on every channel. Legacy import has to stay exempt — 225,669 of 256,161 legacy determinations come from parted columns and never had a whole name to keep, and promotion deliberately invents none — but in-app and Ecdysis determinations do not exist yet, so a CHECK can hold them from the first row. A deployed store cannot gain a CHECK (ADR 0006); nothing writes those channels there today, so the migration says so rather than adding a stand-in view.
notes: Built 2026-09-14: CHECK (channel = 'legacy_import' OR verbatim_identification IS NOT NULL) in schema/040, with migration 0027 carrying the column comment and the reason no stand-in view is needed. Tests that wrote in_app or ecdysis_import determinations now give the name as written.
close_reason: Merged in #59

title: Legacy names resolve to the node the writer meant: case, bracketed subgenera, and a spelling alias file
description:
Seeding mints an animal node for every name string it sees, so a volunteer's 'Agopostemon' or 'andrena' becomes a taxon of its own and a determination on it is filed apart from every other Agapostemon. The ITIS survey on beeline-45v found ~17 such nodes, and every one of the 16 current-season determinations on a name ITIS lacks is one of them.

Most are not misspellings, and a list is the wrong fix for those: letter case (genusVolDet 'andrena', specificEpithet 'Mesillae'), and a subgenus written in brackets where the parser does not look for one (specificEpithet '(Lasioglossum)'; genusVolDet and the staff taxonomy list's genus column 'Xenoglossa (Peponapis)'). Those become parsing rules, and the volunteer and staff-list columns move into ingest/parse-names.sql, which CLAUDE.md already says is the one place names come apart and which today only parses the expert columns. The genuine misspellings (Agopostemon, Lassioglossum, Ericrosis, Peponapsis, Protoxaea glorioso, Osmia rubiflorus) go in a curated ingest/taxon-aliases.csv with an unused-alias view, the same shape as ingest/collector-aliases.csv.

Out of scope, because they are taxonomic choices rather than typing: gender endings (Lasioglossum aspilurus, Epimelissodes obliquus), names from the staff list that ITIS lacks, and species groups (Triepeolus verbesinae complex). Those are beeline-45v.1 and beeline-8g7.
notes:
Built 2026-09-14. Rules in ingest/parse-names.sql cover all three column sources (expert, volunteer via the new legacy_vol_det_taxa, staff taxonomy list); misspellings in ingest/taxon-aliases.csv (6 lines) with legacy_taxon_alias_unused. Osmia rubiflorus is deliberately not aliased: ITIS has no near name, so the intended spelling is unknown. Verified by re-promoting a copy of the dev store's staging: 186 determinations move to the node their writer meant (15 open season, 171 settled) and no other determination changes; 256,161 determinations before and after, 0 unresolved; malformed node names 29 → 0 (18 were double-bracketed subgenera like 'Andrena (Andrena (Andrena))'); 20 fewer nodes; 0 unused aliases. The sandbox needs pnpm db:reseed to pick this up, since it is a promotion change.
Correction to the note above: the re-promotion moved 188 determinations, not 186 — 15 open season and 173 settled (letter case 0/101, bracketed subgenus 3/72, alias 12/0). The commit message on 7c41272 carries the wrong total.
close_reason: Merged in #59

title: Curate the animal taxonomy over ITIS: additions, departures, and a check against each ITIS release
description:
Over 5,000 determinations in the store use a name ITIS either lacks or would rename, so an animal table that simply copies ITIS would misname or flatten them. ITIS is the program's basis for bees and bycatch (Andony, 2026-09-11), but the survey on beeline-45v (2026-09-14) shows ITIS reviews its bees genus by genus and unevenly, and that the program's taxonomists already depart from it. The curated taxonomy has to be ITIS plus a layer the taxonomists own.

What the layer holds:

- Additions — a taxon ITIS does not have becomes an animal node with no ITIS id. Agapostemon subtilior (1,768 determinations) is absent from ITIS, not even as a synonym, although ITIS reviewed Agapostemon in 2024. ITIS carries no bee subgenera outside Colletidae, so Dialictus (1,735 determinations) and the other 29 subgenus nodes are additions too.
- Departures — ITIS has the taxon, but the program accepts a different name or placement. Brachymelecta californica (812 determinations) is only Xeromelecta californica in ITIS, whose Xeromelecta review predates the move. The staff taxonomy list files species under Protandrena that ITIS keeps in Pseudopanurgus: not lag, a different treatment.
- Spellings that resolve to a real node — Agopostemon, andrena, Hylaeus Mesillae and ~27 more are nodes of their own today because seeding mints one for every name it sees. They should point at the real node, with the typed text kept as the determination's verbatim name. This is staff bookkeeping rather than a taxonomic claim, and may want to live apart from the other two.

Each addition and departure says who made it and why, and records what ITIS said at the time (TSN, name, valid or not). That record is what lets each new ITIS release be checked against the layer: a departure ITIS has since adopted can be retired, and an addition ITIS now carries, or a TSN whose name or status changed under a departure, is flagged for a taxonomist. Without that check the layer goes stale in the opposite direction from ITIS. ITIS publishes its whole database monthly as SQLite (https://www.itis.gov/downloads/, ~225 MB zipped); fetching and diffing it is work for maderas.

Shape, by precedent in this repo: until cutover, a curated CSV replayed onto every rebuild the way data/person-overlay.csv is, with its changes kept as append-only events per docs/adr/0007-authored-changes-are-events.md. docs/schema-sketch.md already anticipates roughly this ("git-versioned seed data plus an append-only taxon_change log"). It depends on animal carrying an ITIS TSN, which is the first work item on beeline-45v.

Not decided here:

- Who curates, and through what: a screen, or git. CONTEXT.md names Lincoln Best today, with other taxonomists possibly joining.
- Whether a departure is program-wide or can differ by atlas — beeline-0zb.
- What happens by default to the 38 names ITIS would rename (560 determinations, e.g. Lasioglossum zonulum → zonulus): adopt ITIS's name, or hold each as a departure until a taxonomist rules.
- Names that are not a taxon at all — morphospecies (Melissodes sp.1), species groups (Triepeolus verbesinae complex, 32 determinations) — beeline-8g7.
notes:
DECIDED (Peter, 2026-09-15), on the 38 names ITIS would rename, measured on the dev store: ADOPT the 19 ending corrections (484 dets) and the 5 same-genus synonymies (12 dets) — 24 nodes, 496 determinations, 12 of them merges into a node the tree already holds (zonulum -> zonulus alone is 214). DEPART on the 14 genus moves (63 dets): Protandrena x10 -> Pseudopanurgus (0 dets), Xenoglossa pruinosa -> Peponapis pruinosa (0), Epimelissodes obliqua -> Svastra obliqua (35), Xenoglossodes pomonae -> Tetraloniella pomonae (28). The staff taxonomy list files 13 of those 14 under our genus, which is the evidence that they are a treatment rather than lag.

Also decided: curation is through the agent for now, so the layer lives in git — a curated file replayed on every rebuild, like ingest/taxon-aliases.csv and ingest/person-overlay.csv — not a screen.

DECIDED (Peter, 2026-10-02): the seed stops minting a node for every name it sees. Resolution rule, in order: a name valid in ITIS is admitted as an ITIS name with no curation row (the staff checklist stays as the tree's seed and the volunteer picker, but is bees-only and stale — 19 ITIS-valid species experts determined 2,007 times are off it, L. villosulum 827 alone); an ITIS synonym is adopted by default (resolve to the current name, verbatim_identification keeps the spelling) unless a departure row keeps ours; a name absent from ITIS needs an addition row or the determination is held and reported, as the Ecdysis loader does. The curation file holds only genuine claims, and every row credits a taxonomist (required — the agent transcribes, never decides) and carries a reference (DOI/URL where a paper is behind it) beside the reason and what ITIS said at the time.

Sequencing: nothing changes in seeding until the taxonomist has ruled. The worklist is a Google Sheet for Lincoln, built from the dev store on 2026-10-02 (ITIS 2026-08-26 release, legacy fetched 2026-09-28): https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1lTNxHcILmmVwAk9dtgHFIcGmwYA_mMSTBOT_Ym1WV6M — 6 tabs: 38 names ITIS lacks (24 subgenera; A. subtilior 1,802, B. californica 859), 38 ITIS would rename (24 same-genus, 14 genus moves), 31 ITIS-valid names off the checklist, 4 homonyms, 98 checklist names ITIS lacks with zero dets, 11 wasp rows for whoever determines bycatch. Oddities flagged there, not decided: Epimelissodes obliqua (35, ITIS: Svastra obliqua) and E. obliquus (32, absent) are one species under two endings; Ceratina (Hemihalictus) looks like a typing error. The sheet's filled-in rows become the curation file when they come back; build script in the session scratchpad, regenerate from the store rather than editing the sheet's data by hand.
2026-10-02: sheet emailed to Lincoln; out-of-office reply, so answers are expected the week of 2026-10-05 at the earliest. Blocked on him until then.
2026-10-02: the curation layer's shape is built ahead of Linc's answers — PR #124 (branch taxon-curation): animal_curation (schema/022) + ingest/taxon-curation.csv replayed by src/taxon-curation.ts, animal_curation_stale for the release check, and pnpm taxon:decisions <sheet-id> to merge the sheet's signed answers into the file. Seeding is untouched; what an undecided name does once the seed stops minting is still Peter's call when the sheet comes back.
2026-10-03: PR #124 merged — animal_curation, the curation file and its applier, the stale check, pnpm taxon:decisions, and the taxonomy page showing a decision. Still open: Linc's answers (expected week of 2026-10-05), running taxon:decisions on them, and then the seeding change (stop minting undecided names) — Peter's call once the answers say how many names it touches.
2026-10-03: PR #125 replaces taxon:decisions (dropdown-matching interpreter) with taxon:fetch-sheet (tabs → data/taxon-decisions/<date>/, to be read) and taxon:decide (record a decision said in words, or --batch under one signature; fills TSN/current name/release from the store, refuses what ITIS contradicts, merges). Reading Linc's answers — prose, or 'mostly fine, fix X and Y' by email — is the agent's job; the reason column quotes him verbatim with where it came from.
2026-10-03: PR #125 merged — taxon:fetch-sheet and taxon:decide replace the interpreter. Next: Linc's answers; fetch the sheet, read it, record with taxon:decide (batch for 'as proposed', then corrections), review the diff, taxon:apply.

title: Printed samples: show divergence from the label (date, locality, coordinates)
description:
Decided with Peter, 2026-09-14. Once a sample's labels print, its date, locality and coordinates stop following iNaturalist; everything else keeps following (beeline-1kb.2). Legacy-printed samples are included. When iNaturalist's value for one of those three moves away from what printed, that is a DIVERGENCE FROM THE LABEL. This bead makes divergences visible instead of silently dropping them.

A DIVERGENCE IS NOT A QC CONCERN. Nothing is wrong with the record, which still agrees with its label. So divergences do not go through QC flags, the QC home, manual flags (beeline-plu) or waivers (beeline-1kb.9). They get their own presentation and their own way to be resolved.

NOTHING IS RECORDED WHEN AN EDIT IS NOT TAKEN. The observation's new value is already stored with each sync, so a divergence is a comparison worked out on the fly, like sample_elevation_stale. It cannot go stale and no writer has to remember it.

WHEN IT COUNTS: only when the difference would change what the label says.
- Coordinates: a distance test of about 100 m, NOT a comparison of rounded digits. 100 m is what three decimal places resolve to (Andony, GitHub #22). Comparing digits flags moves of a few metres that cross a rounding boundary (see the measurement in the notes).
- Date: a different day or date range. A time-only change does not count.
- Locality: a change to the printed text. How to treat trivial differences (case, punctuation, the fill-only refresh's normalisation) is open. Whether county, state and country count as locality is open on beeline-1kb.2.

SURFACES (settled in outline):
1. Sample page (/samples/:id): beside each printed value, what iNaturalist says now.
2. Volunteer line on their own record. They made the edit, probably to fix a mistake. Copy goes through the message catalog.
3. A staff list, LATER, once post-cutover data shows it is needed. The measurement found none in two weeks.

RESOLVING: a staff correction moves the record to the new value and then offers a reprint. Staff can mark any label for reprint (beeline-1kb.5). Reprints are always a deliberate choice, never automatic.

OPEN UX QUESTIONS:
- Which side is wrong? A divergence means either the label is wrong (reprint) or iNaturalist is wrong (the volunteer should undo their edit). The UI has to ask, not assume. Who answers: the volunteer, staff, or either?
- What does 'keep what printed' record? Does the divergence disappear for good, or come back if iNaturalist's value changes again? Probably the latter: it is acknowledged against a specific upstream value.
- Can a volunteer act, for example 'my label is wrong, please reprint' (a reprint request), or only see it?
- Where do staff meet divergences, if not on the QC home: a list, a marker on the listings, or the sample page only?
- After turnover the lab holds the specimen, and swapping a label falls to the label czar or another lab member rather than the volunteer (CONTEXT.md 'Label czar'). Does the person who resolves a divergence change with custody?
- Bulk: a volunteer who re-edits many observations at once.
notes:
MEASURED (2026-09-14). Source: the sandbox's data/sample-change.csv, 16 nightly passes from 2026-08-31 to 2026-09-14. Edited samples were matched to the local dev store (2026-09-10) to find the ones with printed labels. Every legacy specimen carries a field number, so every legacy sample counts as printed (66,293 of 67,887). Matched: 80 of 82 edited existing samples.

What the passes did: minting created 594 samples; those are not edits. 82 existing samples were edited, 58 of them printed.

Printed samples, split by season:
- Coordinates: 55 edits, 45 in settled seasons and 10 in the open season. NONE moved 100 m or more; the largest moved 58 m. 46 were iNaturalist's full-precision copy of the same point replacing the legacy import's rounded one (location_source legacy_import → inat_public). That is a one-off upgrade from the legacy data, not a pin move.
- Other fields: 2 staff edits made in the app (locality and county), which are corrections and not upstream changes, and 1 geoprivacy value filled in, which is not on the label.
- Result: ZERO upstream edits in two weeks that would meaningfully change a printed label. No date change, no locality change, no count decrease, no deleted observation, no coordinate move of 100 m or more.

Samples not printed yet (open season, minted from iNaturalist): 20 coordinate edits, 9 of them moved 100 m or more, the largest 6.4 km. So volunteers do move pins, on current-season samples. After cutover those are exactly the samples that print within 1–4 weeks of collection. How often a move comes AFTER printing therefore depends on how soon after collecting volunteers fix things, and two weeks of late-season data cannot say.

Consequences for the design:
- COORDINATES NEED A DISTANCE TEST, NOT A COMPARISON OF ROUNDED DIGITS. Comparing at three decimals flagged 5 of the 55 edits on printed samples as label changes, and every one of them moved less than 60 m. A few metres across a rounding boundary changes a digit. Use a threshold near the label's own precision (about 100 m).
- BUILD ORDER: the sample page and the volunteer line first. Leave the staff list until a season of post-cutover data shows it is needed; right now it would be empty.
- Open question for beeline-1kb.2: do samples whose labels the LEGACY system printed count as locked? If they do, the 46-a-fortnight precision upgrade would be refused after cutover. Nothing is lost by that, since it is the same point, but staff should never be shown those changes. The distance test hides them anyway.
Peter, 2026-09-14: legacy-printed samples ARE locked (beeline-1kb.2). The refused-edit comparison therefore runs over them too, and that is where the distance test earns its keep: without it, every full-precision copy of a legacy point would show up as a refused edit.

title: At cutover: move the content people need to do their work from Canvas
description:
Andony, meeting 2026-09-11: copy over the content of the program's existing Canvas site (https://canvas.oregonstate.edu/courses/1774556).

This is the first concrete step of 'Canvas retirement' in docs/surrounding-systems.md. That scope replaces the program's use of Canvas with static content plus some replacement for its forum and grading. This bead covers the CONTENT only. The forum and grading need their own decisions and are not part of it.

Getting at it: the course requires an OSU sign-in, so nobody on the project can read it by fetching the URL. Canvas can export a whole course as a Common Cartridge (.imscc) file (Settings → Export Course Content): pages, files, modules and quizzes, with their structure. Someone with instructor access should make that export first, so we are working from the whole course and not from copy-pasted pages.

Questions:
- WHERE the content goes. Beeline is the internal tool, behind a sign-in, and the volunteer glossary (/glossary) is the closest thing it has. The public tier (beeline-58b) is the program's public face. Course material for enrolled volunteers could belong to either one, or be split between them: 'what the program is' public, training material behind the sign-in.
- WHETHER it can be public. This repo is public, so anything committed to it is published. That includes content written for enrolled volunteers only, third-party images and videos embedded in the course, and anything carrying OSU licensing terms. Check before any of it lands in git.
- Format: the rendered static content surrounding-systems.md imagines (11ty?), or content in the app, where volunteer-facing copy goes through the message catalog.
- What is still current. Some course material will be out of date, or will describe the legacy system's workflows that Beeline replaces (weekly QC emails, for example). Copy it faithfully first, or edit it on the way across?
- Timing: when Canvas access ends, if a date is known.
notes:
Andony, meeting 2026-09-11: the program is 'not ready for it' yet. Deferred with no date. Pick it up when Andony says the program is ready, not on a schedule.
SCOPE CORRECTED (Peter, meeting 2026-09-11). Canvas is NOT being retired for some time. Educational content stays there. What moves, at cutover, is anything people need in order to do their work, as opposed to material that is purely educational.

What that changes in the description above:
- The deadline is cutover, not open-ended.
- Most of it probably lands in Beeline rather than on the public site. People doing the work are the people signed in, and Beeline already has the kind of home this needs: the glossary and the QC self-service instructions in the message catalog.
- 'Copy faithfully' does not apply. Any work-supporting content in Canvas today describes the legacy system's workflows, so what moves is really a description of how to do the same job in Beeline. Canvas is where to look for WHICH jobs need explaining; it is not the text.
- The 'can it be public' question mostly goes away for content written fresh for Beeline. It still applies to anything carried over word for word, including images.
- Still needed first: a list of the course's pages sorted into 'needed to do the work' and 'educational'. That needs someone with access, and the course export is still the easiest way to get it.

title: Docs: land the 2026-09-11 meeting decisions in CONTEXT.md and the roadmap
description:
Decisions made in the 2026-09-11 meeting with Andony are recorded on beads. The glossary and roadmap still say something different:

- CONTEXT.md 'Upstream' and 'Post-print trouble': once a specimen is minted, the sample stops taking iNaturalist's edits, except the host plant (beeline-1kb.2).
- CONTEXT.md 'Curated taxonomy' and docs/schema-sketch.md: ITIS is the basis for bees and bycatch, not the GBIF backbone, which was only ever a candidate (beeline-45v).
- CONTEXT.md 'Determination': each atlas decides whether a volunteer determination may appear in any public view or export. Washington approves record by record; Oregon trusts the person (beeline-pyr).
- docs/roadmap.md phase 7, Export: no automated connection to Ecdysis. Each atlas's staff moves data by hand, and GBIF probably the same.
- Mailing addresses are managed in Beeline, not via IdeaLogic (GitHub #34), and Beeline produces the Avery mailing labels (beeline-1kb.16). Check whether any doc says otherwise.

One pull request, glossary wording only. The design questions stay on their own beads.
notes:
Also from the meeting: Canvas will not be retired for some time. Only the content people need to do their work moves over, at cutover (beeline-jn3). docs/surrounding-systems.md 'Canvas retirement' reads as though the whole thing is being replaced, so say it is a later scope, with the work-supporting part split out.
Two details in this description were superseded before PR #58 merged:
- The lock starts when labels print, not at minting, and covers date, locality and coordinates only.
- There is no per-atlas gate inside Beeline; staff choose what to upload (beeline-pyr).
The PR reflects the final state.
close_reason: Merged in #58

title: Staff specimen downloads carry volunteer determinations, marked, so staff choose what goes downstream
description:
Settled 2026-09-14. The notes show how it got here. Several earlier notes describe a design that was REVERSED, so read this description first.

Each atlas decides whether a volunteer determination goes anywhere outside the program, and its staff apply that decision OUTSIDE Beeline. For the time being Beeline exports nothing automatically to Ecdysis or GBIF (Andony, 2026-09-11).
- Washington: Caleb Lankford downloads specimen data from Beeline, volunteer determinations included, and uploads to Ecdysis the ones he judges good.
- Oregon: Lincoln Best passes volunteer determinations on only from a volunteer determining in batches who knows what they are doing. He also withholds records under the publication embargo. Both are done by choosing what to upload.
(Andony's account, with Lincoln present.) Other atlases have not been asked yet. Olivia (New Mexico) is 2026-09-17; BC, Idaho and Oklahoma have not been contacted.

WHAT BEELINE OWES:
- The staff specimen download INCLUDES volunteer determinations. It does not filter them.
- It marks each one clearly enough to choose from: channel, determiner, verbatim name, and whether an expert determination exists for the specimen.
- No approval state is modelled.

STILL OPEN:
- Does any public page Beeline itself serves show volunteer determinations? No such page exists yet.
- What does the download need so an atlas's taxon-obscured coordinate policy can be applied by hand at upload (beeline-1kb.7.1)?
notes:
ANSWERED IN PART (Peter, meeting 2026-09-11):
- Scope: the gate applies to ANY public view or export of the data, to any system. That covers GBIF and Ecdysis, the atlases' reports, and any public page Beeline itself might serve (a profile or atlas page, for example), not only exports.
- Caleb's approval is a MARK on the volunteer's determination, not a new expert determination. The volunteer stays the identifier and the mark records who approved it. The mark probably also needs an author, a time and a way to be withdrawn, which would make it an event like the others (ADR 0007). That shape is a guess, not a decision.
- Still unknown: whether the approval is recorded in Beeline or happens in Caleb's own workflow outside it.

What this does to the rest of the bead: every public read and every export has to ask one question, 'may this volunteer determination be shown outside the program?', and each atlas answers it differently. Washington answers with a mark on the record, Oregon with trust in the person. That should be defined once, as a view like the QC rules, rather than repeated in each export.
DECIDED (Andony, meeting 2026-09-11): Beeline will not have an automated connection to Ecdysis for now. Each atlas's staff will move the data there by hand, and GBIF will probably work the same way. For this bead, that means an export is a file Beeline gives staff, not something Beeline sends. The gate therefore has to be applied in the file Beeline produces: staff should not have to remove unapproved volunteer determinations themselves. Beeline's own public pages still need the gate as well.
ANSWERED, and it REVERSES what this bead assumed (Peter, 2026-09-14). The per-atlas gate is not applied in Beeline:
- Washington: Caleb downloads specimen data from Beeline, including any volunteer determinations, and uploads to Ecdysis the ones he wants. His approval IS that choice. Nothing is recorded in Beeline, so there is no mark.
- Oregon: Lincoln Best handles records he wants to embargo the same way, by choosing what to upload.
- For the time being Beeline exports nothing automatically to Ecdysis or GBIF.
So the earlier notes are wrong in two places. An export does NOT have to leave out unapproved volunteer determinations; it has to INCLUDE them, marked clearly enough (channel, determiner, verbatim name) for staff to choose. And there is no approval state to model. What is left of this bead is that requirement on the staff download, plus whether any public page Beeline itself serves would show volunteer determinations, and no such page exists yet.

title: Ground the animal taxonomy in ITIS
description:
Decided by Andony in the 2026-09-11 meeting: ITIS is the basis for bee and bycatch taxonomy, and already has been in practice. Volunteer determinations are made against it. So when the store says a volunteer determined a specimen as a species, that species should be an ITIS name.

Right now nothing in the store says so. 'animal' is seeded from whatever names the legacy records contained (ingest/seed-animals.sql), with no reference to any authority. CONTEXT.md still calls the program itself the authority and names the GBIF backbone as a candidate source for the non-bee part (the schema sketch says the same). ITIS replaces that candidate.

Work:
- Store each animal node's ITIS TSN beside it, the way hosts carry an iNaturalist taxon id, so a name can be checked against ITIS and follow its changes.
- Survey the ~3,567 seeded nodes against ITIS. How many match exactly, how many are synonyms ITIS would rename, and how many ITIS does not have? Report the counts by season. The names ITIS lacks are expected to be mostly morphospecies, and those wait on the taxonomists (beeline-8g7).
- Decide what a volunteer picks a name from when determinations are entered in the app: an ITIS-derived list rather than free text.
- Rewrite CONTEXT.md 'Curated taxonomy', the comment on the animal table, and docs/schema-sketch.md 'Curated taxonomy' to say ITIS.

Still open, and not decided in the meeting:
- Standards for morphospecies and other undescribed entities, which the taxonomists will set (beeline-8g7).
- Whether expert determinations arriving from Ecdysis must also resolve to ITIS, or whether experts may depart from it (beeline-0zb).
- Is 'animal' a copy of ITIS, or ITIS plus program-curated additions? Morphospecies push toward additions.
notes: STATUS (2026-09-15): the COMMENT ON TABLE animal item is DONE — schema/020 now says the taxonomy is based on ITIS, landed with beeline-45v.4 (#62), so that work item can be struck from the note above. Also done since: beeline-45v.5 (#63) exposes the tree at /taxonomy for anyone signed in, with each node's animal_itis standing, which is where curation will land; beeline-0wu and beeline-k5j (#64) fixed two seeding defects the page made visible. On the dev store now: 3,357 current in ITIS, 38 outdated, 4 ambiguous, 147 absent. Still open on this epic: the schema conflict (animal_id NOT NULL vs verbatim_identification nullable) and the ITIS-derived name list for volunteer entry; the curation layer itself is beeline-45v.1.

title: Mailing labels: Avery-format PDF of addresses for a print run
description:
Decided in the 2026-09-11 meeting with Andony: Beeline produces the mailing labels, not just the specimen labels. This follows from managing addresses ourselves (beeline-1kb.6, GitHub #34 closed): no other system holds the addresses to print them from.

For a print run, render a PDF of address labels laid out for an Avery sheet, so staff can print them and stick them on the envelopes that carry each collector's cut-apart labels.

Things it has to get right, from the address data already measured on beeline-1kb.6:
- One mailing label per address, not per person. Households and labs share addresses (26 shared, including groups of 8, 12 and 16), so a run that includes both Pedersons prints one envelope rather than two.
- People whose record says not to mail ("Keep in lab", a course code) get no mailing label; they still need to show up somewhere so their specimen labels are not lost.
- A collector in the run with no address has to be named before printing, not dropped silently.
- Like the specimen labels (beeline-1kb.4), render from what the run saw when it froze, so a reprint of the sheet matches.

Open questions:
- Which Avery product (e.g. 5160, 30 per sheet)? Ask Arthur what stock the program has.
- Is there a return address, and does it vary by atlas?
- Rendering can probably share PDF tooling with beeline-1kb.4, but the layout is unrelated.

title: Staff manually flag a sample for QC (looks wrong, breaks no rule)
description:
Raised by Andony in the 2026-09-11 meeting. Staff can see a sample that looks wrong — a date, place, or determination that is implausible — without any QC rule firing on it. Today there is no way to say so: QC findings come only from the rule views, so a human's doubt has nowhere to land and the volunteer is never asked.

Staff should be able to flag a sample by hand, with a note saying what looks wrong, so it reaches the collector the way a rule finding does and can be resolved.

The inverse of beeline-1kb.9 (waivers: a rule fires and staff say it is fine); the two probably want one design.

Open questions:
- Does a manual flag block printing, like a blocking rule, or only ask?
- Who clears it — the staffer who raised it, any staff, or the volunteer by editing?
- Storage: an authored event (ADR 0007 shape, survives rebuild) rather than a table the blow-away erases.
- Samples only, or specimens/determinations too?
notes:
ANSWERED IN PART (Peter, 2026-09-18, after the first print-run demo): the point of a manual flag is to HOLD A SAMPLE BACK FROM PRINTING.
