3. LISTINGS SCOPE keeps its geographic meaning and gains 'outside'; collector membership becomes a SEPARATE staff-only filter. The two axes are independent - one control answering both would answer neither, given 469 of the 632 are members travelling.
4. SAMPLE SIDE gets all three: a QC rule, the CA/CAN fix, and a positive way to tell the two absences apart. Mechanism: atlas_region(state_province PK, country, atlas_id) replaces the six-way CASE in promote-legacy.sql. A row with a NULL atlas positively says 'known region, no atlas covers it'; no row at all says geography did not resolve. Keyed on state_province, NOT (country, state): country adds no discrimination for OR/WA/BC/ID/NM/OK and would regress the one null-country Oregon sample. Country is recorded on the row so a mismatch can be flagged.

Country: normalise to ISO alpha-3 at promotion (CA->CAN, NZ->NZL), matching the 'USA' that 62,410 rows already use. The CA/CAN split affects BC too, not only YT: 2,321 CA + 1,497 CAN.

The two CAN/UT samples are Bonnie Zand's, Kane County, Mount Carmel, 37.19N -112.65W - unambiguously Utah, and she is a BC collector whose country field kept her usual CAN. NOT hard-patched: under the new lookup they match region UT (country USA), disagree with the sample's CAN, and the new rule flags them by name. Surfacing the bug beats silently filing it as 'outside', and it is the rule's own proof.
Built (2026-08-24). All four decisions implemented; pnpm typecheck + 272 tests green, migration verified both directions against a store built at the previous schema, and against a copy of the dev store.

SCHEMA
- person_membership replaces person_home_atlas: (person_id PK, kind CHECK IN ('atlas','program'), atlas_id, CHECK ((kind='atlas') = (atlas_id IS NOT NULL))). Row present = answered; absent = never asked.
- atlas_region (state_province PK, country, atlas_id) replaces the six-way CASE in promote-legacy.sql. Complete for the US and Canada — 64 rows, six carrying an atlas — so 'no row' means unrecognised rather than 'not one of the six'.
- qc_rule_place_unrecognised (warning): fires on a state the lookup cannot find, or a country that contradicts it. Being outside the six is NOT flagged.
- migrations/0010-membership-and-atlas-region.sql, verified with --check both ways.

INGEST
- promote-legacy.sql joins atlas_region and normalises country to ISO alpha-3 (CA->CAN, NZ->NZL). Atlas assignments are unchanged region for region.

APP
- /people: the column is 'Belongs to', not 'Atlas', and reads '—' / an atlas code / 'Program'. The select offers Master Melittology alongside the six, and clearing still means 'not recorded'. The overlay field stays home_atlas and takes 'program'.
- Listings: scope gains 'outside' (atlas_id IS NULL); a separate staff-only 'member' filter asks where the collector belongs, with values atlas code / program / unrecorded. 'unrecorded' is an anti-join over the whole collector list — a sample collected by a WaBA member and someone unasked is not unrecorded.
- /design/identity states the branding answer: with no atlas to act on behalf of, the program acts as itself.
- CONTEXT.md gains a Membership entry; the glossary says an atlas is not something everyone has.

AGAINST THE REAL DEV STORE, after migrating a copy:
- countries: USA 62,410 / CAN 3,882 / NZL 1 / null 1 (BC no longer split 2,321+1,497)
- outside-atlas samples: 632 holding 2,664 specimens, unchanged
- place_unrecognised fires on exactly 3: the two 'country CAN disagrees: UT is in USA', and 'state_province Waikato is not a US state or Canadian province'

NOT DONE, deliberately: no membership rows written for the ~13 program-only candidates. Naming a real person as program-only is a decision about them, and belongs to whoever knows — the model can now record it with a reason line (beeline-fie).

Also fixed in passing: test/promote-legacy.test.ts was failing on main since bcffd87 — the 398 graduated rows name people the fixture does not contain, so every one reported unresolved. It now reads test/fixtures/person-overlay.csv, which exercises both an atlas member and a program-only one.

title: Shared couple accounts: one iNat login, two collectors
description:
Couples sharing one iNat account is a normal pattern in this data, and the promotion rule (ingest/promote-legacy.sql, beeline-eft) handles it badly: it awards the account to whoever files marginally more records under it, silently.

Measured on the dev store, 2026-08-24 — accounts claimed by more than one solo collector, by the winner's share:

  tom_julie       2 people   53%   Tom Robertson 2130 / Julie Biddle 1923
  Lohump          2 people   54%
  pandg           3 people   59%
  Sublettes       2 people   60%
  dto             2 people   62%
  nicolaspackard  2 people   64%

At a 53/47 split 'more records' is a coin flip. Consequences with real auth: the partner who loses gets no inat_account and cannot sign in at all, and if they DO sign in with the shared account they land on their partner's person record and see their partner's samples as their own. inat_account.person_id is a PK and inat_user_id is UNIQUE, so the schema currently insists an account belongs to exactly one person.

This is not new. The reference implementation hardcodes a split for exactly one of these: 'iNat login pandg after 2021 resolves to Gretchen or Robert by sampleId > 100' (docs/reference-implementation.md, Data model). They hit it and patched it by hand for one couple.

Options, none obviously right:
  a) Bind nobody when the split is near-even. Safe and honest, but ~6 active collectors cannot sign in, and they are among the most productive in the dataset (pandg alone carries 20,694 records).
  b) Let one account map to several people and disambiguate at sign-in — 'you are signing in as tom_julie; are you Tom or Julie?' Needs inat_account to stop being 1:1 and the session to carry the choice.
  c) Model the household: the account belongs to a couple, samples stay attributed to the individual collector via sample_collector (which already holds both).

Worth deciding before cutover: it is the difference between a productive volunteer being able to see their own records and not. Relates to beeline-2gw (the 19 bindings a re-promote gains, Tom Robertson among them) and beeline-fvx (individual volunteer tokens).
notes:
MEASURED AGAINST THE LIVE SANDBOX after the beeline-eyk re-promote
(2026-08-24), which changes the numbers this bead was filed with: the
collector fixes merged four duplicate people and stopped one stray recordedBy
collecting 1,675 samples, so some near-even splits moved.

161 people with samples have no account at all — 5,170 samples between them.
17 of those, holding 2,329 samples, have records pointing at an account
somebody ELSE holds:

  Robert Pederson  1087  pandg           held by Gretchen Pederson
  Steve Sheehy      420  smalaby         held by Sarah Malaby
  Julie Biddle      363  tom_julie       held by Tom Robertson
  Emily Carlson     254  amelathopoulos  held by Andony Melathopoulos
  Jane Pope          31  pandg           held by Gretchen Pederson
  + Shaw Steinmetz, Brendan McGarry, Edward Lisowski, Barrett Barrett,
    Juan Benitez, Cort Gardner, Amy Greenwalt

That list is three problems wearing one shape, and only one of them is this
bead:

1. REAL SHARED HOUSEHOLDS — the Pedersons (with Jane Pope also under pandg),
Sheehy/Malaby, Robertson/Biddle. This bead.

2. DUPLICATE PERSON RECORDS — Steinmetz, McGarry, Lisowski, Barrett, Benitez,
Gardner, Greenwalt. One human spelled twice; there is no partner to give an
account to. Every one disappears when data/collector-duplicate-worksheet.csv
becomes alias lines in ingest/collector-aliases.csv (beeline-eyk).

3. RECORDS SOMEBODY ELSE TYPED IN — Emily Carlson's 254 carry amelathopoulos
because Andony entered them. She needs her own account resolved from iNat,
not a share of his. Different fix entirely.

So the population this bead actually has to solve for is about four
households, not seventeen — worth knowing before choosing between (a), (b)
and (c), because (b) and (c) are a lot of machinery for four.

ASKED OF ANDONY (docs/questions.md, new "People and accounts" section): who
Pete is, who Jane Pope is, whether these households would each register an
account — which dissolves this bead with no model change — and whether Emily
Carlson has one. Worth waiting for, since the answer decides whether any of
a/b/c is needed.

DONE MEANWHILE (beeline-eyk): /people no longer renders the partner as a
blank. The row reads "No account — Their records use pandg, which is Gretchen
Pederson's", and the person page names it as a shared login only one person
can hold. That squares the display, not the model.
SHRUNK by beeline-eyk (2026-08-24). Peter's verdicts merged 11 duplicate person records, and seven of them were on this bead's list of 17 people sitting on somebody else's account — Steinmetz, McGarry, Lisowski, Barrett, Benitez, Gardner, Greenwalt. They were never partners locked out of an account; they were one human spelled twice, and they no longer exist as separate people. What remains is the real thing: the Pedersons (plus Jane Pope under pandg), Sheehy/Malaby, Robertson/Biddle — about four households — and Emily Carlson, who needs her own account resolved rather than a share of Andony's. Four households is a different decision from seventeen people, and it is the number to weigh options (a), (b) and (c) against. Still waiting on Andony (docs/questions.md, People and accounts) on whether these households would each register an account, which dissolves this with no model change.
RE-MEASURED 2026-08-25 on a store promoted with current code. The table in the
description is stale: it was measured on 2026-08-24, and the identity fixes
(d25aac7, 2d6b085, f6c0b32, 8ddc141 — beeline-eyk) landed later the same day.
Four of its six contested logins were duplicate person records, not households,
and they are gone.

Accounts more than one person files records under, by the winner's share:

  tom_julie        2   53%  Tom Robertson 2130 / Julie Biddle 1923
  pandg            3   59%  Gretchen Pederson 12138 / Robert Pederson 8482 / Jane Pope 74
  smalaby          2   66%  Sarah Malaby 692 / Steve Sheehy 361
  amelathopoulos   2   95%  Andony Melathopoulos 3019 / Emily Carlson 151
  rogerdormaier    2   96%  Roger Dormaier 551 / Jan Dormaier 20
  beesofcanada     2  100%  Lincoln Best 2091 / Rob Caulfield 1
  schiappad        2  100%  David Schiappa 1699 / Martin Stein 4
  vanjinbo         2  100%  Carol Yamada 3555 / Courtney Neron 2
  molfamily        2  100%  Michael O'Loughlin 14188 / Meghan O'Loughlin 6
  marksg           2  100%  Mark Gorman 7569 / Pam Arion 1

Gone since the merges: Lohump (54%), Sublettes (60%), dto (62%),
nicolaspackard (64%). Those were one human filed twice, and beeline-eyk fixed
them.

This splits the bead into two problems that were previously blurred together:

1. THREE CONTESTED HOUSEHOLDS — tom_julie, pandg, smalaby. Only here is "more
   records" a coin flip, and only here does option (a) (bind nobody) strand an
   active collector. pandg is still the flagship at 20,694 records.

2. SEVEN STRAY-ROW LOGINS at 95-100%. Awarding by record count picks the right
   holder every time, so the account binding is not the problem — but the
   minority person still ends up with no inat_account, and they are not a
   household at all. marksg's Pam Arion is ONE row whose recordedBy names her
   while its own firstName/lastName/userLogin all say Mark Gorman, on a
   consecutive field number in Mark's print batch: a data-entry slip, not a
   collector. amelathopoulos/Emily Carlson is the known "somebody else typed it
   in" case (beeline-gju). These want a different remedy from the households,
   and probably a QC finding rather than a model change.

Also relevant, from the co-collecting question (2026-08-25): the same pair can
swap primaries. sample_collector holds "Michael O'Loughlin + Dan O'Loughlin"
on 312 samples and "Dan O'Loughlin + Michael O'Loughlin" on 23, so
sample.collector_id — position 1, whose sample numbering it is — is not a
stable property of the pair. Whatever oyl does about accounts must not assume
one member of a household is always the primary.
DECIDED 2026-08-25 (Peter). Option (c), in its lightest form.

• inat_account STAYS 1:1 with person. The iNat login is the key. Someone who
  does not want an iNat account does not want a Beeline account either, so the
  model should not contort to give them one.
• Master Melittology progress accrues to the PERSON, not the account. A
  collector with no account still accumulates it and still appears in the
  roster — which the store already supports: 155 of 565 people have no
  inat_account and 145 of them are already the PRIMARY collector on samples.
  An account-less collector is the normal case, not an edge one.
• NEW: an explicit "may act for" link — one person may see and act on another's
  samples. This is option (c) without making inat_account 1:many and without
  pushing a "which of you is this?" choice into every sign-in.
• Options (a) and (b) are rejected. (a) strands Robert Pederson and Julie
  Biddle, who are both still collecting in 2026 (1,087 and 363 samples).

WHY THE LINK IS NEEDED AT ALL — the measurement that forced it. recordedBy
already splits each household's samples correctly across two person records:

  Gretchen Pederson 1146 (holds pandg)   / Robert Pederson 1087 (no account)
  Tom Robertson      421 (holds tom_julie)/ Julie Biddle     363 (no account)
  Sarah Malaby       215 +419 secondary   / Steve Sheehy     420 (no account)

So the near-even award decides only WHO CAN SIGN IN — it does not misattribute
a single sample. That is a much smaller problem than this bead originally
described, and it is what makes keeping 1:1 cheap. But `mine` scope is forced
for volunteers, so the partner holding the account cannot see the other's
samples: 1,087 Pederson samples are invisible to the only person who can log
in, and nobody can act on their QC findings. The link exists to close exactly
that, and nothing more.

OPEN QUESTIONS ON THE LINK, in the order they bite:

1. WHO GRANTS IT. The obvious answer — the person being acted for — cannot sign
   in, which is the whole problem. So staff grant it on request, through
   /people, and it goes to the person overlay like every other staff decision
   about people. Worth stating in the schema comment, because "the subject
   consents" is the answer everyone reaches for first and it does not work
   here.
2. DIRECTIONAL OR SYMMETRIC. Directional. Gretchen acting for Robert does not
   imply the reverse, and a household where only one partner is active should
   not silently become mutual.
3. DOES IT WIDEN `mine`, OR IS IT AN EXPLICIT "ACTING AS" SWITCH. Widening is
   simpler; a switch is more honest about whose work is on screen and keeps
   dashboards and MM progress unambiguous. Leaning switch.
4. IT MUST NOT TOUCH ATTRIBUTION. Progress, labels and recordedBy stay on the
   person who collected. Delegation is visibility and action, never credit.

WHAT IS LEFT AFTER THE LINK:

• Which person holds each shared account is CURATION, not code. Ask the
  household who uses the login; staff rebind on /people; the overlay replays it
  onto every rebuild. No promotion change needed.
• The seven stray-row logins (95-100%) are not households and want a different
  remedy — probably a QC finding, not a model change. See the re-measurement
  note above.
• Individual misattributions are fixed by REASSIGNMENT, which is beeline-v0j
  plus beeline-2c3.20 and not this bead. v0j already argues the same case from
  the iNat side ("who collected this is a fact iNaturalist cannot express") and
  says to do it with 2c3.20 so the primary and the secondaries are decided
  together. Peter's framing on 2026-08-25 agrees: one primary, zero or more
  secondaries, reassignable — including to a collector with no account.
  Constraint for that work, from the co-collecting measurement: the same pair
  can swap primaries (Michael+Dan O'Loughlin on 312 samples, Dan+Michael on
  23), so nothing may assume a stable primary within a household.
  Who may reassign: the sample's current primary, plus staff. Once progress
  ties to a person a reassignment is a credit transfer — giving credit away is
  safe, claiming it is not, so a person should never be able to add themselves
  to a sample they are not already on.
STORE HALF BUILT, 2026-08-25 (dfcc489).

  schema/010_people_atlases.sql  person_delegate (person_id, acts_for_id,
                                 granted_at, granted_by), PK on the pair,
                                 CHECK person_id <> acts_for_id
  migrations/0011-person-delegate.sql   table only, no rows — the grants come
                                 from the overlay like every other decision
                                 about people. Verified against a store built
                                 before the change.
  src/person-overlay.ts          `acts_for` overlay field + splitRefs()
  src/apply-person-overlay.ts    applies it; the resolver is now threaded into
                                 applyField, since this is the first field
                                 whose VALUE names a person
  src/model.ts                   PersonDelegateTable
  test/person-overlay.test.ts    6 tests

The overlay value names the WHOLE set, semicolon-separated
(`name:Robert Pederson;inat:429964`). One row per (person_ref, field) with
latest-wins cannot express "and also", so a second grant would erase the
first; stating the set makes growing and shrinking equally replayable. Blank
revokes everything. A reference naming nobody applies NONE of the set — a
half-applied grant silently drops whoever followed the bad reference.

Verified end to end on real data: granting Gretchen Pederson, who holds pandg,
reach over Robert makes his 1,087 samples visible from the account that can
actually sign in.

STILL OPEN — the app half, which is question 3 above and the branch point for
listings.ts scope parsing, the dashboard, the QC home and CSV export: does a
delegation widen `mine`, or is it an explicit "acting as" switch? Leaning
switch, so `mine` keeps meaning mine and a volunteer can always tell whose
work is on screen — which also gives beeline-o22 an event worth logging.

Nothing yet grants a delegation through the UI; /people/:id needs the
affordance beside the account rebind, and no real grant has been written to
ingest/person-overlay.csv. The three households (pandg, tom_julie, smalaby)
still need someone to ASK who uses each login before any grant is recorded —
that curation is unchanged by this commit.
CORRECTION to the note above: question 3 is NOT open. Peter settled it on
2026-08-25 along with the overlay value format — an explicit "ACTING AS"
SWITCH, not a widening of `mine`.

So, decided:

• `mine` keeps meaning mine. It never silently blends two people's samples.
• A delegate with at least one grant gets a way to say "I am acting for
  Robert", and that state is visible while it is on — in the chrome, not
  buried in a filter.
• Scope stays a question about the SAMPLES (`mine` / an atlas / outside /
  all); acting-as changes WHO "mine" means, and the two compose rather than
  one absorbing the other.
• Because it is an explicit act with a start and an end, it is something
  beeline-o22's audit log can record: "Gretchen acted for Robert" is exactly
  the class of change the overlay cannot currently answer.

Reasoning, for the record: once Master Melittology progress hangs off the
person, a page that quietly merged Gretchen's 1,146 samples with Robert's
1,087 would leave a volunteer unable to tell whose work they were reading,
and `mine` would stop meaning what it says everywhere else in the app.

(The commit message on dfcc489 says this was still open. It stands as written
— history is not rewritten here — and this note is the correction.)
SETTLED AND CLOSED 2026-08-28. Three decisions (Peter), and the measurement
behind each. Numbers re-measured on a store copy migrated to head; the local
store predates the beeline-eyk merges, so the alias file was folded into the
query and none of the four households appear in it.

1. GRANTS RECORDED, all three households plus Jane Pope. Written to
   ingest/person-overlay.csv, author rainhead:

     Gretchen Pederson  acts_for  name:Robert Pederson;name:Jane Pope
     Tom Robertson      acts_for  name:Julie Biddle
     Sarah Malaby       acts_for  name:Steve Sheehy

   What each one actually closes, measured as samples the partner collects
   on which the account holder is not also a collector:

     Gretchen -> Robert     1087 samples,   10 co-collected,  1077 unreachable
     Tom      -> Julie       363 samples,    0 co-collected,   363 unreachable
     Gretchen -> Jane Pope    31 samples,    0 co-collected,    31 unreachable
     Sarah    -> Steve        420 samples,  419 co-collected,     1 unreachable

   smalaby was never really a lockout: Sarah is already a secondary collector
   on 419 of Steve's 420, so `mine` reached them without any grant. Recorded
   anyway — the household is the same shape and one sample is not a reason to
   make it the exception. Jane Pope's grant is the speculative one and carries
   a consequence now noted on docs/questions.md #2: it assumes filing under
   pandg makes her household, and a blank acts_for value withdraws it.

   Verified end to end: `pnpm person:apply` on a migrated copy applied 409 rows
   with one expected miss (name:Cory Gardner, who exists only once the aliases
   are applied at promotion, which that copy predates), and person_delegate
   holds all four rows reaching 1,901 samples.

2. THE STRAY-ROW LOGINS GET NOTHING — no QC rule, no model change. The bead
   speculated a finding; measured, there is nothing to find. Of the people
   whose records carry a login somebody else holds and who are not one of the
   households:

     own iNat account already, never locked out:
       Martin Stein 698 samples, Robert Buschman 444, Jan Dormaier 394
     no account, but already a separate bead:
       Emily Carlson 254 (beeline-gju, records Andony typed in)
     no account, the entire residue:
       Meghan O'Loughlin 3, Courtney Neron 2, Rob Caulfield 1

   Six samples across three people, none collecting since 2023. A rule that
   fires six times on inactive people costs more to read than it saves. The
   95-100% table in the earlier note is what made this look bigger than it is:
   a minority share of a login is not the same as being locked out of one, and
   three of the six largest cases hold their own account.

3. CLOSED. Everything the 2026-08-25 decision called for is built and verified
   (schema, migration 0011, overlay field, apply, /people/:id/delegate, the
   acting-as switch and every mine surface), and the grants are now recorded.
   What remains is not this bead: the ask of each household (docs/questions.md
   #1-3, now about preference rather than access), Emily Carlson (beeline-gju),
   and reassignment (beeline-v0j with beeline-2c3.20).
close_reason: Delegation built and verified; the three household grants plus Jane Pope are recorded in ingest/person-overlay.csv; the stray-row logins measured down to six samples across three inactive people and need nothing.

title: No audit log for changes to people
description:
What exists today is a correction store that happens to name an author, not an audit log.

data/person-overlay.csv records every change made through /people with author (the signed-in iNat login) and reason. It is genuinely useful and was designed deliberately. But it is one CURRENT row per (person_ref, field) — a later edit REPLACES the earlier one — so it answers 'who last changed this, and why' and cannot answer:

  • when it changed
  • what the value was before
  • that it changed twice
  • who changed it the first time

Gaps beyond that:

1. Nothing displays it. It is a CSV on the server's disk; no screen reads it. person_admin.granted_at / granted_by are the only queryable provenance in the store and nothing reads those either.

2. Nothing outside /people is covered. Legacy promotion creates people and binds accounts wholesale with no record but the code that did it — which is exactly the class of change beeline-eft turned out to be, silently binding three people to the wrong iNat account. And ingest/promote-observations.sql rewrites inat_account.login whenever iNat renames an account, with no trace.

3. The overlay is the wrong shape for history by design (ADR 0004: latest-wins, no timestamp arithmetic). Do not bend it into a log — a log wants append-only rows with a timestamp, which is what determination already is ('append-only events: a correction is a newer event, never an edit', schema/040).

Suggested shape: a person_change table in the same append-only spirit — (entity_id, person_id, field, old_value, new_value, author, source, changed_at) — written by the overlay applier and by promotion, with a history section on /people/:id and a recent-changes view on /people. Whether promotion's bulk writes belong in it, or only differences from the previous promotion, is the open question: 580 people x 6 fields on every rebuild would drown the signal.

Note the reference implementation has no audit trail either (docs/reference-implementation.md, 'Users and auth'), so there is nothing to match — only a bar to clear. Worth deciding before cutover, when the store stops being disposable and 'who changed this' stops having 'nobody, we rebuilt it' as an answer.
notes:
Peter, 2026-08-24: is there a more deliberately uniform approach to change
auditing and provenance tracking? Two questions, not one, and worth keeping
apart.

PROVENANCE is a property of a value at rest — which source answered, and by
what authority it holds. Five instances, deliberately different shapes:
sample_location.source (which upstream, and how trusted), elevation_source_id
(which dataset, reproducibly), sample.atlas_assigned_by (geography vs a
person), determination.channel, person_admin.granted_by. Flattening them
would lose what each carries; elevation_source_id is a citation, not an audit
record. The uniformity that pays here is COVERAGE, not shape: every column
whose provenance varies per row should have a sibling saying so, and finding
the ones that do not is beeline-bla's first output. sample.locality is one.

CHANGE AUDITING is a sequence of events. This bead. And the shape is already
settled elsewhere in the project — schema/040: determinations are append-only
events, 'a correction is a newer event, never an edit'. So the uniform
principle to adopt is that one, generalised: authored changes are events.

WHY THERE ARE TWO OVERLAYS, and why that is not the inconsistency it looks
like. corrections.csv carries base_value and does a three-way merge because
it authors over UPSTREAM data that can move underneath it. person-overlay.csv
has no base_value because it authors over DERIVED data, recomputed from
scratch every rebuild, so there is nothing to conflict with. The
upstream/derived/authored vocabulary predicts the difference and says there
should be exactly two. Uniforming them would break the merge semantics ADR
0004 exists for.

TIMING. Both overlays are CSVs specifically because they must survive the
blow-away. That constraint dies at cutover, and the natural home for authored
events is then a table. Designing the general mechanism now means designing
around a constraint that is about to disappear — whereas the catalog
(beeline-bla) is the inventory of what it would have to carry, so it is the
step that usefully precedes this one.
close_reason: Closed

title: Populate person home atlas: 580 unknowns, and how to fill them
description:
person_home_atlas exists (beeline-039) and is empty. Every person on /people reads 'Atlas —'. Nothing schedules filling it, and it is not in docs/roadmap.md.

Not cutover-blocking as things stand: the listings scope picker deliberately does not depend on home atlas (staff scoping is the admin allowlist plus an atlas picker), and sample->atlas assignment is by geography and unaffected. It becomes load-bearing when atlas branding lands on the volunteer dashboard and profile (beeline-2c3.11), because the colorway is chosen by home atlas.

What the dev store says about doing it from geography (2026-08-24, 570 people with samples):

  498  collect in exactly one atlas       unambiguous
   42  top atlas >= 90% of their samples  near-certain
   21  top atlas 70-90%                   probably fine, worth a look
    5  genuinely split                    needs a human
   10  have samples, none carrying an atlas
    4  have no samples at all

So ~95% could be proposed with high confidence and ~26 people need a decision.

The catch is deliberate. schema/010 says atlas_id here is 'set by staff, never inferred from where their samples landed — a Washington volunteer collecting in Oregon is still WaBA', and Michael O'Loughlin is the illustration: 2,499 OBA, 83 WaBA, 3 ID. Geography would call him OBA and be right, but it would call someone else wrong for the same reason, and the column is documented as never guessed.

Suggested shape, which keeps the stance: derive a PROPOSAL, not a value. Show the geographic distribution as a suggestion on the /people detail page (and a bulk 'unset home atlas' filter on the listing), so staff confirm 498 obvious ones with one click each rather than typing 580 from scratch. Every confirmation goes through the overlay as now, so it survives the rebuild and reads as a decision someone made.

Decide before atlas branding starts, not before cutover.
notes:
Source decided (Peter, 2026-08-24): WAIT for an address-derived list. Nothing loaded — no geography-derived rows were written to the sandbox or anywhere else.

Reasoning: the program knows volunteers' registration addresses; Beeline does not, and should not have to. scripts/fetch-legacy.sh pulls only the occurrences collection, and mailing_address is sketched (docs/schema-sketch.md) but deliberately unbuilt, marked private. Deriving atlas from an address OUTSIDE Beeline and loading only the resulting association keeps one low-sensitivity fact per person out of a store that today holds no home addresses at all — importing addresses to compute a six-value enum would be a real ADR 0003 escalation for a small gain. It also avoids writing an inference into a column documented as 'set by staff, never inferred from where their samples landed'.

Geography measured better than expected and is a usable FALLBACK where an address is missing: where both signals exist it agrees with declared iNat project membership 144 of 147 times (98%). The three disagreements look like genuine border cases, not errors — two people in the WaBA project whose samples fall in Oregon, one in the OBA project whose fall in Idaho. Note the project signal itself covers only ~150 people (83 via 18521, 82 via 166376, 62 via 99706, which names no atlas), so it validates geography rather than replacing it.

Worksheet generated for Peter at data/home-atlas-worksheet.csv (584 people from the sandbox, gitignored): display_name, samples, geography_suggests, confidence, home_atlas (blank to fill). Confidence reads 'only atlas' where geography is unambiguous, otherwise the top atlas's share and how many atlases they span.

To load it back: fill home_atlas with an atlas code (OBA, WaBA, BC, ID, NM, OK), leave blank to skip. It goes in through the person overlay keyed name:<display_name> — never entity_id, which differs between dev and sandbox — with author and reason recorded, so it survives the pre-cutover rebuild and reads as a decision someone made.
Graduated into git 2026-08-24 (commit bcffd87): all 398 home-atlas rows moved from the sandbox's data/person-overlay.csv into ingest/person-overlay.csv, and the app-written file reset to a bare header. One home per decision, backed up, and reviewable in a diff — the hand-off ADR 0004 describes. Verified by re-applying afterwards: 398 applied, 0 unresolved, atlas counts unchanged (OBA 211, WaBA 117, BC 39, ID 19, NM 11, OK 1).

Two rows still rest on an unconfirmed assumption and say so in their reason lines: Cara Staab and Heather Datavis [sic: Davis] were assigned OBA because usernames.csv says OR, against geography saying NM on 1 and 3 samples respectively. Megan Asche is the standing proof the assumption is not free — the roster said OR, geography said WaBA, and geography was right.

186 people remain without an atlas. Do not treat that as a backlog to clear: an unknown number of them are Master Melittology members with no member atlas, which is a real state the model cannot express yet (beeline-lcl).
Unblocked for the 186 (Peter, 2026-08-24): person_membership can now say 'Master Melittology, no atlas' as a positive answer, distinct from 'not asked' (beeline-lcl). The overlay field is still home_atlas; its value is an atlas code or 'program'.

What is actually left, from the dev store: 162 of the 182 the overlay did not reach collect entirely inside one atlas and are a roster-match gap, not a membership question — Lincoln Best, 338 samples, is among them. 7 collect both in and out. 10 collect entirely outside the six and are the real program-only candidates: Roy Beckemeyer (67, KS), Coby Klein (15, NY), Kirsten Bovee (12, CA), Sara Dimas (11, AZ), Nikki Zebrowski (9, PA), Georgia Lopez (7, CO), Guillermo Fernandez (3, NY), Brissa Garcia (1, CA), Susan Boersma (1, AK), Peter Best (1, ON). 3 have no samples.

No rows written for any of them: naming a real person as program-only is a decision about them, and the address-derived source this bead is waiting on is the thing that would settle it.
The address-derived list this bead is waiting on is now fetchable.
`pnpm legacy:fetch` lands the legacy usernames register at
`data/legacy/usernames.csv` (gitignored, beeline-8t8), and 551 of its 617 rows
carry a stateProvince — which is exactly what the 398 existing `home_atlas`
rows in ingest/person-overlay.csv were curated from, each citing
"usernames.csv" as its basis.

Read it from the FILE, not from the store: `legacy_username_register` stages
the name columns only and deliberately drops stateProvince along with the rest
of the address, since the mailing-address satellite does not exist yet
(beeline-1kb.6, ADR 0003). Duplicate logins are a hazard — 20 logins repeat and
4 of those name two different people (nflowers2 is Patricia Ellerby and Nancy
Flowers), so dedupe before matching; `legacy_register_ambiguous_login` is the
same exclusion done for names.

title: A combobox island: one typeahead for taxa, people, places
description:
There is no combobox component. Every field that ought to offer choices is a bare text input the user has to guess into, matched server-side by substring:

  /samples, /specimens  taxon, collector, place  (src/app/views/listings.tsx)
  /people               name or login            (src/app/views/roster.tsx)

and determination entry will want one for taxa the moment it lands. beeline-2ae is about how a taxon picker should BEHAVE — typing 'B. californicus' finds B. fervidus and says it is a junior synonym — and presupposes a control that does not exist yet. This bead is the control.

Wanted: one Lit light-DOM island (src/app/islands/, the second real one after menus.ts), backed by a JSON suggest endpoint per entity kind, with the shape the rest of the app already commits to:

• Degrades to the plain text input it replaces. Listings put every filter in the query string so a filtered listing is a shareable URL; the combobox must keep submitting the same parameter with scripting off, matching the 'works without JavaScript' stance the pager and filter bar already take.
• Submits a stable id where one exists, not the display string — the same lesson as beeline-eft, where matching people by login instead of inat_user_id was the whole bug. Free text stays allowed for search; a picked value should carry the entity_id.
• Accessible: it is a combobox, so it needs the listbox roles, aria-activedescendant, and arrow/escape/enter handling. Worth doing once, centrally, rather than three times badly.
• Names render through the existing derivation, never as typed text: TaxonName for italics/subgenus/qualifier by rank, labelName() for people (src/person-name.ts, /design/names).
• A component in src/app/views/components/ plus a section on /design/components, per the library's own rule that a screen needing a treatment gets a component.

Open question for whoever picks it up: whether suggestions come from one generic /suggest?kind= endpoint or one per kind. Volunteer-facing copy goes through the message catalog; the admin screens do too (see /jobs, /people).

title: One human, two person records: recordedBy spelling is the identity key
description:
Found while measuring beeline-b3p, 2026-08-23, against a clean promotion of the real 383k rows.

Person identity is the exact recordedBy string (legacy_person_name is SELECT DISTINCT name), so one human spelled two ways becomes two people — and because sample_collector takes every name on the pair, BOTH land on every one of their samples. The sample then reads as a two-person collecting pair when one person collected it.

Five (fn, ln) pairs in 383k rows carry two recordedBy spellings. Promotion today produces:

  [Mark Gorman, Pam Arion]        1675 samples
  [David Schiappa, Martin Stein]   272 samples
  [Amy GRotta, Amy Grotta]          53 samples
  [Barrett Barrett, Mary Barrett]   17 samples
  [Emma Hoskins, Emily Hoskins]     14 samples

Three of the five are certainly one human listed twice — 84 samples whose listing and label print the same person as a pair. 'Amy GRotta' vs 'Amy Grotta' differs only in case, which is the cheapest possible thing to catch. The other two (1947 samples) are two different humans, but it is unverified whether the second name collected or merely entered the data — worth asking, because 1675 samples is not a rounding error and beeline-2c3.20 (who marks co-collectors) is the place the answer belongs.

Note this is not the same as the five pairs promote-legacy.sql already documents at the legacy_person_map comment. That comment is about which person a pair RESOLVES to; this is about both of them becoming collectors.

Do before cutover: labels are about to stop being cheap to change, and a duplicated collector is visible on one.

Open questions for Peter/Andony: is Emily or Emma the right spelling; is 'Barrett Barrett' a data-entry artifact for Mary Barrett; did Pam Arion and Martin Stein collect, or file? Correcting recordedBy would also need it added to the correctable vocabulary in ingest/promote-legacy.sql (three lists, per its comment) — it is not there today.
notes:
FIXED (2026-08-24), measured on a clean rebuild of the real 383k rows.

Two defects, both shipped:

1. sample_collector was rolled up per (firstName, lastName) pair, so every
name the pair ever recorded landed on every sample the pair ever produced.
It now reads from the rows each sample is made of (legacy_row_collector,
keyed by _id), with the primary unioned in because the sample carries their
numbering by definition. Pam Arion goes from 1,675 samples to 1; Martin
Stein from 272 to 3.

2. Identity was the exact recordedBy string. Folded to letters and digits it
merges four splits, not one: Amy GRotta/Amy Grotta, MaryJo/Mary Jo Mosby,
AC/Ac Quinn, Jackson MacPherson/Macpherson. Display name is the majority
spelling; parts follow it.

580 people -> 576. Co-collector rows 2,935 -> 920. Specimens on joint
samples 36,959 -> 26,085, which lands on the 25,949 joint specimens counted
independently for beeline-2c3.20 — the pair rollup had inflated it 42%.
Samples and specimens unchanged; every genuine pair survives.

The open questions the bead asked are mostly answered by the fix rather than
by a decision: Pam Arion and Martin Stein are named on 1 and 4 rows, so
whether they collected or filed now only affects 4 samples, and both look
like ordinary co-collection at that scale.

STILL OPEN, and the reason this is blocked rather than closed: the
duplicates the fold cannot reach. ingest/collector-aliases.csv is the
mechanism (Peter's call, 2026-08-24, in the shape of determiner-aliases.csv)
and ships empty. The worklist it is curated from is
legacy_collector_duplicate_candidate — person records filing under one
legacy iNat login, minus people who appear together on one row. 19 logins;
ten look like one human spelled twice, and it is a wider set than the five
this bead started from:

  Shawn/Shaw Steinmetz 1092/352 · Juan Manuel Benitez Alvarez/Juan Benitez
  715/81 · Ed/Edward Lisowski 303/106 · Brendon/Brendan McGarry 190/89 ·
  Mary Barrett/Barrett Barrett 195/16 · Corey/Cort Gardner 131/36 ·
  Arndt Arndt/Jeff Arndt 82/2 · Emma/Emily Hoskins 25/21 · Thomas/Tom
  Mitchell 18/18 · Heather Davis/Davis Davis 8/2

Four of those are the surname typed into firstName. Amy Leonard/Amy
Greenwalt (106/97, one login, disjoint 2024 windows) is genuinely unclear.
Peter is reviewing data/collector-duplicate-worksheet.csv (untracked); the
verdicts become alias lines.
DISPLAY-NAME RULE CHANGED (Peter, 2026-08-24): a name changes over time only
in response to corrections, so the spelling used LAST wins, not the one most
rows carry. Frequency was rewarding whichever era someone collected most in,
which is not evidence about their name.

Qualified by the data: the later spelling wins only where it SUCCEEDS the
earlier — first used after the other was last used. 'Amy GRotta' is one row
dated inside a 1,549-row run of 'Amy Grotta', so a plain last-used rule would
let one stray keystroke in a final season rename someone. Interleaved
spellings fall back to frequency.

Three of the four folds are clean successions, none overlapping: MaryJo Mosby
(->2023) then Mary Jo Mosby (2025->); AC Quinn (->2024) then Ac Quinn;
Jackson MacPherson (2024) then Jackson Macpherson. Two display names changed.

Recency is the collection date — the only ordering the dump has, since staged
_ids are content hashes with no timestamp and dateLabelPrint is a batch print
date in mixed formats. fieldNumber (the catalogue sequence) orders all four
groups identically, so the two proxies agree.

The rule also resolves the one worklist candidate that had no answer:
amy2027 is 'Amy Leonard' through 2024-06-05 then 'Amy Greenwalt' from
2024-07-03 — one login, one given name, one season. A name change, not two
people.

Where it needs overruling: 'Ac Quinn' is a form title-casing initials rather
than anyone correcting anything, and for jeffarndt / heather-davis the later
spelling is the surname-typed-into-firstName artifact ('Arndt Arndt', 'Davis
Davis'). ingest/person-overlay.csv (display_name) and the alias CSV are where
those get overridden.
SANDBOX RE-DERIVED (2026-08-24). The fixes are promotion logic, so no
migration carried them: maderas was shaped right and derived wrong, and
db:migrate --check saw nothing because nothing had drifted.

Worse than expected before looking. The sandbox's sample_collector held
exactly one row per sample — 66,314 for 66,314 — because its data predated
collectors becoming a list at all (beeline-77j), while its code did not. So
the store's data was older than its code, which no tool in the repo could
see.

New tool: pnpm db:reseed <old> <new> (src/reseed-store.ts). Builds a fresh
store from schema/*.sql exactly as db:build does, carries across only what
nothing can re-derive — legacy_occurrence plus sync_run/observation_load/
observation_seen and job_run — and draws entity_id_seq forward past the
carried ids (DuckDB has no ALTER SEQUENCE, and a carried id below the fresh
build's seed ids throws as an ADR 0002 identity collision). Procedure in
docs/runbooks/deploy-maderas.md; rehearse on a copy first.

Rehearsed on a copy, then run for real. maderas now: 576 people (was 584),
66,294 samples, 67,214 collector rows of which 920 are co-collectors (was
66,314 / 0), 12,302 linked samples — the number its own last nightly logged.
Sync state intact: 18 runs, 15,261 loads, 20,814 presence rows, so deletion
detection keeps its proof and no re-sweep is needed. Admin roster identical
(the same 6, re-seeded from the checked-in list because person_admin rebuilt
empty and the overlay records no admin decision). AC Quinn, Amy Grotta,
Jackson Macpherson and Mary Jo Mosby are one person each there now.

One difference that is the sandbox catching up, not a regression: 1,019
within_sample_disagreement findings, which a dev rebuild on the same code
produces identically and the old store had none of.

Rollback: ~/dev/beeline/beeline-prev.duckdb on maderas (also a
beeline.duckdb.pre-migrate from the migrate tool). Delete both once this has
been used for a few days.
/people REWORKED (Peter, 2026-08-24). The 'Evidence' column and the 'Only
bindings to check' filter were both unreadable — Peter could not read his own
filter label. The vocabulary was the tell: the screen was built around a
curation task rather than around the people it lists, and that task ends at
cutover while the listing does not.

Now: Person | iNaturalist account | Samples | Belongs to | Admin. A wrong
account says so in the account cell ('probably the wrong account', 'not in
their records'); a right one says nothing, because a column of reassurances is
about our checking rather than about the people. Ordered as a roster (samples,
then name) rather than sorting the doubtful to the front, so the count of them
moved above the table as one sentence with a link. A store with no legacy
staging drops the apparatus entirely — filter included — instead of a banner
explaining absent verdicts, which is also the post-cutover shape.

Gone from anything a person reads: binding, attested, backed, outweighed, no
legacy records. Someone with no account reads 'No account', not an em dash.
The person page keeps the full sentence with its numbers.

Zero flagged accounts in the current sandbox data, so the callout does not
render there; the flagged path is covered by tests instead.
OPEN AND UNFILED (2026-08-24): db:reseed pushes entity_id_seq past the carried sync/observation ids, so the sandbox's person ids jumped from small numbers to 722,366–1,173,080 and /people/722436 is now a normal URL. Legal (ADR 0002: per-store sequence draw, never referenced externally) but ugly, and it ratchets — each reseed adds the previous store's high-water mark to the floor. Compacting it means renumbering the ~36k carried rows into the low range and rewriting sync_run_id in observation_load and observation_seen; then reseeds land in the same id space every time. Offered to Peter, not taken up, not filed as its own bead. Int32 gives room for ~1,900 reseeds, so this is aesthetics and tidiness, not a deadline.
RESOLVED, and it was avoidable (2026-08-24). Peter: 'does reseed not create a new database?' It does — which is exactly why carrying the sync/observation ids verbatim was never required. entity_id_seq starts at 1 in the new store and every person, sample and specimen is renumbered anyway; ADR 0002 already says an entity_id is a per-store draw, which is why the overlay refuses to key on one. Only the association between a sync run and the rows pointing at it has to survive — 18 rows to remap. db:reseed now renumbers everything it carries: sync_run ids 722,366+ become 7–24, and a full re-promote spans 15,339–466,053 instead of starting where the old store ended. Reseeding the result again lands in the same range, pinned by test. Supersedes the earlier note offering this as unfiled work. NOT yet applied to the sandbox, which still carries the ratcheted ids from the first reseed — re-running db:reseed there would compact them, at the cost of changing every person URL again.
DECIDED (Peter, 2026-08-24): no further reseed of the sandbox until there is a more substantive reason than compacting ids. The renumbering fix stands in the tool and applies to the next reseed whenever one is warranted; the sandbox keeps its 722k-1.17M ids meanwhile, which matters less now that /people is addressed by login (48221f4). Do not re-propose this on its own.
CLOSED (2026-08-24). Peter returned all 19 verdicts; ingest/collector-aliases.csv now carries 12 lines merging 11 people, and the 8 marked separate are exactly the 8 the detector still lists. 576 people -> 565, specimens unchanged, one sample merged. He overruled my reading four times: Shawn not Shaw, Brendan not Brendon, Emma for the interleaved Hoskins pair, and Cory Gardner per her iNat profile — a spelling in no record, which the alias CSV can name because it maps spellings to a person rather than picking between them. She needed an overlay line for given_name, the AC Quinn shape. Filling the CSV exposed a silent bug: legacy_person_name keyed only on canonical spellings, orphaning four overlay rows that named an aliased-away spelling; it now holds every spelling, one row per name, pinned by test.
CORRECTION (Peter, 2026-08-24): most of the eleven rulings came from looking up iNaturalist profiles; Emma Hoskins was arbitrary. My merge commit called every overrule 'a fact no rule could have reached', which is true of ten and not of that one. ingest/collector-aliases.csv now carries a third column, basis — 'iNat profile' for the checked ones, 'arbitrary — ask her' for Hoskins — because an unchecked conclusion and a verified one are indistinguishable in alias,person, and that indistinguishability is exactly how beeline-eft's wrong binding survived review. Emma will print on labels and reach Ecdysis and GBIF looking as settled as the rest. Added to docs/questions.md (People and accounts, Q4) so it is asked rather than quietly decided on her behalf; one line reverses it.
SANDBOX RE-PROMOTED (2026-08-25) with the alias merges. 576 people -> 565, samples 66,294 -> 66,293, specimens unchanged at 380,279, collector rows 67,214 -> 67,201. 401 overlay decisions applied, none unresolved — the four that the orphaning bug would have lost are back. Shared-login worklist 19 logins -> 8. Sync state intact: 21 runs, 15,351 loads, 20,914 presence rows, so no re-sweep. Admin roster unchanged (same six, re-seeded from the checked-in list). First run of the renumbering reseed on real data: entity_id_seq started at 15,454 instead of 722k, and person ids now span 15,454-466,156 instead of 722,368-1,173,082. Rollback is ~/dev/beeline/beeline-prev.duckdb (the pre-merge store); beeline.duckdb.pre-migrate from 2026-08-24 is also still there and can go.
close_reason: Fixed and verified: per-sample collectors, folded identity, the alias mechanism, and Peter's 19 verdicts applied. 565 people; the shared-login worklist is down to the 8 genuinely separate ones.

title: Ask Andony: may one atlas's staff see another atlas's true coordinates?
description: The last open piece of the in-app half of the taxon-geoprivacy question (docs/questions.md). Settled 2026-08-23: a collector sees their own true coordinates, and their own atlas's staff see them, in the app and in its CSV exports — that is a participant reading their own records, not revelation. What is not settled: Beeline's staff surface is a global allowlist with an all-atlases scope (beeline-2c3.21, no per-atlas staff role exists), so a WaBA staff member can currently read OBA's true coordinates for taxon-obscured records. Ask whether that is acceptable across the six atlases or whether the cross-atlas scope must exclude obscured coordinates — and if the latter, it needs the per-atlas staff role that beeline-2c3.21 deferred. Implementation proceeds meanwhile (Peter's call). Unrelated to the downstream question, which stays open: labels, Ecdysis, GBIF.

title: Listing refinements from Peter's first look
description: Four things from using /samples and /specimens against real data (Peter, 2026-08-23): (1) samples read in iNaturalist upload order within a day — should be the collector's own numbering, descending, because a day's samples reach iNat in whatever order they were photographed; (2) specimens can be filtered to a taxon but not to 'not determined', which is the gap staff actually chase; (3) staff need a collector filter on both listings; (4) wide tables should be full-bleed rather than held to the prose measure.
acceptance_criteria: Sample rows order by date desc then sample number desc (12 above 9, not lexical); a Determination filter offers determined/not determined on both listings; a Collector filter appears for staff only and matches anyone on the sample; a listing table spans the window while prose keeps its measure.
close_reason: Shipped together: settled seasons (season/settled_sample views, dashboard scoping with a visible count and link), sample-number ordering, determination and collector filters, qc=flagged, full-bleed tables.

title: Seasons settle on 1 March: old samples stop asking on the dashboard
description: Peter, 2026-08-23, looking at his own QC home: the one flag he has is on a 2024 sample. From 1 March each year the previous season's samples are settled — not immutable, still fixable, but no longer worth the dashboard asking about. Store-wide today that is 6,651 flagged samples before 2026-03-01 against 211 in the current season, so an unscoped dashboard is mostly archaeology. Settled is a dashboard-attention rule only: flags are still derived, still block printing, and settled samples are still browsable and fixable. The dashboard says how many settled samples still carry flags and links to them, so nothing disappears silently.
design: A settled_sample view over a season view (1 March of this year, or last year until this year's 1 March arrives), so the rule lives in SQL with the other QC rules rather than in app code. Trap samples are judged on date_end, so a trap that ran across 1 March stays in the season. The listings gain a qc=flagged filter (blocking or warning) for the dashboard's link to point at.
acceptance_criteria: A flagged sample from a previous season does not appear in the dashboard's attention list; the dashboard says how many such samples exist and links to them; printability and the flags themselves are unchanged.
close_reason: Shipped together: settled seasons (season/settled_sample views, dashboard scoping with a visible count and link), sample-number ordering, determination and collector filters, qc=flagged, full-bleed tables.

title: qc_finding costs ~0.7s per read on a full store — consider materializing it
description: Measured 2026-08-23 on the rebuilt 66k-sample, 380k-specimen store, after beeline-2c3.22 took the QC home from 10s to ~1.2s. What is left is the union of eleven rule views: a bare count over qc_finding is 0.68s, blocking_sample 1.0s, printable_sample 1.3s. The QC home reads the finding set twice (its own list, and pending_print_sample through printability), so the flagship page sits at 1.2-1.6s against a one-second interactive budget; /samples and /specimens pay one read each. Per-person filtering does not help — the rule views each scan the whole sample table and the planner cannot push the collector join into the union. Options: materialize findings into a table refreshed after promote/sync (keeps the rules as SQL views, adds a refresh step and a staleness question — findings would no longer be true the instant an in-app edit lands), narrow the expensive rule views, or accept the second. Worth deciding before volunteers arrive, not before.
acceptance_criteria: Either the flagship page is inside the interactive budget on a full store, or the budget is explicitly re-set for page reads with the reasoning recorded.
close_reason: Resolved by beeline-2c3.36/37: storing observation_field and the regex locality rule took the qc_finding union from ~670 ms to ~25 ms, inside the interactive budget.

title: Rename specimen.catalog_number to field_number
description: Vocabulary decided 2026-08-23 (beeline-nfo): the number Beeline mints and prints on a label is the FIELD number; 'catalog number' is the museum's identifier, arriving from Ecdysis with its institutional prefix (WSDA_2303966). CONTEXT.md, the volunteer glossary, and the sample/specimen listings now say field number; the store still says specimen.catalog_number, and the sketch's minted_catalog_number is the same misnomer. Rename with the printing phase, when the minting code is written: specimen.catalog_number -> field_number (schema/030, model.ts, ingest/promote-legacy.sql, src/app/listings.ts, migrations/NNNN for the sandbox), and reserve catalog_number for the museum identifier that Ecdysis import will bring back. Doing it now would touch ingestion mid-rebuild for no behavioural gain; doing it after the printing code is written means renaming more.
acceptance_criteria: No column, view, or type in the store calls Beeline's printed number a catalog number; a specimen can carry both a field number and, later, a museum catalog number without the two sharing a name.
close_reason:
Done. specimen.catalog_number -> field_number across schema/030, model.ts, ingest/promote-legacy.sql, both listings, the specimen view, and the tests; docs/schema-sketch.md's minted_catalog_number -> minted_field_number; CONTEXT.md's 'the store still spells it catalog_number' sentence retired; README, roadmap, questions P6/P7, and ADRs 0001/0002/0006 corrected where they called Beeline's number a catalog number (identifier only in the ADRs, never the reasoning). load-legacy.ts's 'catalogNumber' and the fixtures keep the name — that is the legacy Mongo key, and it really is the museum's number.

Migration 0007 is a table rebuild, not a rename: DuckDB 1.5.5 refuses ALTER TABLE ... RENAME COLUMN and DROP COLUMN on any table involved in a foreign key, whether or not the column participates, and specimen sits between sample and determination. ADD COLUMN is allowed, which does not help. So specimen and determination are copied out, dropped, recreated verbatim from schema, and copied back with entity_ids preserved, with determination_of_record and the printability chain rebuilt around them. Re-test the simple rename when DuckDB moves past 1.5.x (beeline-c1b).

Ingestion was the stated reason to defer, so it was re-run whole rather than trusted: db:build + legacy:load + legacy:promote over the real 383k rows returns counts identical to the pre-rename run, and all four identifier eras land.

title: Sentry integration, including the user feedback widget
description: Pre-cutover requirement (Peter, 2026-08-23). beeline-8w6 names Sentry in its plan but nothing is wired up, and it does not cover user feedback at all. Needs: SDK in the app process (@sentry/node around the Hono handler and the job scheduler, so a failed job or unhandled exception alerts a human rather than leaving a null completed_at), environment and release tagging so sandbox noise is separable from production, and the User Feedback widget on volunteer-facing pages so a volunteer who hits something wrong can say what they were doing — the reference implementation had no such channel and staff heard about problems by email. Scrub before send: no coordinates, no session cookie, no OAuth token, and person identity only as far as the iNat login (ADR 0003 keeps private data out of the main store; it must not leak into an error report either). DSN comes from the environment like every other secret (~/.config/beeline/env on maderas), and the app must run fine without one.
acceptance_criteria: An unhandled exception and a failed job both reach Sentry with environment and release tags; a volunteer can submit feedback from a normal page; no coordinate, token, or cookie appears in any captured event; the app boots and serves with SENTRY_DSN unset.
notes: Wanted before December 2026 cutover, when the blow-away era ends and a silent failure starts costing real data.
close_reason: Shipped in #103: errors, logs and job check-ins reach Sentry with environment and release tags, scrubbed of coordinates, tokens, cookies and all identity beyond the iNat login; the app runs unchanged with SENTRY_DSN unset. Uptime monitor on /healthz created in Sentry. The feedback widget stays out: it needs a paid plan, and the header's email link covers volunteer feedback (see the 2026-09-21 comment). Tracing and application metrics are a follow-up.

title: Call them flags, not findings — MM has said flags for years
description:
Peter: the reference site calls these flags, and that is how Master Melittology has communicated about them for years. Volunteers already have a word for this; we invented a second one.

The rename appears deliberate — the glossary entry argues 'a finding is not a mark against you, it is a to-do' — but that reframing costs every volunteer the mapping from what they have been told for years to what the screen says. The reference implementation's own surface is flags: errorFlags, /api/flags (docs/reference-implementation.md:34,43,66).

Decide, then apply consistently. Volunteer-facing copy is the cheap part (src/app/messages/en.ts). The schema also says finding throughout — qc_finding, sample_promotion_finding, the 120_views_qc_rules views — so a full rename reaches the store; keeping the internal name and changing only the copy is a legitimate middle. Related: beeline-0i2.
close_reason: Glossary revision pass applied: alphabetical, examples rendered through TaxonName, sample/observation/floral-host cover the no-host case, label and sync copy fixed, findings renamed to flags in volunteer copy (schema keeps qc_finding), field number vs catalog number settled in the glossary and CONTEXT.md (column rename filed as beeline-1kb.11).

title: Catalog number vs field number: the glossary conflates two identifiers
description:
Peter's question on the glossary entry: 'is that true? Doesn't the catalog number include the WSDA_ prefix, or is that a different concept?'

It looks like a different concept. From docs/reference-implementation.md:
- :17 — the identifier printed on the label is fieldNumber (2-digit year + zero-padded sequence, 25000001), assigned only to flag-free records.
- :18 — catalogNumber in their schema means the MUSEUM's identifier, read from Ecdysis determination exports by stripping WSDA_.

So the number Beeline mints and prints is a field number; the catalog number arrives later from the museum and carries the institutional prefix. Our schema stores specimen.catalog_number as 'opaque verbatim text: all four historical identifier eras land here' with minted_catalog_number 'returning with the printing phase' (schema/030_samples_specimens.sql:94-100) — which is already the printed-identifier sense, under the museum's name.

Decide the vocabulary before the printing phase writes it into the UI, then fix the glossary entry (currently: 'The unique number printed on a specimen's label'), CONTEXT.md, and the column names if they should change. Related: beeline-0i2.

title: Glossary: nomenclature entries print their examples upright
description:
The scientific-name entry reads 'The formal Latin name of an organism, like Bombus vosnesenskii. Genus names and everything below them are written in italics' — with Bombus vosnesenskii sitting right there in roman type, contradicting the sentence it illustrates.

Same problem in subgenus (Bombus (Psithyrus) insularis), cf-aff (Bombus cf. occidentalis), sp. (Bombus sp.), and authorship. Definitions are plain strings in the catalog, so they cannot carry markup by design.

The fix is presumably an example field rendered through TaxonName (src/app/views/components/taxon.tsx) — which already knows italics, bracket, and qualifier placement from rank — rather than markup in the copy. A glossary that sets its own examples wrong is teaching the opposite of what it says.

The nightly pipeline in src/app/jobs/ stays as it is; this is about not writing a promise into the catalog that the schedule will outgrow.

title: Glossary: Observation and Sample don't cover the no-floral-host case
description:
Both entries assume there is a plant. Some samples have no floral host: bees taken off no flower are documented by a blank/subjectless iNaturalist observation — no photo, no identification — which exists only to carry the sample number and specimen count.

CONTEXT.md:12 already records this ('a blank/subjectless observation for bees collected off no flower') and the sample table comment says 'one floral host (or none)'. The glossary is the only place that doesn't admit it — and a volunteer with a blank observation is exactly the person looking the word up.

title: Pre-cutover: Content Security Policy on every response
description:
No CSP header is set anywhere today (no hono/secure-headers, no manual header). Before cutover the app should send a restrictive Content-Security-Policy — plus the usual companions (X-Content-Type-Options, Referrer-Policy, frame-ancestors 'none') — from one place in src/app/server.tsx so every route is covered by construction, the way session-gating already is.

What the policy has to accommodate, as the app stands now:
- script-src: one module bundle, the Vite-built islands, served same-origin (src/app/views/layout.tsx:93). No inline script, no inline handlers — so 'self' should suffice with no unsafe-inline.
- style-src: same-origin stylesheets, but inline style= attributes exist on /design pages (design/space.tsx, type.tsx, color.tsx, identity.tsx, names.tsx). Either drop those attributes into real classes or allow style-src-attr 'unsafe-inline' — decide rather than blanket-allowing unsafe-inline for stylesheets.
- img-src: 'self' plus static.inaturalist.org (the account-menu avatar, layout.tsx:116) — pin the actual avatar host(s) rather than https:.
- connect-src/form-action/frame-ancestors/base-uri/object-src: lock down; the app makes no browser-side cross-origin requests, and OAuth redirects are top-level navigations (not form-action) — verify before choosing.

Worth checking at the same time whether report-only should run on the sandbox first to catch violations before enforcing.
acceptance_criteria: A CSP (and companion security headers) is applied centrally in src/app/server.tsx to every response; a test asserts the header is present on a representative page; /design and the account-menu avatar still render without console CSP violations; the inline-style decision is recorded (either refactored away or explicitly allowed via style-src-attr).
notes:
Named pre-cutover, matching beeline-27c. Not urgent while the sandbox is the only deployment, but must land before real volunteer traffic.

Delivery: an HTTP response header set by the app, not a <meta http-equiv> tag in the HTML — the meta form can't carry frame-ancestors or report-to, applies only to pages (not the CSV downloads, /tokens.css, or the islands bundle), and takes effect only after the parser reaches it.
close_reason: Fixed in #122

title: Printings listing for an atlas's collectors
description: Staff want to see all printings for their atlas's collectors, alongside the sample and specimen listings (Peter, 2026-08-23). Deferred out of the listing work because printing has no model yet: print_run/printed_label are sketched (docs/schema-sketch.md) and wait on the Arthur/Andony walkthrough (beeline-1kb.1). Today the only proof of printing is that a specimen row exists, with its verbatim catalog_number — a printings page over that proxy would say nothing the specimen listing doesn't. Build it when print runs exist: one row per run, scoped by atlas the same way the sample/specimen listings are.

title: Listing pages: samples and specimens, with mine / atlas / all-atlases scopes
description: Volunteers can only see samples that need attention (the QC home). There is no way to browse everything you collected, and staff helping someone have no way to look at an atlas's data at all. Two paged listings — /samples and /specimens — with filters (date range, place, taxon, QC status), free-text search (sample number, collector, catalog number), and CSV export of the current view. Scope is a query parameter: mine (default, and the only option for a volunteer), a single atlas, or all atlases; staff = the existing admin allowlist (config.adminLogins), because no per-atlas staff role exists yet and a picker defers that model (Peter, 2026-08-23). CSV omits coordinates — believed-true coordinates should not leave the app one click from a listing.
design: Scope via ?scope=mine|all|<atlas code>, remembered in a cookie so nav links land where staff left off; forced to mine for non-admins. Filters live in the query string so a filtered view is a shareable URL. Taxon filter matches the determination of record's animal and any descendant (recursive CTE over animal.parent_id), so 'Bombus' and 'Apidae' both work. QC status reads qc_finding severities at sample level, for specimens too.
acceptance_criteria: A volunteer sees only their own samples/specimens and no scope control; an admin can scope to one atlas or all; filters and search compose; CSV returns the same rows as the page without paging and without coordinates; every string comes from the message catalog.
close_reason: Shipped: /samples and /specimens with mine/atlas/all scopes, filters, search, paging, CSV. Printings deferred to beeline-1kb.10.

title: Fetch the legacy usernames register (curated name parts, initials, addresses)
description: OBP-Server keeps a hand-curated per-person register at shared/data/usernames.csv (UsernamesService), keyed by userLogin: fullName, firstName, firstNameInitial, lastName, email, address, city, stateProvince, zipPostal, country. The checked-in copy is a header only — the real file lives on the production server, because it holds emails and mailing addresses. This is the authoritative source for three things we are otherwise guessing at: person.given_name/family_name (curated, not split), person.label_name (firstNameInitial IS the stored label override — the legacy system chose the same model Peter did), and mailing addresses for beeline-1kb.6.
design: Fetch alongside the occurrence dump (scripts/fetch-legacy.sh, production access is 'beeline' in ~/.ssh/config). Names and initials belong in the main store on person; email/address are private and belong in the private store (ADR 0003) or at minimum outside git — data/legacy/ is gitignored, but the loader must not promote addresses into beeline.duckdb. Note the register is keyed by userLogin, so it only covers people with iNat accounts; the trap-only collectors (most co-collectors) will not be in it.
notes:
Done, with one premise of this bead reversed by the data.

FETCHED. scripts/fetch-legacy.sh now pulls shared/data/usernames.csv alongside
the occurrence dump. The file is not UTF-8 — it carries three stray no-break
spaces of mixed provenance (0xA0, Windows-1252, twice; 0xCA, Mac Roman, once),
all inside address fields, from years of hand-editing in Excel on both
platforms. DuckDB rejects the raw file outright (encoding='latin-1' fails too),
so the fetch normalises those two bytes to a plain space and FAILS on any other
undecodable byte rather than guessing — the next one could land in a name.
Verified both paths: a crafted 'José' row exits 1 and writes nothing.

STAGED. ingest/promote-register.sql builds legacy_username_register from the
name columns only. email, address, city, stateProvince, zipPostal and country
are deliberately not staged: the mailing-address satellite does not exist yet
(beeline-1kb.6, ADR 0003), so those stay in the gitignored file. beeline-fie's
address-derived home-atlas list should read that file directly for the same
reason. The register is optional — promotion without one reads as empty rather
than fatal, so a clone with the occurrence dump and no register still works.

THE PREMISE THAT DID NOT SURVIVE. This bead called the register 'the
authoritative source' for given_name/family_name/label_name. Measured against
the real store it is a second opinion, not an authority:

  - It fills NO missing name part. All 15 people with NULL parts have no iNat
    login, so the register — keyed by login — cannot reach any of them. It is
    exactly the trap-only-collector gap this bead predicted, and it turns out
    to be the whole of the gap.
  - Of the 414 people it does reach it disagrees about 25, and adopting it
    wholesale would fix about four names and break at least one: tom_julie is
    a shared household login, and its register row would rename Tom Robertson
    to Julie Biddle (beeline-oyl).
  - firstNameInitial is NOT the rich label override this bead hoped for: 411
    of 414 are the mechanical first letter. Exactly one is a real override
    (Juan Manuel Benitez Alvarez -> 'J.M.'); the other two are register rows
    whose firstName column holds the surname.
  - The register has the one-login-two-people problem itself: 20 duplicate
    logins, 4 of which disagree about the name (nflowers2 is Patricia Ellerby
    and Nancy Flowers). Those are excluded from comparison, never picked
    between.

So it lands the way every other name decision in this project lands: as a
worklist. legacy_register_name_conflict reports 45 rows over 25 people, one
row per (person, field), and a human graduates verdicts into
ingest/person-overlay.csv. Nothing writes to person. The curation itself is
beeline-d09.

Also: 203 register logins match nobody in the store — people who registered
but never collected, or whose login has since changed. Not chased.

title: Who marks co-collectors, and how
description: The model now holds co-collectors (sample_collector, beeline-77j) and legacy promotion fills it from recordedBy. Nothing yet lets anyone mark a co-collector on a sample that did not come from the legacy import, so post-cutover the information stops arriving.
design: Evidence (383k-row dump): (1) PER SAMPLE, NOT PER PERSON — everyone in a pair also collects alone, often more: Michael O'Loughlin 14,818 solo specimens vs ~22,864 joint, Dan 12,286 solo, Judith Maxwell 11,224 solo. A person-level 'collects with X' default would silently mis-attribute thousands of samples. (2) It is overwhelmingly a TRAP practice: 22,066 of the 25,949 joint specimens have trap-style sample ids, which is two thirds of ALL trap specimens; joint net specimens are 1.1% of net. So the marking moment is trap sample entry — the interface deferred past cutover (docs/roadmap.md). Proposal: the collector marks it on the sample, in-app. /samples/:id/edit already exists, is collector-gated, and covers exactly the non-iNat (trap/manual) population where 85% of this lives — add a co-collector picker there. For the 377 iNat-backed joint specimens the fact has no home upstream (iNat has one observer), so co-collectors would be the first field editable in-app on an iNat-backed sample: the principle being that in-app editing is for facts iNaturalist cannot express, not for facts it owns.
notes:
ANSWERED by Peter 2026-08-23: (a) roster privacy is a non-issue — the full active membership (name, affiliations) is available to every active member of any atlas, so a person picker over active members is fine. (b) durability: pre-cutover only, and smaller than first stated — see below. (c) label text: inferred from the legacy code, recorded on beeline-1kb.1.

DURABILITY, restated: nothing is at risk in the model, only in the sandbox. sample_collector lives in beeline.duckdb, which is rebuilt from Mongo until cutover, so a co-collector a volunteer marks in the app today vanishes at the next rebuild — the same reason corrections live in data/corrections.csv outside the blow-away path (ADR 0004). Post-cutover there is no rebuild and the question disappears. AND there is a neat path for the legacy-backed case: promotion now reads collectors from the staging recordedBy column, so adding recordedBy to EDITABLE_FIELDS makes a co-collector edit an ordinary correction event, anchored on the staging _id like every other one, re-applying on every rebuild. That covers every sample that exists today. Only a sample with no staging row (an iNat-created sample, which nothing creates yet) has nothing to anchor to.

FOR ANDONY (Peter is asking, week of 2026-08-24) — collaboration:
1. Is collecting as a pair a thing the program wants to support first-class, or a workaround for one household sharing one iNat account? The data says both exist: 11 stable groups, ~26k specimens, 2019-2025 — but also OccurrenceService.js hard-codes the shared login 'pandg' to split Pederson samples by sampleId > 100.
2. Does a co-collector get equal standing — their name on the label, on the record, in exports (Darwin Core recordedBy already lists them) — or is one person the collector of record and the other a credit?
3. Who says so: the collector when entering a trap sample, or staff? Everything joint in the data is trap or manual entry; iNat cannot express it at all, so for the 377 iNat-backed joint specimens someone has to say it in Beeline.
4. Can a pair be standing ("we always run this trap line together") or is it per sample? Every one of these people also collects alone, often more than jointly, so Beeline models it per sample — but a standing pair could be an entry-time default.

Open: what a label prints for two collectors (beeline-1kb.1, options recorded there).

title: Person names: label form needs more than display_name
description: Labels print the collector as e.g. 'P. Abrahamsen', which display_name cannot yield reliably. Legacy Mongo carries firstName/lastName separately, but ingest/promote-legacy.sql collapses them to display_name = concat_ws(' ', fn, ln) and drops the parts (recoverable — promotion re-runs from Mongo — but absent from the model today). Mongo's own recordedBy is the FULL form ('Andony Melathopoulos'), so the abbreviated label form was rendered at print time by the legacy system, never stored.
design: Evidence from the 383,032-row dump (582 distinct first/last pairs): 11 multi-word surnames, including particles that must ride with the family name — Van Otterloo, Vanden Heuvel, Benitez Alvarez, Hirst Johns; one middle initial stranded in lastName (Karen / 'G. Barron'); 8 hyphenated surnames (Marks-Fife, Red-Laird, Shinnick-Gordon), which abbreviate fine; a few joint entries that are really co-collectors crammed into one field — 'Maggie | Henry' / 'Graham | Whitridge', 'Jan/Walt' / 'Ochsner/ Stahlnecker', and a four-person one; no non-ASCII yet, but the schema should not assume it. Separately, determination.identifiedBy is already initials-style and inconsistent verbatim text: L.R.Best, 'A.S. Jackson', 'AS Jackson', 'Caleb A. Lankford', 'Karen W. Wright'. Options for the collector's printed form: (A) structured given/family on person, label form derived like TaxonName derives from rank; (B) A plus an optional stored override for what derivation gets wrong or a person prefers; (C) store the label form only. Leaning B. Label content itself is gated on the printing walkthrough (beeline-1kb.1, P1-P7) and rendering on beeline-1kb.4, but the name parts are cheap to capture now and the roster/admin screens want them anyway.
notes: RESOLVED 2026-08-23 in 03bded4: sample_collector shipped, promotion keys people on recordedBy members, dashboard and sample editor read the list, shared samples say 'collected with X'. The remaining question — who marks co-collectors on new samples — is beeline-2c3.20.
