title: Migration tool + deploy script for the sandbox
description: Deploying beeline-2c3.18 needed a hand-written one-off script to add a view to the sandbox store: the blow-away stance covers fresh builds but says nothing about a deployed database that must catch up, and 'no migration system' left that gap to be filled by hand every time (with a CHECKPOINT rule, beeline-vyi, that is easy to forget). Peter asked for a basic migration tool with a record of applied migrations, and a deploy script that calls it.
design: schema/*.sql stays the source of truth for fresh builds; migrations/NNNN-slug.sql are deltas that bring an existing store forward, recorded in a schema_migration ledger. db:build stamps every migration as applied (a fresh build is current by construction), so only deployed stores ever run them. Each migration in its own transaction, CHECKPOINT at the end per the DuckDB WAL rule. --baseline stamps without running (for a store that already carries the change, e.g. the sandbox after the hand-applied view). --check diffs the store's tables/views/columns against a fresh in-memory schema build, so a forgotten migration is visible. scripts/deploy-maderas.sh: pull, install, build, stop, migrate, start, wait on healthz — the stop is required because one process owns the store (ADR 0005).
close_reason: Shipped and used for a real deploy: migrations/ + schema_migration ledger + db:migrate (--status/--check/--baseline), scripts/deploy-maderas.sh, ADR 0006

title: Decide the snapshot boundary for trusted coordinates in observation_load
description: ADR 0003 claims the main file is safe to copy, but trusted syncs store private_geojson (true coordinates of obscured observations) in observation_load.content in the main database. Decide before handing snapshots around: redact load content on export, move load content (or a private projection of it) into the private store, or explicitly accept trusted coordinates as main-store data and revise the ADR's copy-freely claim. Surfaced by the 2026-08-22 full-history review; ADR 0003 now carries the caveat.
close_reason:
Decided (Peter, 2026-08-23): true coordinates are ordinary main-store data. No redaction on load, no private projection of observation_load.

The two stores protect different SUBJECTS. The private store protects participants — tokens, mailing addresses, email — data that exposes a person who did not sign up for it. A taxon-obscured coordinate protects a plant population from collectors, which is a real duty but not participant privacy and does not want the same mechanism. Everyone with access to the main db is trusted to also protect the plants.

Two consequences recorded in ADR 0003: collector locations were never private anyway (collecting for the program implies willingness to say where), so the only secrecy interest in a coordinate is the taxon-driven one; and the control moves from the file to the recipient — 'safe to copy by construction' becomes 'safe to copy to someone trusted', which makes the ADR's own casual example (handing a snapshot to a student) the case that stops being casual. That path wants a derived export with redaction (roadmap phase 7), not a file copy.

Says nothing about REVELATION: whether an atlas may show taxon-obscured coordinates on a label, in the app, or in an export stays per-atlas, open, and a go-live blocker (docs/questions.md).

title: DuckDB: WAL replay of ALTER on sequence-default table fails with INTERNAL error — repro + upstream report
description: Observed 2026-08-22 on the sandbox (DuckDB 1.5.5, @duckdb/node-api 1.5.5-r.4): ALTER TABLE sync_run ADD COLUMN ... committed to the WAL (process exited before checkpoint after a later statement threw), and reopening the database failed WAL replay with 'INTERNAL Error: Calling DatabaseManager::GetDefaultDatabase with no default database set' — stack shows ReplayAlter → BindCreateTableInfo → BindDefaultValues, i.e. re-binding the table's nextval('entity_id_seq') default without database context. Consequence: the file is unopenable until the WAL is deleted; if the WAL also held committed DML, that would be data loss — serious for post-cutover durability (every entity table carries a sequence default). To do: (1) minimal repro (create table with nextval default, ALTER ADD COLUMN, kill before checkpoint, reopen); (2) check duckdb/duckdb for an existing issue, report if new; (3) until fixed, the operational rule stands: explicit CHECKPOINT after any DDL (runbook updated); (4) re-test on DuckDB upgrades.
notes:
Investigated 2026-08-22. (1) Minimal repro, pure CLI, 3 commands:
  duckdb r.db -c "CREATE SEQUENCE seq; CREATE TABLE t (id BIGINT DEFAULT nextval('seq'), name TEXT); INSERT INTO t (name) VALUES ('a');"
  duckdb r.db -c "PRAGMA disable_checkpoint_on_shutdown; ALTER TABLE t ADD COLUMN extra TEXT;"
  duckdb r.db -c "SELECT * FROM t;"   # INTERNAL Error: ...GetDefaultDatabase with no default database set
Reproduces on v1.5.5 CLI and @duckdb/node-api 1.5.5-r.4 (also without the pragma, via exit-without-close).
(2) Known upstream — no new report needed. Canonical open issue: duckdb/duckdb#18259 (since 1.3.x, 'under review'). Exact variant duckdb/duckdb#21490 closed by PR #21516 (merged to main 2026-03-20): moves default_database assignment earlier in DatabaseManager::AttachDatabase so WAL-replay binding can qualify function/sequence lookups. Fix is NOT in any release (v1.5.5, 2026-07-22, diverged from it). Verified our exact nextval repro passes on nightly 1.6.0.dev365. Open siblings: #19712, #20543, #22044 (DROP INDEX variant — separate replay path, unverified).
(3) Runbook rule (explicit CHECKPOINT after one-off DDL) stands until upgrade past 1.5.x — follow-up beeline-c1b.
(4) Did not comment upstream; if desired, a confirmation comment on #18259 noting the nextval variant + that #21516 fixes it on nightly would help triage.
close_reason: Repro'd (3-command CLI case); already reported upstream (duckdb#18259) and fixed on main (PR #21516, verified on 1.6.0.dev365). Not in any release yet — CHECKPOINT-after-DDL rule stands; beeline-c1b tracks dropping it at upgrade.

title: Nightly sync misses edits to observations older than the window
description: The nightly pipeline syncs d1 = today − BEELINE_SYNC_DAYS (14) with no d2 — but iNat's d1/d2 filter on observed_on, not edit time. A volunteer fixing a June observation in August (exactly what the QC page instructs) is never re-fetched, so their finding never clears: the self-service promise currently only holds for observations under two weeks old. Late determinations and deletion detection age out the same way. Candidate fixes: (a) add updated_since to the sweep — fetch anything changed since the last successful run regardless of observed_on (the precise tool; check it composes with the id-keyset pagination); (b) a second weekly night job sweeping the whole season/year; (c) simply widen the window (costly against the 100 req/min budget as seasons accumulate). Decide against sync-inat's drift-immunity design notes; observation_seen/deletion semantics must stay coherent for whichever window a run declares.
design: Design (Peter + analysis, 2026-08-22): SLO = current within 24h for creations/edits and within a week for deletions, over the trailing 12 months. Two run kinds. (1) Nightly INCREMENTAL: id-keyset sweep with updated_since = last completed run's started_at − 1h margin (activity-based: catches edits/creations of ANY-aged observation; overlap is free via hash-dedup); first run ever falls back to a full 12-month sweep. Recorded with sync_run.updated_since NOT NULL, and the missing_upstream covering-run join EXCLUDES such runs — an updated_since sweep proves nothing about absence (not-updated ≠ gone). observation_seen rows from them still advance last_seen (presence is presence). (2) Weekly ANTI-ENTROPY: full id-keyset sweep, d1 = today − 365d, no updated_since — the presence proof that drives deletion detection and catches anything incremental missed. Both end with promote + elevation. id-keyset composes with updated_since (immutable-id cursor unaffected by filters; mid-sweep updates caught next night via the margin). Salishsea decision 018 is the cursor prior art; its 'self-healing 10-day window' crutch is what this replaces.
close_reason: updated_since incremental nightly + Sunday anti-entropy sweep implemented, tested (98 green), deployed to sandbox (schema surgery applied: updated_since column, sample_promotion_finding backfill-table, views replayed, checkpointed)

title: In-app sample editing for non-iNat samples (trap/legacy)
description: Split from the QC flagship (beeline-2c3.6): samples without a backing iNaturalist observation can't be fixed upstream, so their QC findings need in-app editing — a sample edit form (locality, place fields, protocol, counts) writing directly to the sample layer, gated to the collector (and eventually staff). The QC page already shows these samples with 'staff can correct it; in-app editing is coming' copy (m.qc.notInatBacked). Design question: are collector edits to non-iNat samples plain UPDATEs pre-cutover, or events once the correction overlay (ADR 0004) goes live?
design: Decisions (Peter, 2026-08-22): collector edits are correction EVENTS per ADR 0004 (frozen-upstream case), never plain UPDATEs — sample entity_ids are minted at promote (nextval) so they aren't stable, and plain UPDATEs vanish on blow-away rebuilds. Events are keyed by staging Mongo _id + column, same vocabulary as legacy_correction_pivot (ingest/promote-legacy.sql); a sample-level edit fans out to all staging _ids grouped into that sample (legacy_sample_map). Durable store: an app-written corrections file under data/ (same CSV schema: _id, field, base_value, new_value, author, reason), OUTSIDE the blow-away path; promote reads the UNION of ingest/legacy-corrections.csv (git-curated) and the app file — one merge rule, one vocabulary. NOT the private store: ADR 0003 reserves it for must-never-travel data (tokens, addresses); corrections are attributed model assertions that should copy freely. Staff may graduate app rows into the git CSV for review trail. Scope: fields limited to the existing correctable vocabulary (locality, country/stateProvince/county, samplingProtocol, dates, coordinates); specimen counts are row add/remove, not field edits — split to a separate bead.
notes: Implementation note (2026-08-22): the app store data/corrections.csv keeps ONE CURRENT ROW per (_id, field) — a later edit replaces the row (src/corrections.ts) rather than appending, so promotion never sees app-side duplicates and latest-wins needs no timestamps. This diverges from the recorded 'append-only events' phrasing deliberately: the CSV duplicate rule (max new_value wins + warning) would otherwise pick arbitrarily between a volunteer's typo and their fix. History of superseded app corrections is not kept; the git CSV remains the reviewed/curated archive staff graduate rows into. First cut fields: locality, country, state_province, county, protocol. Saves also settle stored within_sample_disagreement findings for edited fields. Counts split to beeline-2c3.9.
close_reason: Shipped: /samples/:id/edit (collector-gated, non-iNat only) writes correction events to data/corrections.csv (survives blow-away rebuilds; promote reads union of git CSV + app file, app rows winning) and updates the live sample row so qc_finding clears immediately. QC card now links the edit form. 109 tests green incl. full rebuild round-trip.

title: QC waivers: schema and staff workflow (printability's waiver clause)
description: Deferred here from the QC flagship (beeline-2c3.6, decision 2026-08-22): waivers exist to unblock printing, so they land with this phase. qc_waiver per the sketch (staff excuses a specific blocking finding on a specific sample; append-only, visible), the printable_sample view gains its 'no blocking finding without a live waiver' clause, and the staff UI decides who may waive — which needs the minimal staff concept the schema has so far avoided.

title: Deployment: single process, TLS, secrets, private-store key
description: Where and how the app runs: a single Node process (it owns the database — exactly one instance, ever) under a supervisor (systemd) behind TLS (Caddy or nginx), on the production host. Secrets: the private.duckdb encryption key lives outside both database files (environment/secrets manager, never beside the file, never in repo or backups — ADR 0003 says key management is the whole game). Sandbox-until-launch: dev instances are expected and cheap (blow-away era), so document how a fresh instance comes up — db:build, legacy load, inat login — building on the existing README flow. Pre-cutover this can be modest; real backups start phase 7.
design: Decisions (Peter, 2026-08-22): sandbox deploys to maderas — EXPLICITLY TEMPORARY, production hosting re-decided at cutover with Andony. Hostname beeline.beeatlas.net (DNS via the beeatlas repo's CDK stack, never hand-edit Route 53). Sandbox gets its own iNat OAuth app under Peter's account (one callback URL per registration; dev app's slot stays localhost:3054). Pattern: user systemd service + Apache ProxyPass + certbot, same as beeatlas-api. Tracked config in infra/maderas/; runbook docs/runbooks/deploy-maderas.md.
notes: Remaining manual steps (Peter/sudo): CDK DNS record in beeatlas repo; register sandbox OAuth app; on maderas run runbook §1-6 (clone, secrets incl. openssl rand -hex 32 private key, db provisioning, systemd unit, Apache vhost + certbot). Claude can drive the no-sudo parts over ssh on request.
close_reason: Sandbox live at https://beeline.beeatlas.net: user systemd service (owns the DB, encrypted private store, key in ~/.config/beeline/env) behind Apache ProxyPass + certbot on maderas (temporary hosting, re-decided at cutover). Infra tracked in infra/maderas/, runbook docs/runbooks/deploy-maderas.md.

title: Self-service QC experience (flagship)
description: The phase's flagship, replacing the legacy weekly hand-assembled CSV emails: a volunteer signs in, sees their flagged records, understands exactly what to do (the qc_rule guidance text), and resolves them in one session. Most fixes happen on iNaturalist and clear on next sync — the app's job is to say so clearly and reflect the clearing; trap samples get in-app fixes. Findings are already queryable per-rule views (130_view_qc_finding). Scope questions to settle in design: waiver UI for staff (qc_waiver exists in schema), sample-keyed vs finding-keyed presentation, and how resolved-on-next-sync is communicated (finding disappears vs shown pending). Staff overrides and corrections UI can start here or split out once scoped.
design: Decisions (Peter, 2026-08-22): sample-keyed presentation (cards of your samples-with-findings, one fix-on-iNat link each); honest timestamps for sync state (findings are derived views that disappear after sync; page shows last sync_run and 'fixes appear after next sync' — no fixed-marker state); waivers deferred to label printing (filed under beeline-1kb); your QC list IS the home page (empty state congratulates).
close_reason: Sample-keyed QC home shipped: catalog instructions, fix links, honest sync timestamps, all-clear state; 86 tests green; waivers→1kb.9, in-app editing→new bead

title: Message catalog: all user-facing strings from page one
description: Every user-facing string goes through a lightweight message catalog from the first page, even while en is the only catalog — keeping the fr-CA question (beeline-1a7) a content question instead of an architecture question, and giving the pronouns work (beeline-0qr) a vocabulary home. Keep it boring: keyed messages with interpolation, no framework. Decide how the guidance text living in the database (qc_rule guidance in schema/050_qc.sql, COMMENT ON strings surfaced to users, if any) relates to the catalog — likely: the catalog owns what users see, the schema keeps its copy as documentation.
close_reason: Typed en catalog owns all UI copy incl. QC instructions (pinned to qc_rule seed by test) and pronoun forms; 79 tests green

title: In-process job scheduler under the interactivity SLAs
description: Move the hand-run pipelines (inat:sync, inat:promote, elevation:fetch/derive) into the app process as scheduled jobs, replacing the legacy nothing-runs-on-a-schedule admin-task model. Jobs are authenticated-or-abort and fail loudly (partial fetches never report empty success — reference-implementation requirement 3). Every job step respects the ADR 0005 write-budget SLA — chunked transactions that yield the database — except tasks scheduled into the middle-of-the-night carve-out, which may run long. Needs: job registry, schedule, run history (visible to staff), and failure surfacing (ties into beeline-8w6 operational logging).
close_reason: Job framework (LA-night due logic, SLA-timed steps, job_run history), nightly sync pipeline + session purge, /jobs page with run-now; 95 tests green

title: Auth: iNat OAuth sign-in, sessions, approval gate
description: iNat OAuth from the first page — the flow exists in src/inat-login.ts for the pipeline; this generalizes it to the app: sign in with iNaturalist, mint a session (signed HTTP-only cookie, hand-rolled — no session framework), store the OAuth token in the private store per ADR 0003 (stored at first login but not used until the person is approved; purged after months of inactivity and on membership drop). The approval gate is the person↔atlas link: an unapproved signer-in sees a holding page, not data. CSRF protection on all writes. No anonymous reads anywhere — enforced structurally by the scaffold, verified here.
close_reason: OAuth flow, private-store sessions, approval gate, CSRF origin check; 75 tests green

title: App scaffold: Hono server, SSR layout, Lit islands build
description: The skeleton everything else hangs on: Hono on Node (web-standard Request/Response — handlers stay portable functions per the easily-replaced dependency philosophy), server-rendered HTML pages, Vite building the Lit light-DOM island components, dev/prod entry points, and the app process opening beeline.duckdb read-write plus ATTACHing private.duckdb per ADR 0003. Kysely (pinned 0.28.x) is already the query layer. Includes the base page layout and the environment banner hook point (beeline-2u8, sandbox-until-launch, becomes trivial once the layout exists). No page ships without a session — the scaffold should make an unauthenticated route the thing you have to work to create.
design: Decisions (Peter, 2026-08-22): src/app/ in the same package (no workspace split; app shares src/db.ts + src/model.ts). Server views in hono/jsx (TSX; visibly distinct from lit-html, markup typechecked) — hono/html rejected because its lit-lookalike syntax has different semantics. Dev: tsx watch for the server + vite build --watch for Lit islands (no Vite in the server path; dev and prod identical in shape; no HMR accepted). CSS: Material Design 3 as design language — material-color-utilities generates the scheme from a seed color, tokens as CSS custom properties, hand-rolled base stylesheet over semantic HTML; @material/web NOT adopted as foundation (maintenance mode pending new maintainers, github.com/material-components/material-web/discussions/5642) but individual widgets may be cherry-picked into islands later. Pico rejected (bad prior experience).
close_reason: Scaffold live: server+SSR+session gate+islands+pattern library, 69 tests green, proofed in browser

title: ADR 0005: app owns the DuckDB file; ingestion in-process; interactivity SLAs
description: Resolve ADR 0001's phase-4 decision point: the app store stays DuckDB, and the single Node app process owns beeline.duckdb read-write — single-writer becomes the concurrency model rather than a constraint. Ingestion (inat:sync, promotes, elevation) moves inside the process as scheduled jobs (reference-implementation requirement 3 wants scheduled ingestion anyway). The teeth: explicit interactivity SLAs — a budget for how long any transaction or job step may hold the database/write path before yielding, with a carve-out for middle-of-the-night tasks that may run long. Long jobs chunk their transactions to stay under budget. ADR 0003's encrypted private.duckdb ATTACH survives unchanged; the Postgres port remains available via dialect-neutral DDL if the tripwire ever fires again. Also record the web stack (Hono; SSR HTML + Lit light-DOM islands; message catalog from page one) — here or as a sibling ADR, per the sparing-ADRs convention. Update ADR 0001's status line and the roadmap's phase-4 decision-point note.
close_reason: ADR 0005 written; ADR 0001/0003 status lines and roadmap updated

title: Web app (roadmap phase 4)
description: The authenticated web app: iNat OAuth from the first page, no anonymous reads (sample_location makes leaks a live hazard), self-service QC as the flagship experience. Stack decided 2026-08-22 (Peter): DuckDB stays as the app store with the app process owning the database file and ingestion moving in-process as scheduled jobs — with explicit interactivity SLAs bounding how long anything may tie up the database, and a carve-out for middle-of-the-night tasks; Hono as the HTTP layer; server-rendered HTML with Lit light-DOM islands for interactivity (the pnwmoths/salishsea pattern, applied server-side); all user-facing strings through a message catalog from page one. Determinations UI is phase 6, label printing phase 5 — this phase ends when a volunteer can sign in, see their flagged records, and resolve them in one session.

title: End-to-end mock exercise: print runs, proofing, reprints, mailing
description: The phase's acceptance test per the roadmap: with mock data, walk the whole lifecycle — prepare a run from printable samples, pull a record while proofing, approve, render sheets, mark printed and mailed, file and fulfill a reprint, and verify the snapshots survive later data edits (a post-print correction names the invalidated labels; a count decrease raises the specimens-exceed-count finding). Exercised pre-cutover while databases are still blow-away; the first real run happens at cutover, December 2026.
notes: SCANNER CHECK DONE (Arthur, 2026-09-18, reported by Peter after the demo meeting): labels rendered by src/label-pdf.ts scan. Both forms were tried and both read: the vector DataMatrix that shipped in #79, and the earlier 1-bit bitmap that looked blurry on screen. So the DMRE 8x18 symbol, digits only, at the reference implementation's geometry, is confirmed readable, including the quiet zone CodeRabbit questioned on #79 (0.79pt between the text boxes and the matrix, under one module). The blur was cosmetic rather than functional; vector stays, since it is also what prints cleanly. Still owed for this exercise: holding a sheet against a legacy label at the same scale, and the rest of the lifecycle (pulls, reprints, mailing) once those are built.

title: Per-atlas geoprivacy revelation policy wired into printability
description: Beeline retains both coordinate pairs; whether an atlas may reveal true coordinates of taxon-obscured records on printed labels is a per-atlas policy/regulatory question and a go-live blocker (docs/questions.md, Taxon geoprivacy). This issue is the model side: a per-atlas policy the printable_sample view consults, with the safe default (taxon-obscured records unprintable, current behavior) until an atlas answers. Also decide the interim alternative the question raises: stay unprintable vs print with obscured coordinates. The regulatory legwork itself (asking each atlas) stays with staff; cutover is gated on the answers.

title: Mailing addresses: private satellite, deliverability, mailing workflow
description: mailing_address as a per-person private satellite (sketch: readable only by the label-printing side, writable by its owner) — same isolation discipline as sample_location: joining it in is a deliberate act. Needs: how addresses are collected (self-service in the web app?), deliverability/bounce tracking, and the mailing step of the print-run state machine (printed → mailed). How other atlases plan to mail — postage, bulk-mail access — is question P3. Blank-cell-between-collectors in the sheet layout exists to serve cutting and mailing per collector; the mailing workflow should say what staff actually do between printed and mailed.
notes:
The addresses this needs are now on disk. `pnpm legacy:fetch` pulls the legacy
usernames register to `data/legacy/usernames.csv` (gitignored) — 617 rows keyed
by iNat login, of which 575 carry an address and 551 a stateProvince
(beeline-8t8).

They are deliberately NOT in beeline.duckdb. `legacy_username_register` stages
the name columns only; email, address, city, stateProvince, zipPostal and
country stay in the file, because the private satellite this bead designs is
where they belong (ADR 0003) and it does not exist yet. So this bead does not
need a fetch step — it needs a destination, and then a loader that reads those
columns out of the file it already has.

Coverage caveat carried over: the register is keyed by userLogin, so it reaches
only people with iNat accounts. 414 of 580 people in the store match a register
row; the trap-only co-collectors are not in it and never will be.
WHERE LABELS GET MAILED — measured 2026-08-25 against the fetched register,
after Peter flagged "I assume labels get mailed to the address attached to the
account, but this is an assumption".

Mostly true in the legacy system, and it breaks in three ways this bead should
design around rather than inherit.

1. THE FIELD IS DOING DOUBLE DUTY AS A DELIVERY INSTRUCTION. Of 575 register
   rows carrying an address, 16 logins share an 11-character value reading
   "Keep in lab", 12 share "Not Specified", and 8 share a 6-character course
   code (ENT499 appears in the file). At least 36 are not mailing addresses at
   all — they record a decision NOT to mail. A mailing_address satellite that
   only holds addresses cannot express "keep in the lab", and that is a real
   state the print-run lifecycle has to carry between printed and mailed.

2. THE MAILING UNIT IS A HOUSEHOLD OR A LAB, NOT AN ACCOUNT. 26 addresses are
   shared by two or more logins — 21 by two, two by three, plus the
   institutional clusters of 8, 12 and 16. As a per-PERSON satellite (the
   sketch's shape) Gretchen and Robert Pederson get two rows that must be kept
   in sync, and one lab bench gets sixteen. Worth deciding whether the
   satellite hangs off the person and duplicates, or whether an address is its
   own thing that people point at.

3. A COLLECTOR WITH NO LOGIN HAS NO ADDRESS ANYWHERE. The register is keyed by
   userLogin, so it reaches nobody without one. Four people actively collecting
   in 2024-25 have no iNat login on any record: Mario Luppino (111 samples),
   Heather Andrews (99), Salena Helmreich (21), Michael Getz (6). No login, no
   register row, no address. The household partners are fine — Robert Pederson
   and Julie Biddle file under pandg and tom_julie, which carry Bend and Salem
   addresses — but these four are the population "mail to the address on the
   account" silently drops, and they are exactly the people beeline-oyl decided
   will never have an account.

The three contested households all do have an address on the shared account
(pandg → Bend, tom_julie → Salem, smalaby → Klamath Falls), so for couples the
assumption holds for the reason that makes it work: one household, one address.
DECIDED (Andony, meeting 2026-09-11): we will not integrate with IdeaLogic for mailing addresses (GitHub #34). Beeline will manage the address records itself, so this bead has to cover where addresses come from, not just where they are stored.

- The first set of addresses comes from the legacy register (data/legacy/usernames.csv, already fetched; the gaps and oddities are in the note above).
- After that, Beeline is the only place addresses are kept, so it needs a way to maintain them. Either volunteers edit their own address, or staff edit it on /people/:id, or both. Collectors without an iNaturalist login have no other route, so staff editing is needed either way.
- Addresses are private data (ADR 0003). They need the same care as coordinates, and the repo is public (no addresses in fixtures, issues, or PRs).
- An authored address has to survive a rebuild the same way the person overlay does, because a store rebuild would otherwise wipe it until cutover.

title: Reprints and artifact lifecycle: superseded labels, voided numbers
description: reprint_request per the sketch: specimen, requester, reason, fulfilled by a later run. Provisional stance to confirm via walkthrough P6–P7: the catalog number is the specimen's permanent identity — fixing bad label data means a new print under the same number (printed_label rows across runs form the revision history; latest print = current intended label), with destruction of the old label a physical-workflow obligation the model may need to record rather than assume. Minting a new number is reserved for identity errors and would be an explicit append-only voiding event on minted_catalog_number with downstream Ecdysis/GBIF notification. Whether disposition needs first-class events (label_scrapped, number_voided) or stays derived-plus-convention awaits the staff answers. This also delivers requirement 5 from reference-implementation.md: corrections must be able to name the physical labels they invalidate.
notes:
THE PROVISIONAL STANCE IS CONTRADICTED BY PRACTICE (Arthur, 2026-09-08).

This bead assumed the catalog number is the specimen's permanent identity, that fixing bad label data means a new print under the SAME number, and that minting a new one is reserved for identity errors. Arthur says the opposite is what staff actually do: when a printed label disagrees with the record, the label is reprinted under a NEW field number. So a specimen wears several field numbers over its life, one at a time, and voiding is routine rather than exceptional — which also decides the question this bead deferred, since a routine voiding needs first-class events and a museum catalog number derived from a retired number is stale rather than wrong.

Arthur's sketch for the new system: the volunteer confirms the pinned label disagrees with the record, we reprint under a new number, send it, and keep a record of it having happened; a flag reference sheet then pulls those specimens for manual verification when everyone submits their bees. For a duplicate number, keep the pinned label that matches the record and renumber the other.

Not a decision yet — Arthur described practice and proposed a shape; the choice between his rule and this bead's is Peter's and Andony's, and is question 4 of docs/questions.md 'Printing and mailing'. Nothing here should be built until it is settled, because the two stances need different schemas.

Legacy evidence is inconclusive and deliberately recorded as such: 545 specimen identities (same collector, sample, specimen and date, coordinates agreeing to 3dp) carry more than one field number, 116 printed on different days — but 1,778 further identities with differing coordinates are same-day duplicate sample numbers producing the same signature, so 545 is an upper bound, not a measurement.
CORRECTION (2026-09-09): my previous note said Arthur's account contradicts this bead's provisional stance and should probably replace it. That was written without reading gh-17's comments, where Andony had answered the same question eight days earlier — and Andony AGREES with this bead.

Andony (gh-17, 2026-08-31): 'Field numbers are not voided, even if no physical specimen exists for a given number', and 'Ensure the label generation system supports reprinting of existing IDs when label metadata is updated.'
Arthur (2026-09-08): numbers 'have been permanently scrapped', and a label disagreeing with the record is reprinted 'under a different field number'.

So it is not practice-versus-proposal. It is two people who run printing giving opposite answers about their own system, and this bead's stance matching one of them. Nothing is settled and nothing here should be built.

Possible reconciliation, not to be assumed: Arthur's label-lifecycle wording ('check WHICH label matches the information associated with a field number') may be about resolving a DUPLICATE, where a second number is genuinely needed and Andony would likely agree. But his separate answer about permanently scrapped numbers and ghost records is not about duplicates, so the two cannot be waved together. Ask them in the same room — docs/questions.md 'Printing and mailing' question 4.
SUPERSEDED in substance by ADR 0008 (docs/adr/0008-specimen-identity.md), merged to main 2026-09-10 as proposed.

This bead's provisional stance — the number is the specimen's permanent identity, a data-error reprint carries it, minting reserved for identity errors — is largely what the ADR decided, but the reasoning behind it was wrong and the ADR says so. The field number was never what downstream cites. That is dwc:occurrenceID, which Beeline does not have and which the reference implementation derives FROM the field number for Oregon. With Beeline minting its own, a renumbering costs an otherCatalogNumbers entry rather than a broken published link.

So what remains of this bead is narrow: if gh-17 comes back saying a bad-data reprint does renumber, the model needs a renumbering event beyond the duplicate repair, the reprint screen has to offer it, and otherCatalogNumbers becomes a routine export column. Nothing else moves — and notably 'nothing is voided' does not move either, because the registry makes the current number derived, so a superseded number is a non-current row rather than a voided one. That is the whole cost, and it is bounded.

Arthur narrowed it further on 2026-09-09: a lost-label reprint keeps its field number, so his renumbering is confined to the bad-data case. Question 1 of the Printing section in docs/questions.md is what is left.
Peter, 2026-09-14: staff need a way to mark ANY printed label for reprint, not only in response to a collector's reprint request. One case that motivates it is a refused iNaturalist edit that staff decide to accept (beeline-1kb.17), but the mechanism is general: a staff member picks specimens or labels, gives a reason, and they are queued for a later run. It is the same reprint_request row with a staff author instead of the collector.
Peter, 2026-09-14: VOLUNTEERS can request reprints of a SELECTION of their labels, with an explanation of why. The explanation is typically one of two: "I never received it", or "I accidentally destroyed/cut/marred it".

Design implications, not decided:
- Offer the two common reasons as quick choices, with free text always available. An explanation is required.
- Selection has to work at the sizes people think in: one specimen's label, every label from a sample, and every label from one mailing. Someone who never received an envelope is missing all of it.
- "Never received" may be a mailing problem, not a label problem. When a whole mailing, or repeated mailings, never arrive, staff should be pointed at the address (beeline-1kb.6) before another envelope goes to the same place. A reprint mailing also needs its own address label (beeline-1kb.16).
- A request lands in a later print run. The collector should be able to see that it is pending, and when it printed.
- Arthur confirmed a lost-label reprint keeps its field number (2026-09-09), so these requests never renumber anything.
Staff marking any label (note above) is the same request with a staff author.

title: Label rendering: PDF sheets with barcodes
description: Render frozen printed_label content to printable PDF sheets. Reference implementation: 250 labels per US Letter sheet via pdf-lib, 3–5pt auto-shrinking Oxygen Mono, DataMatrix barcode of the catalog number, blank cell between collectors, location like 'USA:OR:BentonCo Corvallis', date as day.RomanMonth year - sample.specimen ('14.VII2025-3.2'). Whether the 250/page geometry and tiny fonts are constraints of stock, printer, or mere convention is question P2; other atlases' equipment and stock is P3 — confirm before hard-coding the geometry. Input is the snapshot (printed_label.content), never live data, so a sheet can be re-rendered byte-identical later.
notes: BUILT 2026-09-17, PR #75 (src/label-pdf.ts, assets/fonts) and the screens in PR #76 (/print-runs, the run page, /print-runs/:id/labels.pdf cached under data/print-runs with pdf_sha256 recorded; Label column on the sample page, Labels block on the specimen page). Close when #76 merges. Geometry is the reference's verbatim per Arthur's request; the DataMatrix is a 1-bit image XObject from bwip-js's module matrix (raw()), digits only, DMRE 8x18 stood on end; renders byte-identical (test hashes two renders). Warnings at the reference's thresholds (location 38, collector 22, method 5) plus a missing county; never a block. The county-suffix data defect the rehearsal surfaced is beeline-gr7.
close_reason: Merged as #75 (20dbf1d) and #76 (a8118df) on 2026-09-18 and deployed to the sandbox: the renderer, the /print-runs screens, the cached PDF route, and the volunteer's label state. Closed over beeline-1kb.1 for the same reason as beeline-1kb.2; Arthur's view of the collector line is gh-77 (beeline-1kb.18).

title: Proofing pulls: remove records from a prepared run
description: Between prepared and approved, the proofer (Arthur today) can pull records out of a run before it goes to paper. What he actually inspects and what causes a pull is question P1 — this issue is blocked on the walkthrough. Design questions: does a pull just drop printed_label rows from the run (numbers already minted and burned?) or are numbers minted only at approval; does a pulled record get a QC finding or a note; can a pull shrink a run to zero.

title: Print run model: freeze, specimen individuation, catalog number minting
description: The core event: a print run freezes printable samples into specimen rows, mints their catalog numbers, and snapshots label content + QC findings as seen at freeze time (printed_label), immune to later data changes. State machine prepared → approved → printed → mailed per the sketch. Minting must be a hard uniqueness guarantee (sequence/constraint) scoped to what Beeline itself mints — no global UNIQUE on specimen.catalog_number, history forbids it (25051768 exists twice on paper). A canceled run's numbers stay burned: gaps are harmless, reuse never is. Consequences already committed to in the sketch: before printing QC operates at sample level; count decreases only become findings after printing. Design after the walkthrough answers land.
notes: BUILT 2026-09-17, PR #74 (schema/035, schema/117, schema/155, src/print-run.ts, src/label-text.ts, migrations 0030–0031; promotion lock in mint-samples.sql and promote-observations.sql). Close when #74 merges. Decisions taken in the build, beyond the plan: (1) cancelling destroys nothing — DuckDB will not delete a referenced row in the transaction that removed its references, so a canceled run keeps its labels, its specimens keep their rows with field_number cleared, numbers stay burned, individuated_specimen takes them out of pending/count_below_printed, and the next freeze re-adopts the rows (same occurrence_id, new number); (2) 'prints its own labels' is a satellite row atlas_printing, not a column — DuckDB cannot add a NOT NULL column to a referenced table by migration; (3) every author column after prepared_by is a plain INTEGER, since a FK is an index and an indexed column on a referenced row cannot be updated; (4) occurrence_id is a UUID v7 with a unique index in its own migration; (5) the freeze runs behind an in-process lock on its own connection, and stops on a pending sample with no location row or no single primary collector. Rehearsed on a dev-store copy: 5,411 labels, 1,062 samples, 128 collectors, 23 sheets, first number 26072092, both check views empty. Not built here: pulls (1kb.3), reprints (1kb.5), the divergence surfaces (1kb.17).
close_reason: Merged as #74 (f20d7f8) on 2026-09-18 and deployed to the sandbox; migrations 0030 and 0031 applied at boot. Closed over its dependency on beeline-1kb.1: the walkthrough gated the design, Peter chose to build the first slice on the answers already in hand, and what is still open there (the bad-data reprint) touches only the reprint path, which is beeline-1kb.5.

title: Printing walkthrough with Arthur/Andony (questions P1–P8)
description: Observe the printing moment end to end and get answers to docs/questions.md 'Printing and mailing' P1–P7: what Arthur inspects when proofing and what pulls a record from a run (P1); whether 250-per-page / 3–5pt fonts are stock, printer, or convention (P2); how other atlases plan to print and mail (P3); the E-prefix and 2018 name-based identifiers on physical labels (P4); where historical cross-project duplicate field numbers lived (P5); label lifecycle on bad data — same-number reprint, old label destroyed, confirmed or on faith (P6); whether a catalog number has ever been voided and how Ecdysis/GBIF would learn (P7). The roadmap gates phase-5 design on this walkthrough; P6–P7 decide whether disposition needs first-class events (label_scrapped, number_voided) or stays derived-plus-convention.
notes:
LABEL COLLECTOR TEXT, read off the legacy code (2026-08-23, ~/dev/OBP-Server): worker/src/handlers/LabelsSubtaskHandler.js composes the collector line as `${firstNameInitial}${lastName}` — no separator. So a solo label reads 'P.Abrahamsen', not 'P. Abrahamsen'; the space is not there, presumably deliberate on a 0.666in-wide label at 3-5pt. firstNameInitial is not derived: it comes from the curated register shared/data/usernames.csv (UsernamesService), i.e. the legacy system already stored a per-person label override.

For pairs the same concatenation produces artifacts, not a design: "M. and D.O'Loughlin" (10,984 specimens), "M. | D.O'Loughlin | O'Loughlin" (10,515), 'S./S.Sheehy&Malaby' (1,242), and 'L. | M. | A. | R.Best| Herrmann | Melathopoulos | Seitz' — 55 characters on a label whose longest solo name is 26. So P1-P7 should include: what SHOULD a shared label say? Options: 'M.&D.O''Loughlin', 'M.O''Loughlin & D.O''Loughlin', or first collector only. Related: OccurrenceService.js:415-423 hard-codes the shared household login 'pandg', assigning Gretchen or Robert Pederson by whether sampleId > 100 — a shared-account problem patched in code.

Other label fields, for the record: location 'USA:OR:BentonCo Corvallis', coordinates '44.565 -123.262 72m', date '14.VII2025-1.3' (day.RomanMonth[-day2.Month]year-sample.specimen), method net/trap/nest lowercased from samplingProtocol.
SCOPE REFRESHED 2026-08-28: docs/questions.md 'Printing and mailing' has renumbered since this bead was written. It now runs P1-P8: an attribution question was inserted at P7 (records belonging to no member atlas), pushing the field-number lifecycle question this bead called P7 down to P8. The attribution one is a program decision rather than a bench practice, so it has moved out to its own child, beeline-1kb.1.2, and is for Andony rather than Arthur. Everything else this bead describes still maps one-to-one; only the numbering moved.
ANSWERED IN PART (Arthur, 2026-09-08), landed in docs on branch arthur-printing-answers.

Answered: P1 proofing (two labels per sheet, different volunteers where the sheet has more than one; field number copied into the dashboard search and compared on recordedBy / sampleId / specimenId / verbatimEventDate; no disagreement ever found; escalation checks Andony's R script first, then blames the labels subtask rather than the observations subtask). P2 stock (US Letter, 163 g/m2 cardstock — so 250-per-sheet is layout convention, not a stock or printer limit, and there is room for another row or two at the same label and font sizes; Arthur recommends matching the existing geometry). P6 label lifecycle. P7 number scrapping ('ghost records': data written to a number, then emptied and moved to a new one; one such row in 383,032 legacy records, Stephanie_Hazen:18.053.058, plus seventeen missing only the sample number).

Still open, now questions 1-3 and 5-7 of docs/questions.md 'Printing and mailing': what pulls a record out of a run by hand (the other half of P1); whether a superseded label's swap is ever confirmed; whether a lost-label reprint keeps its number; how a post-publication retirement reaches Ecdysis/GBIF (the other half of P7); the E prefix and 2018 identifiers (P4); where the cross-project duplicates lived (P5).

P3 is not Arthur's to answer and is deleted: no other atlas currently prints or mails (Peter, 2026-08-28).
gh-17 also carries ANDONY's answers (2026-08-31), which my earlier note missed entirely. They answer P4 (the E prefix denotes Emily Carlson's PhD work) and partly P5 (duplicate resolution is underway, 2025 then back through 2024), and they CONTRADICT Arthur on P6/P7 — see beeline-1kb.5. gh-17 also asks a sixth question neither has answered: what a shared label should say for a collecting pair, which is two thirds of legacy trap specimens. The issue is not closeable.

title: Label printing (roadmap phase 5)
description: Own the pre-print lifecycle the legacy system never persisted: print runs, proofing pulls, reprints, mailing addresses — exercised end to end with mock data before cutover. Design happens after the Arthur/Andony printing walkthrough (questions P1–P7 in docs/questions.md). The schema sketch's Label governance section (print_run, printed_label, reprint_request, minted_catalog_number) is the starting point, re-reviewed when built per the sketch's status note. Legacy findings that shape this phase: print state was one mutable string per record (no history, no sheets, no way to name which physical labels a correction invalidates); catalog-number uniqueness was advisory scan-and-increment (one live duplicate, 25051768); everything in production is already printed, so the replacement owns the entire pre-print population for the first time.
notes: 2026-08-27: the reference implementation answers a question this phase would otherwise have had to ask. A label carries no taxon — LabelsSubtaskHandler.js:59-113 builds exactly six fields (location, coordinates+elevation, date, collector, method, field number) and never reads scientificName/genus/specificEpithet/identifiedBy, and the determinations subtask produces no label of its own. So printing happens before determination and is not gated on one, which errorFlags corroborates by naming no taxon field. Consequences: determination qualifiers (beeline-tgu) and morphospecies (beeline-8g7) cannot affect a label, and printability needs no clause for either — they are export questions (phase 7, DwC identificationQualifier/verbatimIdentification), not printing ones. Whether Beeline's label should differ from the reference here is worth one sentence at the Arthur/Andony walkthrough, but nothing in the reference suggests anyone wants a taxon on the pin.

title: Expert determination workflows: discovery before building the expert UI
description: Peter (2026-08-22): we don't know enough about how taxonomists actually work — what filtering/sorting they need when determining volunteer specimens. The pros likely have carefully honed processes and may prefer uploading spreadsheets, perhaps via Ecdysis (determination.channel 'ecdysis_import' already models that path). The in-app expert grid (beeline-bcq wireframes, marked provisional) may mostly serve staff/semi-experts like Peter; some volunteers might also prefer a validated spreadsheet-upload path. Talk through with Andony / Caleb Lankford / outside experts (Joel Gardner) before building anything expert-facing.
notes:
2026-08-27: beeline-tgu (identification qualifiers: the store cannot record cf./aff., which the glossary already teaches) needs an answer from the same conversation — do determiners use qualifiers, which vocabulary, and should a qualified determination be printable? Worth carrying into the discovery rather than guessing a CHECK.
2026-08-27: beeline-tgu shipped determination.qualifier with the vocabulary cf./aff./nr. — the three that modify a species assertion. Only nr. is attested in legacy data (3 records). If determiners actually use a wider vocabulary, or want sp. nov. / s. str. recorded rather than derived, that is a change to the CHECK and belongs in this discovery.
Andony, meeting 2026-09-11: no automated connection to Ecdysis for now, in either direction. Moving data goes through each atlas's staff, and GBIF probably the same. Expert determinations made in Ecdysis therefore come back as spreadsheets that staff bring in, which is the 'ecdysis_import' channel already imagined. An automated connection is not on the table.
Peter, 2026-09-14: typically only taxonomists will enter determinations. They work in batches, in some cases through Ecdysis. The real impact on Beeline is that verbatim determinations are preserved, and not all of them will resolve to ITIS taxa (beeline-45v).
CORRECTION (Peter, 2026-09-14): taxonomists are not the only ones entering determinations. Volunteers commonly do. Taxonomists are typically the source of determinations whose names are not in ITIS; they work in batches and sometimes through Ecdysis.

title: Environment banner: sandbox-until-launch and dev instances
description: Peter (2026-08-21, beeline-fmg session): every page must carry an obvious banner when the site is a sandbox — from first deploy until launch cutover — and on dev instances. Rationale: pre-cutover databases are blown away and rebuilt (no migrations), so nothing entered in the sandbox survives; a real volunteer poking at it must never mistake sandbox work for counted work. Design notes: driven by deployment config (environment name), unmissable but not workflow-blocking, present on the front door too (pre-login), and translated (es day-one like all surface text). Banner text should say what the environment IS and that changes will not be kept.
close_reason: Done as of de447d6. Config-driven (config.environment; every non-production instance banners), text from the message catalog (m.layout.envBanner — states which instance and that data may be blown away), unmissable but non-blocking (tertiary-container strip above the header), and now on the pre-session pages too: sign-in and pending-approval render through PublicPage, which was the last gap. Translation is the catalog seam; the locale set is beeline-1a7's question, not this issue's.

title: Data catalog and handling policy
description: Peter (2026-08-20, beeline-fmg session): at some point Beeline needs a data catalog + handling policy — a document enumerating every column's data class (public / operational / private / credential), retention rule, and backup treatment. Not now. It will lean on ADR 0003 (private satellites in a separately-secured encrypted store) for the storage architecture; the policy adds the per-column inventory and retention schedule (token TTL, pending-person purge window, address retention).
notes:
SECOND AXIS (Peter, 2026-08-24): the catalog should also record how each
attribute is HANDLED — upstream, derived, or authored — not only its data
class and retention. Motivation is user-facing: the answer is often not
straightforward, since Beeline is not authoritative over what it ingests from
Mongo, and a volunteer needs to know per field whether to fix it here, fix it
on iNaturalist, or that it cannot be fixed because it is computed.

Vocabulary settled this session (see also CONTEXT.md, pending): UPSTREAM =
authority lives elsewhere (iNat observations; the frozen legacy dump); fix at
source or record a correction over it. DERIVED = owned by nobody, a function
of its inputs, and a rebuild reproduces it exactly — that is the test.
AUTHORED = Beeline is the authority because it exists nowhere else.

FINDING, from classifying sample's 20 columns: a per-column enum cannot
answer this, because provenance often varies PER ROW. sample.atlas_id is
derived from geography on most rows and authored on some. locality is
upstream-frozen on most and authored on the corrected ones.

But the project has already solved that, consistently, in five places, and
has never named the pattern: where provenance varies per row, a SIBLING
COLUMN carries it.

  sample.atlas_assigned_by      null ⇒ geography, set ⇒ administrative
  sample_location.source        inat_trusted / inat_public / legacy_import
  sample_location.elevation_source_id   which DEM answered
  determination.channel         expert / volunteer
  person_admin.granted_by       who granted it, or 'seed'

So the catalog is a per-column POLICY, not a per-column label: what class the
column is, and — where it varies — which column records the per-row answer.
Its first useful output is therefore not 163 labels but the list of columns
whose provenance varies with NO sibling to say so. sample.locality is one:
whether a value came from Mongo or from a staff correction is knowable only
by reading data/corrections.csv, not from the store.

SECOND USE, code-level: promote-legacy.sql maintains the correctable
vocabulary by hand in THREE parallel lists, with a comment warning to extend
them together. A catalog could be the one source those are generated from.

SIZE: 163 columns across 31 tables, excluding legacy staging and qc_rule
views. Roughly ten classifications are genuinely open rather than merely
unwritten — sample.collector_id is beeline-v0j, and specimen tables cross
from derived to authored at cutover, which is what cutover IS.
SCOPE (Peter, 2026-08-24): catalog and classification are sometimes two documents, but this project is small enough for one — both axes (data class + retention, and handling: upstream/derived/authored) in a single catalog. No strong feeling, so one unless it gets unwieldy.

title: Trusted-access operations: whose token, project trust audit
description: Legacy uses one app-wide OAuth token (admin-linked). Decide Beeline's: which account(s) hold project-curator trust per project (OBA 18521, Master Melittologist 99706, WaBA 166376, others), token refresh (JWT expires 24h), and sanity-check iNat obscured-coordinate terms per CONTEXT note.
notes: SOURCE-PROJECT MAP (2026-08-21, sampled legacy obs per state → project_ids): OR→18521 oregon-bee-atlas-plant-images-sampleid; WA→166376 washington-bee-atlas-…-sample-ids; BC/NM/ID/KS/MT/YT (all other atlases)→99706 master-melittologist-outside-of-oregon. Border strays (NV/CA) ride in via 18521. Production sync = three sweeps, one per project. TRUST STATUS: rainhead is manager of 18521+166376 (project-curator trust LIVE-CONFIRMED today: private_geojson delivered, vtbo false; 2 samples upgraded inat_trusted from real WaBA July data, elevations retained, 3m accuracy). 99706 remains: Andony is sole manager — either he authorizes the OAuth app once, or (simpler) adds rainhead/service account as curator. OAuth+JWT-mint tooling (pnpm inat:login) built and validated. Remaining decisions: personal account vs service account for production; get 99706 curator access.
close_reason: Decisions made and architecture validated. Token policy: dev = rainhead, production = Andony (amelathopoulos), until per-volunteer tokens (beeline-fvx); OAuth apps owned by the individual user they run as. Andony admins all three source projects so production needs no new grants. Source-project map: OR→18521, WA→166376, all other atlases→99706. Tooling built and live-validated: pnpm inat:login (auth-code flow → stored access token → 24h JWT mint), project-curator trusted reads confirmed on real data (2 samples upgraded inat_trusted from WaBA July window). Trust audit method: presence of private_geojson under the curator token (preferences field serializes {} regardless). Production onboarding filed separately.

title: Deletion detection: absent from a complete covering run
description: Sketch rule: an observation is deleted when absent from a *complete* run that should have covered it (source + window + completed_at). Blocks further printing for its specimens; staff investigate. Needs window bookkeeping semantics.
close_reason: Deletion detection delivered: observation_seen presence log (hash-deduped loads can't distinguish unchanged from gone), written unconditionally per fetched observation inside the sync transaction. qc_rule_observation_missing_upstream (blocking): fires when a completed run over a seen source, started after last-seen, with a window containing observed_on, does not return the observation; covers deleted / removed-from-project / date-edited-out — staff investigate; reappearing clears by advancing last_seen. Schema change means existing DBs need a rebuild (no-migration stance).

title: Correction overlay: three-way merge design (ADR candidate)
description: Roadmap: design here though it matters post-cutover. Corrections apply over the latest load: take upstream when upstream changed and we didn't correct; keep the correction otherwise; upstream changing a corrected field resolves nothing — surfaces a QC finding. Shares shape with the legacy staging overlay (beeline-uuu).
close_reason: Design delivered as ADR 0004 (accepted 2026-08-21): corrections are append-only events anchored on the load the corrector saw — that load is the merge base. Upstream unchanged → correction applies; converged → auto-retire via one-way superseded_by_load_id latch; both moved → correction stands + correction_conflict warning finding, resolved only by a new correction based on the current load. Field vocabulary = observation_current_fields columns. Overlay applies at promotion. beeline-uuu legacy overlay = same shape with frozen upstream. Correction table itself waits for the self-service phase; no sync schema change needed.

title: Provenance upgrades from sync
description: Trusted reads (private_geojson + viewer_trusted_by_observer) upgrade sample_location source legacy_import → inat_trusted with true coordinates + real positional_accuracy; unobscured obs → inat_public. Also: geoprivacy/taxon_geoprivacy flags onto samples; obscured-untrusted samples get NO location (invariant). Staff login/ORCID harvesting from iNat users rides along (beeline-gju).
notes:
Real-data note (2026-08-20): taxon_geoprivacy arrives as the string 'open' (not only null) — map 'open' → NULL when propagating flags to sample (CHECK allows only obscured/private). Live window had 6 obscured obs; 1 obscured+taxon-open, 5 obscured+null.

CRITICAL detection rule (2026-08-20): viewer_trusted_by_observer=false even when project trust delivers private coordinates — it signals only PERSONAL trust. The operative signal for source='inat_trusted' is the PRESENCE of private_geojson in the projection. Trust is per-query-context (requester's curator role on the project named in the query + observer's opt-in), so the same observation can yield different projections through different project queries.
close_reason: Provenance promotion delivered: ingest/promote-observations.sql + src/promote-observations.ts (pnpm inat:promote), idempotent and transactional. Geoprivacy flags synced both directions ('open'→NULL); locations upgraded to inat_trusted on presence of private_geojson (the operative trust signal) else inat_public when unobscured; obscured-untrusted writes nothing (legacy believed-true rows kept); elevation survives only when coordinates unchanged, else cleared for beeline-bqz re-derivation. Observer→collector inat_account harvest (beeline-gju rides along) with both-ways-unambiguous guard. Live copy run: 264 samples upgraded to inat_public (anonymous smoke sync had no private coords), 2 accounts linked, 1 conflict refused.

title: Within-sample field disagreement: surface as a QC finding
description: Promotion takes descriptive fields from a representative row (min _id) per sample group; legacy rows within one sample can disagree (one sample held three localities: 'Dungeness Recreation Area' vs 'St Helens'). This is the entire residual in the errorFlags reconciliation (~100 of 380k rows, 0.03%): legacy flags per row, we per sample. Our one-locality-per-sample model is arguably correct — but the disagreement itself should become a finding (staging-level, keyed to the sample group) so staff can pick the right value. Candidates: locality, coordinates, county, protocol.
close_reason: within_sample_disagreement: sample-keyed findings persisted at promotion (sample_promotion_finding table, unioned into qc_finding, warning severity). Fields: locality, coordinates, county, protocol, country, state_province; empty = no opinion. Production run: 973 findings; reconcile residual ~100 → ~40 rows. Biggest cluster: trap-line rows with incrementing forest-road localities merged into one sample.

title: Pre-cutover entity audit (ADR 0002)
description: Before cutover makes ids forever, re-ask which tables want to be entities — cheap now, annoying after. Known candidates when their phases arrive: printed_label (physical-label identity for the scrapped/superseded/voided lifecycle), print_run, qc_waiver, correction, trap-site entities. Also revisit the deliberately-deferred entity registry table (real FK integrity for polymorphic refs) when corrections land. See docs/adr/0002-entities.md.

title: Correction overlay for staging rows that can't be fixed upstream
description: The residue answer for blocked legacy rows: rows fixable upstream get fixed in Mongo/iNat and picked up by re-fetch + re-promote (the cheap loop). Rows whose upstream is frozen (or wrong forever, like the 2,640 printed duplicate_specimen losers) get staff corrections keyed by Mongo _id — the correction table returns with entity='legacy_occurrence', applied by promotion before parsing, so fixes are explicit, attributed, and survive every re-run. Until then blocked rows remain permanently in staging with findings — never dropped; the final cutover staging snapshot is the archive, and catalog-number lookup should eventually search it too (135 printed fieldNumbers currently resolve to nothing in the model).
close_reason: Overlay implemented per ADR 0004 frozen-upstream case: ingest/legacy-corrections.csv (curated in git, survives blow-away rebuilds) keyed by Mongo _id + staging column; legacy_occurrence_corrected view applies it before parsing so blocked rows can be unblocked without touching upstream. Statuses per correction: applies / retired (upstream converged) / conflict (correction stands + warning finding) / orphaned / invalid_field / duplicate — all non-applies states surface as findings. Correctable vocabulary: 20 identity/parse/label columns (three lists in promote-legacy.sql extend together). Counts in promote output. 58/58 tests; full 383k-row rebuild reproduces identical results with the empty seed CSV. Staff can now start filling the CSV against the 2,753 blocked rows (2,640 are duplicate_specimen, inherently uncorrectable — the remaining ~113 date/name/specimen-number rows are the real targets).

title: Acceptance: reconcile QC findings and counts against production errorFlags
description: Compare qc_finding per rule against production errorFlags (~38k flagged, 97% locality). Expect explainable diffs (e.g. WY records flagged in prod due to their missing state-abbreviation entry). Also reconcile record/sample/specimen counts.
close_reason: Acceptance reconciliation complete (pnpm legacy:reconcile). Rule-by-rule vs production errorFlags over 380,279 promoted rows: locality 37,069 both / 36 only-legacy / 51 only-ours (99.98% agreement); uncertainty 1,087 both / 5 / 5; county 99 both / 2 / 5; protocol, country, stateProvince, coordinates: near-exact. Locality semantics ported exactly from OccurrenceService.updateErrorFlags + includesIllegalSuffix (double-quote not single, word-bounded suffix list incl. County); place_unabbreviated rule added (length checks — no abbreviation table needed, closing that half of beeline-kw8.6). Residual disagreements are entirely within-sample field heterogeneity (new bead). Exclusions documented in the script: phylumPlant (12 rows, phase 3), identity-field flags (blocked rows, in legacy_promotion_finding), 2,753 unpromoted rows.

title: Determinations ingestion (expert + volunteer channels)
description: Expert columns → is_expert=true determination events (identifiedBy → determiner_name); VolDet columns → volunteer events. channel='legacy_import'. determination_of_record should then reproduce legacy's precedence.
close_reason: ingest/promote-determinations.sql: expert columns → is_expert=true events (identifiedBy as determiner_name), *VolDet columns → volunteer events with the collector as determiner. Deepest-asserted-taxon resolution on (rank, scientific_name); 256,161 determinations (187,011 expert / 69,150 volunteer), ZERO unresolved (legacy_unresolved_determination view is the loud-failure surface). determination_of_record covers 195,059 specimens (51% — rest await determination, consistent with multi-year lag); top species are plausible PNW bees with correct authorship. Open: determined_on unknowable from legacy (no date column); recorded_at = ingestion time.

title: Taxonomy seeding: animal table from determination columns
description: Resolve phylum/class/order/family/genus/subgenus/specificEpithet/scientificName (expert) and familyVolDet/genusVolDet/speciesVolDet (volunteer) into the curated animal tree. Expert names are free text in legacy — expect variants needing normalization.
close_reason: Curated CSV found at /app/shared/data/taxonomy/taxonomy_*.csv on prod (family,genus,species — 3,314 rows, exported 2026-08-07; local OBP-Server beeTaxonomy.json was empty). fetch-legacy.sh now pulls the newest one. ingest/seed-animals.sql builds the tree: spine + CSV + every verbatim-asserted taxon → 3,567 nodes (3,382 species, 130 genera, 30 subgenera, 15 families, 4 orders, 3 subspecies). Authorship extracted from verbatim scientificName. legacy_taxon_uncurated view lists nodes beyond the curated list for review: 68 species, 68 genera (23 attached above family — no known family), 9 families. Ranks derived from data, not legacy taxonRank (subgenus-in-genus-column etc.).

title: Elevation derivation: provenance and recomputation
description: sample.elevation_m is derived, not collected. Legacy (OBP-Server ElevationService) reads SRTM 1-arc-second GeoTIFF tiles (elevation/N44_W124_1arc_v3.tif pattern) per coordinate and stores the string on the occurrence; values < -10 become empty. It IS in MongoDB, so phase 2 copies it verbatim. Open design: record how a value was derived (source DEM, which coordinate pair), when to recompute (coordinate corrections), and the obscured-record trap OBP-Server notes in ObservationRepository.js:14 — trusted obscured records need elevation from private coordinates, not public geojson. Also: elevation is deliberately absent from required-field QC (reference nonEmptyFields omits it).
notes:
Production survey 2026-08-20 (read-only, ssh beeline → docker mongo, db api-backend): 371,212/383,032 occurrences (96.9%) carry numeric verbatimElevation. Gaps: 11,820 empty — 28 with no coordinates, 11,792 WITH coordinates but no elevation (scattered across years/states: OR-2022 2,602; WA-2025 1,873; BC-2025 1,655; BC prominent overall — possibly missing GeoTIFF tiles or intermittent lookup failures, not a single era). Plus 8 records where verbatimElevation='Corvallis' (locality leaked into the field; all near 44.60,-123.26). Phase 2 implications: ingest verbatim but expect ~3% null; the 8 'Corvallis' values must fail the integer cast into elevation_m and surface as staging findings; re-derivation for the 11,792 is a candidate first use of our own elevation derivation.

Location restructure (2026-08-20): elevation_m now lives in sample_location, making it by construction a property of the believed-true coordinates. Derivation design here should record source DEM + which coordinates, and covers re-deriving the 11,792 legacy gaps.

2026-08-20: elevation_source table added (description, file_name, file_hash) with sample_location.elevation_source_id and a CHECK that elevation_m and its source are both-or-neither — an elevation never arrives without provenance. Legacy import gets one 'legacy verbatimElevation' source row; Beeline-derived values reference the DEM tile by name + content hash. Remaining design here: the derivation process itself (tile acquisition, recompute triggers on coordinate correction, the 11,792 legacy gaps).
close_reason: Derivation delivered: pnpm elevation:derive (src/derive-elevation.ts) fills NULL-elevation sample_location rows from SRTM 1-arc-second tiles in data/dem/, matching the reference dataset + nearest-pixel semantics (validated: 151/155 legacy values reproduced exactly on shared tiles; outliers are half-pixel boundary effects). Provenance per tile via elevation_source (file name + sha256, found-or-created). Recompute trigger = promotion clearing elevation on moved coordinates + idempotent NULL-fill. Obscured trap structurally impossible: derivation reads sample_location, which only holds believed-true coordinates. Live run: 875/995 gaps filled; remainder = 1 SRTM void, >60°N Yukon (SRTM coverage limit), tiles legacy also lacks, and one bogus NZ coordinate (spun off as implausible-coordinates QC rule bead). 74 tiles (1.1GB) rsynced from the legacy server into gitignored data/dem/.

title: Kysely smoke test on kysely-duckdb dialect
description: Hand-written Kysely DB interface for the schema; smoke test insert/select through kysely-duckdb (runoshun) on @duckdb/node-api against in-memory DB with real DDL applied. Fallback candidate: @oorabona/kysely-duckdb. Decides the query layer while switching is cheap (roadmap phase 1).
notes: Outcome: kysely-duckdb 0.4.0 (runoshun) on @duckdb/node-api works — insert-returning with sequence defaults, typed joins, views all pass. Two rough edges: (1) kysely pinned to 0.28.x because kysely-duckdb 0.4.0 imports DEFAULT_MIGRATION_LOCK_TABLE, removed in kysely 0.29 — unpin when kysely-duckdb catches up; (2) its published types resolve kysely's CJS declarations vs our ESM, bridged with a documented cast in src/db.ts. Related: beeline-wot (Drizzle).
close_reason: Closed

title: Operational logging & error reporting
description:
The data model is the audit log for domain events; this issue is the operational layer. Guiding principle from the reference implementation's failures: **failures are loud** — no silent degradation (anonymous fallback, coerced empty results, dropped tails).

Plan:
- Structured JSON logs to stdout (pino); platform handles retention. No log infra to run.
- Sentry for error tracking/alerting: a failed sync_run or unhandled exception alerts a human, never just a null completed_at.
- Pipeline detail (per-page fetches, rate limits, skips) in logs; outcomes stay in sync_run rows.
- Once auth exists: request logs carry user identity. Decide whether reads of sample_true_location get a deliberate access log — may become a compliance need depending on per-atlas geoprivacy answers (docs/questions.md).

Timing: pino from first pipeline code (roadmap phase 2–3); Sentry no later than the web app (phase 4).

title: Legacy export outgrew the CLI's DuckDB budget after #136
description: On the sandbox reseed of 2026-10-04 the legacy:export CLI ran out of DuckDB's 1 GB budget (fly.toml BEELINE_DUCKDB_MEMORY_LIMIT) on its two threads: #136 added staged columns and the per-row method/end date/place join (legacy_occurrence_corrected read twice). Measured locally on the reseeded corpus: 2 threads OOM at 1 GB, 1 thread fits in 512-768 MB. The nightly legacy-export job already sets threads = 1 and fits; the CLI does not. Options: have the CLI set threads = 1 as the job does, or read the per-row fields in the one staged join instead of a second pass over the corrected view. The registry.ts comment's ~600 MB / ~800 MB figures are from the 2026-09-27 corpus, before #136.

title: [bug] auth.test: sign-in rename test fails outside UTC (last_login_at off by the local offset)
description:
test/auth.test.ts "a deployed store's sign-in table is renamed in place, rows and all, and its comments follow the DDL" fails on a workstation in Pacific time and passes with TZ=UTC. Found on main at c94be02 (2026-10-04) while running the suite for beeline-en7i.

    - "last_login_at": 2025-05-01T12:00:00.000Z,
    + "last_login_at": 2025-05-01T19:00:00.000Z,

Seven hours is the PDT offset, so a timestamp without a zone is being read as local time somewhere between the fixture's INSERT and the Kysely read — either the fixture writes a naive TIMESTAMP literal into a TIMESTAMPTZ column under the session's local zone, or the rename path copies through a type that drops the zone. Find which before fixing: if it is the rename path, a deployed store's sign-in times shift by the server's offset on rename, which is a real defect rather than a test one. Fly runs in UTC, which is why nothing has noticed.

title: Error pages a volunteer can act on, not a bare 'Internal Server Error'
description:
When a request fails, the app answers with the plain-text body 'Internal Server Error' (onAppError, src/app/error-reporting.ts). Unknown routes and missing records get bare text too: '404 Not Found', or m.record.notFound via c.text in server.tsx. A volunteer who hits one has no header, no way back, and nothing to tell staff. On 2026-10-01 /specimens returned exactly that against a dev store four migrations behind (a DuckDB Binder Error on determined_on_precision), and the screen gave no hint why.

What a better page does:
- Renders inside Layout, so the header, the menu and Send feedback are still there. Copy comes from the message catalog, like every volunteer-facing view.
- Says what happened in plain words, offers a way back (the previous page, home), and pre-fills the feedback mailto with a reference staff can look up: the Sentry event id from captureException, alongside the page and time the mailto already carries.
- Uses one shape for a failed request (500) and for an unknown address or unreachable record (404). Record pages deliberately answer unreachable with 404 so a URL cannot be probed, so the 404 page must not say which of the two it was.
- Never shows the error message outside development. The redaction rule (CLAUDE.md, Errors and logs) applies: DuckDB errors quote the value they failed on. In development, show the message and the stack. A Binder Error there could add 'is the store behind? pnpm db:migrate --status'.
- Falls back to a static page if rendering Layout itself fails, for example because the store is unreachable: the error page must not depend on what broke.

Not in scope: detecting a store that is behind its migrations at boot. That would be a separate change.
close_reason: Shipped in #118 (90030d2), deployed to the sandbox 2026-10-01.

title: Drop auto-retirement from the correction overlay (ADR 0004)
description:
ADR 0004's merge table says a correction auto-retires when upstream changes TO the corrected value: from then on upstream is taken, and the correction silently stops governing the field. That is surprising — a person asserted a value and the system quietly stops honouring the assertion because of something upstream did — and it will almost certainly never fire: the only implemented instance of the table is the legacy one, whose upstream (Mongo staging) is frozen, and the iNat-observation correction table it was written for was never built. The one iNat-side instance that does exist, the staff locality/coordinate override (beeline-649, beeline-942), already deliberately does without it: "nothing auto-retires — the override stands until a person removes it."

Where it lives:
- docs/adr/0004-correction-overlay.md — the merge table row "changed to the corrected value → auto-retires", and the "Resolution and retirement are recorded … superseded_by_load_id latch" bullet.
- ingest/promote-legacy.sql — legacy_correction_state's `WHEN staged_value = coalesce(c.new_value, '') THEN 'retired'` branch, and the header comment above it.
- src/promote-legacy.ts — the correctionsRetired count in the promotion report.
- test/legacy-corrections.test.ts:45 — "upstream converging to the corrected value retires the correction".

The one load-bearing use to preserve: beeline-eef's revert. An X→Z→X edit writes an identity event (base = new = staged) that shadows the stale X→Z row, and today the merge classifies it 'retired'. Without the branch it must classify as 'applies' (a no-op, since new equals staged) — not 'conflict'. So the rule becomes: staged equals base OR new → applies; anything else → conflict. Update the comments in src/app/sample-edit.ts:155 and src/app/locality-override.ts:29, which describe reverting as retiring, and test/sample-edit.test.ts:153.

Done when: the ADR's table has no retire row (an amendment noting the change and why, not a silent rewrite), no status value 'retired' exists, the revert test still passes, and upstream converging on the corrected value reads as the correction applying.

title: Determination printing
description:
Idea (Peter, 2026-09-21): support printing determinations, i.e. what a specimen was determined to be.

This is a separate concern from label printing (epic beeline-1kb), not an extension of it. The specimen label records the collecting event and is governed by print runs, field numbers and mailing. Determination printing starts from `determination` / `determination_of_record` and shares none of that machinery.

Open questions:
- Contents: the name through `TaxonName` (italics, subgenus, qualifier), plus the determiner and the year? Sex? Is authorship included?
- Who prints, when, and over which selection of specimens.
- Sheet layout, and whether OBP-Server (~/dev/OBP-Server) ever printed these.
- Whether what was printed needs recording, so a later determination is visible as disagreeing with it.

Probably a question for Arthur and Andony (GitHub issue) before any engineering.

title: pnpm test runs every test twice: vitest reaches into .claude/worktrees
description:
Found 2026-09-18 while working on beeline-hza. test/promote-legacy-merges.test.ts and test/promote-legacy-names.test.ts failed a full 'pnpm vitest run' twice with "Hook timed out in 10000ms" — the beforeEach that calls loadLegacyStaging(conn, FIXTURE) — and passed every time run alone and in three subsequent clean full runs. The cause was machine load: two dev app processes were running alongside the suite. Nothing in the change under test touched legacy loading.

vite.config.ts sets testTimeout: 30_000 and says nothing about hooks, so the hook timeout is vitest's 10s default. The legacy fixtures are the heaviest setup in the suite and sit close enough to it that a loaded runner closes the gap — the same shape as beeline-e5b, and the same reason it is worth pre-empting: a CI runner is a loaded machine by definition.

The fix is probably one line, hookTimeout: 30_000 beside the testTimeout that is already there, on the argument that a setup step and a test step have no reason to be held to different clocks. Worth a moment first on whether the legacy fixture should be that slow: it is the same fixture in several files and each one loads it per test.
notes:
CAUSE FOUND, 2026-09-18, and the bead's first diagnosis was wrong. The suite was not merely running on a loaded machine — it was running TWICE.

There is a git worktree at .claude/worktrees/store-bench holding a full checkout at c861d21, and vitest's default excludes (node_modules, dist, .idea, .git, .cache) do not cover it. So `pnpm vitest run` discovers 92 test files where test/ holds 46, runs every test twice, and doubles the wall clock — which is what pushed the heaviest beforeEach in the suite past vitest's 10s hook default.
