Consequences beyond the timeout, and they are worse than it: a local `pnpm test` reports a pass or a failure for code that is not the working tree, and a run takes twice as long as it should for no information. It would do this in any worktree an agent leaves behind, which is what makes it worth fixing rather than cleaning up.

THE FIX IS THE EXCLUDE, NOT THE TIMEOUT: add '.claude/worktrees/**' to test.exclude in vite.config.ts, keeping vitest's defaults. Raising hookTimeout to match the testTimeout that is already there is then optional and probably unnecessary — with the suite running once, the legacy hooks are nowhere near 10s.

DO NOT DELETE THE WORKTREE. It is `locked`, it carries uncommitted work (bench/, and modified package.json and tsconfig.json), and it is somebody's.
close_reason: Fixed in #121

title: Ingest iNaturalist observation notes, show them on the sample page, and make them searchable
description:
Asked for by Peter in the meeting going through the first print run, 2026-09-18. An iNaturalist observation carries free-text notes (the API's `description` field), where collectors write what no observation field holds: the plant's condition, weather, who they were with, why a count is odd. The synced JSON already contains it (observation_load.content), but nothing reads it: it is not in the observation_field projection (schema/060, defined by observation_current_fields in schema/105), so it reaches no sample and no screen.

Three parts:

1. INGEST. Add the notes to the observation projection. A new column on observation_field goes LAST, always (CLAUDE.md: the refresh inserts positionally and observation_field_stale compares with EXCEPT, so a TEXT column in the middle swaps silently with its neighbour). Decide whether it then lands on sample (a column that follows upstream like the floral host — it is not on the label, so the post-print lock does not apply) or is read through the observation link at query time. Note iNaturalist notes can contain markdown and HTML; store them verbatim.

2. SHOW. On /samples/:id beside the other observation facts, rendered as text and never as markup (escape it; at most autolink). An absent note is ordinary and gets no row, per DetailList's rule. Whether the volunteer's front page or the listings show any of it is open; a long note in a table cell is probably wrong.

3. SEARCH. Include the notes in the /samples and /specimens search box (src/app/listings.ts), which today matches sample number, field number, locality, host and collector with lower(...) LIKE. Measure first: a LIKE over ~63k observations' notes on every search may want its own index or a separate toggle, and the CSV export should say whether it carries the notes.

Privacy: notes are public on iNaturalist unless the observation is private, and Beeline is for people already trusted with the records (CONTEXT.md), so showing them to the collector and to staff raises nothing new; check what a delegate or an impersonating admin sees follows the existing reach rules without special-casing.
notes:
PR #83 (https://github.com/rainhead/beeline/pull/83), 2026-09-18, parts 1 and 2. CORRECTION TO THIS BEAD'S PREMISE: the notes are NOT in observation_load.content. The sync's fields whitelist IS the projection and never asked for 'description', so 0 of the dev store's 64,227 loads carry any. Adding the field is what makes them exist; nothing can be backfilled and no migration could. Existing observations gain notes only as they are re-fetched — the nightly is incremental, so only the Sunday sweep's trailing year returns on its own, and anything older needs A ONE-OFF FULL SYNC that has not been run. Worth it: 31 of 100 sampled observations carry notes, median 9 chars, longest 151; some redundant ('Sample 2'), some the locality nothing else has ('Wallowa Mountain Loop (NF-39), along Gumboot Creek' where place_guess said 'Wallowa County, OR, USA'). Stored verbatim with markup, escaped at render. Read through the observation link, not copied onto sample. Part 3 (search) still open and still wants a measurement — and there is nothing to search until a sync runs.
Parts 1 and 2 landed in #83 (b4e8054), 2026-09-18. STILL OPEN: part 3, search — and before it, the one-off full sync, without which there is nothing to search. CodeRabbit caught that nullif(trim(x), '') stores the trimmed string: fixed in f433855, trim() is the blankness test and never the stored value, with a test pinning markdown indentation intact.
FULL SYNC RUN 2026-09-18, dev store only (Peter asked for it; sandbox not touched). All three projects, unwindowed:

  99706    9,866 fetched   9,866 new    0 unchanged
  166376  14,389 fetched  14,266 new  123 unchanged
  18521   40,144 fetched  40,121 new   23 unchanged

observation_load 64,227 -> 128,480, exactly doubled: the whitelist changed, so every record's canonical JSON changed with it (canonicalJson keeps nulls, so even description:null is a new hash). observation_field_stale is 0 and db:migrate --check reports the store matches schema/*.sql.

The 146 "unchanged" are NOT a dedup gap: 142 observations belong to two of the three projects and 2 belong to all three, so 142x1 + 2x2 = 146 exactly. An observation already re-fetched under an earlier project in the same session dedups by content hash under the next one. Worth knowing that projects overlap at all — nothing else in the store said so, because every previous sync was windowed to a single month.

NOTES RECOVERED: 21,396 of 64,321 observations, 33.3% — higher than the 31/100 API sample suggested.

WHAT THE CORPUS IS, which is the measurement part 3 (search) was waiting for:

  short, under 25 chars      9,644  45.1%
  prose, 25+ chars           7,193  33.6%
  a bare number              2,389  11.2%
  'sample 7' and the like    1,539   7.2%
  three chars or fewer         631   2.9%

So a fifth of it is the sample number typed into the notes box, and it is redundant: of the 2,389 bare numbers, 2,387 also carry a sampleId observation field and 2,296 say exactly the same thing. Only 2 have no sampleId at all, and 91 disagree with it — that last group is the only part worth a look, and it is small.

WHAT THAT MEANS FOR SEARCH: a plain LIKE across notes makes a search for '7' match ~2,300 records that carry no information the sample number did not already carry, on a box whose other columns are sample number and field number — so the numeric noise lands exactly where it does the most harm. The bead's own suggestion of a separate toggle looks right, or excluding notes that match the record's own sample number. Two thirds of the corpus (the prose and the longer short notes) is the part worth searching.

STILL NOT DONE: the sandbox has none of this. It runs the deployed build, which predates the description whitelist, so it needs a deploy of merged main and then its own full sync.
CORRECTION 2026-09-18 (Peter). The note above called the bare-number notes "the sample number typed into the notes box" and "redundant noise". Both are wrong, and the reading they came from is backwards.

Some versions of the iNaturalist app CANNOT set observation fields at all, so writing the sample id into the notes is the only thing a collector in the field can do. The expectation is that they copy it into the sampleId field later, at a computer with a web browser. The notes are a STAGING AREA, not a mistake.

So the 2,296 bare-number notes that match the sampleId field are not duplication to be filtered out — they are the two-step workflow having COMPLETED, and the note is the original record of what the collector wrote in the field. The interesting population is the opposite one: where the copy step never happened.

Measured: of 64,321 observations, 133 carry no sample-number field at all; 11 of those have a digit in the notes; 8 of those never became samples. Six of the eight filled in NO observation field whatever — no count, no collection method — which is the app-limitation signature rather than forgetfulness about one box.

  OPEN SEASON (3, all vinciau, 2026-05-23): notes '2', '1', '1C red cuckoo'
  settled (5): peter_maxwell 'Sample 2 - ground' (2025-07-19), michelesims
  'Sample 3 mesquite' and 'Sample 2' (2025-04-20), brianalindh 'Placeholder
  for collection number 768' (2020-07-01), laustin '$8 Mt' (2019-05-09,
  count 0, probably not a sample number at all)

These are invisible today and that is the defect: with no sample number they are not observation_sample_candidate, so the placeholder row on the volunteer's front page — which exists for exactly this, a thing made in the field and left unfinished — never shows them. Filed as its own bead.

WHAT IT MEANS FOR SEARCH (part 3): searching notes for a number is USEFUL, not noise — it is how you find a record whose copy step has not happened. The earlier worry still holds in the common case, though, since 2,296 notes restate a number already on the record; the fix I guessed at is right for a better reason than I gave, namely excluding a note that merely equals the record's own sample number rather than excluding numeric notes as a class.

title: Derive localities from coordinates ourselves, and suggest them where a locality is flagged
description:
Direction from Peter, in the meeting going through the first print run, 2026-09-18. Today a sample's locality comes from iNaturalist: the first usable component of the observation's place_guess (observation_locality, schema/108), which is free text a volunteer or a geocoder typed, and it is the dominant source of QC flags (qc_rule_locality_format: too long for a label, street addresses, postal towns). A volunteer clears a flag by editing the observation on iNaturalist and guessing at a name that will pass.

Three steps, in order:

1. DEVELOP THE MAPPING. From a sample's true coordinates to a short place name fit for a 3pt label: what gazetteer or layer (GNIS populated places and features, protected-area names, Canadian equivalents for BC), what 'nearest' means (containment first, then distance, with a cap beyond which no name is offered), how the 18-character label limit and the street-suffix rule are met by construction. Measure it against the localities staff have already accepted, split by open season against settled, before anything is shown to anyone.

2. SUGGEST IT WHERE A LOCALITY IS FLAGGED. On the flag's line on the front page and on the sample page, offer the derived name with a copy-to-clipboard button, so the volunteer pastes it into iNaturalist rather than inventing one. iNaturalist stays the authority; Beeline only proposes. (CONTEXT.md, Staff override already anticipates 'accepting a machine-proposed rewrite' for staff.)

3. EVENTUALLY, PERHAPS, stop using iNaturalist as the authority for locality at all: Beeline derives it and the observation's place_guess becomes evidence rather than source. That changes locality from Upstream to Derived in CONTEXT.md's Data handling terms, and with it what the post-print lock and the divergence comparison (beeline-1kb.17) mean for locality. Not decided; do not build toward it until steps 1 and 2 have shown the mapping is good enough.

Related: the county arriving from iNaturalist with a disambiguating suffix (beeline-gr7, fixed 2026-09-18) is the same family of problem — text iNaturalist wrote for its own purposes ending up on a label.

title: Show every time on the site in the viewer's own timezone, marked up with <time>
description: Peter, 2026-09-18, from the print-run demo: instants were rendering in the server's zone (UTC on Fly), so a run prepared at 2:28pm Pacific read 9:28 PM. The stopgap shipped the same day formats every instant in America/Los_Angeles by name (m.format.dateTime and m.format.day in src/app/messages/en.ts; m.format.date stays zone-free for DATE columns, which arrive as UTC midnight). What is wanted: read the person's timezone — iNaturalist's user record carries a time_zone, and the browser knows its own (Intl.DateTimeFormat().resolvedOptions().timeZone) — and display every time on the site in it. Render each instant as a <time datetime=ISO> element so the markup carries the exact instant whatever is shown, which also lets a small island re-format in the browser's zone without a round trip. Decide the precedence (iNat profile vs browser), where the choice is stored (session? cookie like scope?), what a signed-out page does, and what CSV exports say (probably ISO with offset, unchanged). The front page's schedule note ('every morning at 2am Pacific') names its zone deliberately and should keep doing so.

title: observation_place.county_name carries iNat's disambiguation suffix ('Lincoln County, US, WA')
description: Found freezing a rehearsal print run on the dev store (beeline-1kb.2, 2026-09-17): 54 samples carry a county like 'Lincoln County, US, WA', 'Washington , US, ID' or 'Washington County, US, ID', which is inat_place.name verbatim for the handful of admin_level-20 places iNaturalist disambiguates by appending ', US, <state>'. Most counties arrive bare ('Benton'). On a label that prints as 'USA:WA:Lincoln County, US, WACo Sprague' (39 characters, flagged 'location line long' on 3 labels). The reference implementation papered over two of these in its abbreviation table ('Lincoln , US, WA' → 'Lincoln'); the right fix is at the source: observation_place.county_name (schema/107) should strip the ', US, XX' suffix and probably the trailing ' County', then the fill-only refresh will not fill them again — the 54 already filled need a one-off correction or a re-fill, which is a decision. Split the count by season when measuring.
close_reason: Fixed in #79 (f94b2a7), deployed 2026-09-18: observation_place takes the name before the comma, migration 0032 repaired the samples already filled (81 sample changes recorded at boot on the sandbox), and countyName in src/label-text.ts refuses the suffix regardless. It reached 172 labels in the first run anyone prepared before it was fixed; leaving it for later was the wrong call.

title: Flaky test: the scheduler's shutdown grace test fails under full-suite load
description: test/jobs.test.ts, 'past the grace the job is interrupted: its next step refuses and the failure names it', failed once in a full 'pnpm vitest run' on 2026-09-17 and passed three times out of three run alone, and again in the next full run. Nothing in the change under test touched the scheduler (it was a table component refactor), so this is timing: the test races a grace period against the machine's load. Found while working, not reported. Worth making the grace injectable or the clock fake before it costs a CI run.
notes: PR #81 (https://github.com/rainhead/beeline/pull/81), 2026-09-18. The 20ms-grace-vs-60ms-sleep race is gone: the test waits for the shutdown signal to abort, which is the grace expiring made observable. NOT a confirmed diagnosis of the original one-off failure, which did not reproduce. Two candidate mechanisms were tested and ruled out: a blocked event loop does not reorder the two timers (Node runs expired timers in expiry order), and conn.interrupt() cannot reach the write that records the failure, because the test's Kysely opens its own connection off the instance.
close_reason: Closed

title: Count the samples with no recorded coordinate uncertainty, open season against settled
description: Carried over from GitHub issue #22 (https://github.com/rainhead/beeline/issues/22) when it closed. The coordinate-uncertainty rule, at 100 m or at 250 m, cannot see a sample that records no uncertainty at all, so however tight the limit it does nothing for them. The issue gives two figures that do not agree, 14,274 printable samples in its body and about 34,000 records in a later comment, probably counting different things (samples against specimens, or printable against all). Re-measure rather than copy either: how many samples have coordinates and no uncertainty, split by season.started_on into the open season and the settled ones, and by where the coordinates came from (iNaturalist against the legacy import). If the open-season number is small this is historical residue and needs nothing; if it is live and growing it becomes a question for staff, on GitHub, about whether a missing uncertainty should itself be flagged.
notes:
MEASURED 2026-09-18 on the dev store (67,887 samples; 75 have no location row at all).

Samples with coordinates and no recorded uncertainty, by season and by source:

  open season  inat_public     11,289    903 missing   8.0%
  open season  legacy_import       74      0 missing   0.0%
  settled      inat_public     47,985  8,223 missing  17.1%
  settled      legacy_import    8,464  7,770 missing  91.8%

Printable samples only: 900 in the open season, 13,529 settled (14,429 together,
on which 93,828 specimens sit).

ANSWER: historical residue, shrinking. Not a live gap, so nothing is wanted —
which is the disposition the bead named for this outcome. By year of date_end
the iNat-sourced rate falls monotonically and never once rises:

  2018 37.4%  2019 19.5%  2020 32.2%  2021 31.2%  2022 17.7%
  2023 15.5%  2024 11.6%  2025  9.9%  2026  8.0%

The settled bulk is the legacy import, which carries no uncertainty at all —
90-100% missing every year through 2024, because production Mongo has no such
field. It dies out with the import itself (476 samples in 2025, 74 in 2026).

NOTHING IS BEING DROPPED. Of the 903 open-season samples, ZERO have an
observation that carries positional_accuracy or public_positional_accuracy:
iNaturalist genuinely has no accuracy circle for any of them, so no promotion
fix is available and no rule can conjure one. The 304 settled samples where
upstream does carry an accuracy and the store does not are all legacy_import
with specimens already minted — the post-print lock working as designed, not a
loss.

THE TWO FIGURES IN gh-22 RECONCILE ONE WAY, NOT BOTH. The body's 14,274 is
printable samples with coordinates and no uncertainty and is still right today
(14,429). The comment's ~34,000 matches nothing measurable now: specimens on
those samples is 93,828, all samples missing uncertainty is 16,896. Treat it as
counting something else.

No staff question filed, since the bead conditioned one on the number being
live and growing and it is neither. The rule's blindness is confirmed but
inconsequential: qc_rule_coordinate_uncertainty is
"WHERE coordinate_uncertainty_m > lim.uncertainty_m", and NULL > anything is
never true. Worth reopening only if a downstream consumer (Ecdysis, GBIF) turns
out to require coordinateUncertaintyInMeters, which is beeline-bla's territory.
close_reason: Closed

title: What the Logan bee lab wants to know about volunteers, and what Beeline would need to hold to tell them
description: The USDA bee lab in Logan, Utah is where the BLM surveys' specimens and data are meant to end up, and it wants information about the volunteers: contact details, when and where they were. Beeline holds no email or mailing address for anyone yet. If any of it is passed on, it wants a private satellite with the volunteer's say-so recorded. Blocked on Olivia finding out what they want it for.

title: A per-program list of host plants whose locations are withheld downstream
description: BLM has no embargo except possibly for rare plants; the Washington Native Plant Society's Rare Care program is the same shape; each program and probably each atlas will need its own list. Held in Beeline rather than leaning on iNaturalist's taxon geoprivacy, which obscures the whole observation for everyone. Nothing to build until somebody can say what is on a list; that question is queued for Olivia.

title: A stray volunteer spelling of Osmia ribifloris resolves to the name meant
description: One volunteer determination spells Osmia ribifloris as 'Osmia rubiflorus' (genusVolDet/speciesVolDet), minting a taxon of its own. Confirmed by Peter, 2026-09-15. ingest/taxon-aliases.csv gets the row; verified by a reseed of the dev store.

title: Post-cutover: in-app supply requests, replacing the Google Form
description:
Andony, meeting 2026-09-11: after cutover, give volunteers a way to order supplies in Beeline, replacing the Master Melittologist Supply Request Form (https://docs.google.com/forms/d/e/1FAIpQLSfWAsS8FLDeyaMzybw45TQH_HMteXKxGFbs2hi6wpbirG1_aw/viewform).

What the form is today (read 2026-09-11): the volunteer types their email, name and a full street address on every request, then picks items. Collection boxes (1–2); pins (1–3 envelopes, more by contacting the admin); Avery labels for killing jars (number of sheets); box labels; ethyl acetate for killing jars (a 30 ml bottle, 'I live in Canada', or a larger quantity by contacting the admin); a plastic pipette; extra Kimwipes; a kill jar holder; Bee Atlas stickers (rough quantity); a 2" ruler/photo scale; kill jars, short and tall (a number each); comments. The form notes that shipping happens several times a week and that an order ships once everything is in stock.

What Beeline already covers once it manages addresses (beeline-1kb.6):
- The volunteer is signed in, so name, email and address stop being retyped, and stop drifting away from the address specimen labels are mailed to. The form is effectively a second address book right now.
- The Avery mailing labels (beeline-1kb.16) could print shipping labels for supply orders as well.

Discovery:
- Who fulfils orders today and how. Do they work from the form's response sheet? What do they mark when an order ships, and do they need a queue with states (requested → waiting for stock → shipped)?
- The item list changes. Should staff be able to edit it without a code change? Are some items limited by atlas or by program, and does 'Bee Atlas stickers' mean each atlas has its own?
- Shipping limits the form writes into its choices. Ethyl acetate cannot go to Canada, and larger quantities go through the admin. These are rules about the item and the destination, so they should not live only in the wording of a choice.
- Does anyone outside the program (without a Beeline sign-in) use the form? If so, they need another way to order.
- Whether volunteers should see their own past orders and their status.

Copy is volunteer-facing, so it goes through the message catalog.

title: Post-cutover: replace the pivot tables that summarise recent atlas activity
description:
Andony, meeting 2026-09-11: after cutover, replace or rebuild the existing pivot tables that give staff an overview of recent activity in each atlas. For example: which plants have people been collecting bees from?

This is deliberately scheduled after cutover. Until then the pivot tables keep working from the legacy-format dump (beeline-6q8), so nothing breaks at cutover and this is an improvement rather than a rescue. Deferred until 2027-01-01.

Discovery first:
- Where do the pivot tables live? Presumably spreadsheets on the OSU/MM Drive built from the legacy dump. Who opens them, and how often?
- Every view they offer, read off the actual sheets instead of guessed: host plants by atlas, activity by collector, by county, by week, and so on. Which of them does anyone still use?
- What 'recent' means. The store already has a line for it: the open season (season.started_on / settled_sample).

Things Beeline already has that this would build on:
- Atlas scope and staff reach, from the listings (/samples, /specimens), so an atlas's staff see their own atlas.
- Floral hosts as iNaturalist taxa on the sample, which makes 'what plants' a join. docs/surrounding-systems.md already treats plant–pollinator associations as a query product that landowner reports and Melittoflora will want too, so this should be the same query and not a third one.

Once it is built, check whether anything else still reads the legacy dump. If nothing does, beeline-6q8's nightly job can be retired.

title: db:migrate --check applies pending migrations before it diffs
description: migrations/README.md and the pnpm scripts describe --check as 'diff the store against schema/*.sql', and --status as read-only. In src/migrate.ts only --status skips migrate(): --check runs every pending migration first and then diffs. Found 2026-09-10 running --check on the local dev store to decide whether it was safe to migrate: it applied 0023 and 0024, failed on 0025 (the store already carried that column), and stopped — leaving the store two migrations further along than the question intended. Harmless there, and each migration is its own transaction, but a read-only flag that writes is the one shape of surprise a migration tool should not have, and the deploy script's pre-migrate backup runs only when --status shows PENDING, which a stray --check beforehand would have consumed. Either make --check read-only (diff without applying, reporting what is pending separately) or rename it so the name says it migrates. Also worth a line in the README either way.
close_reason: Merged in PR #56: --status and --check are read-only; --check is --status plus the drift report; --baseline cannot combine with either; runCli exported and tested.

title: neededTiles fetches for coordinates elevation derivation will never use
description:
src/fetch-dem.ts neededTiles() selects DISTINCT coordinates from sample_location WHERE elevation_m IS NULL, but derivation works from sample_elevation_pending (schema/170), which drops coordinates too vague to place — the 100 m elevation_derivation_limit, beeline-6vc. The two have drifted: the pending view came later.

So the fetch downloads tiles for rows nothing will ever derive. Caught in practice on the dev store: the only tile of 11 that neither SRTM nor GLO-30 could supply was s08_w122, open Pacific about 2,000 km west of Peru, wanted by exactly one sample whose public (obscured) coordinate carries 1,196 km of uncertainty. Derivation refuses it either way; the fetch asked for an ocean tile to satisfy it.

Fix: read sample_elevation_pending instead, so the fetch set is exactly what derive will use. Small, but it also removes the one class of 'unavailable' tile that is not a real gap — which matters because that list is how someone judges whether a fetch went well.

Not folded into PR #29 (the source change) to keep that merge clean.
close_reason: Merged in PR #54: neededTiles reads sample_elevation_pending, so the fetch set is exactly what derivation reads.

title: The nightly could fetch its own DEM tiles now that no credential is needed
description:
The nightly pipeline (src/app/jobs/registry.ts) derives elevations and reports missingTiles, but never fetches: fetching used to need an ssh key or a forwarded agent, which an unattended job cannot hold. PR #29 removes that constraint — SRTM comes from OpenTopography and GLO-30 from Copernicus, both over plain HTTPS with no credential — so the job could fetch what it is missing and close the loop itself.

Not done in #29 because it is a behaviour change to a scheduled job rather than a fix: it makes the nightly reach the open internet on a timer and download tens of megabytes per new tile. Worth deciding deliberately.

Shape if taken: a step before 'derive elevations' that fetches only the keys the previous derive named, with a cap on how many tiles one run may pull, so a store that suddenly grows a continent's worth of gaps does not spend the night downloading. Nothing is urgent meanwhile — an unfetched tile is a NULL elevation, never a QC finding and never a block on printing (beeline-6vc).

title: Should the elevation derivation limit match the 250 m printing cap?
description:
Peter, 2026-08-29: "if max coordinate uncertainty is 250m, that should be the
cap for deriving elevation as well."

Today the two thresholds differ on purpose. elevation_derivation_limit
(schema/170) is 100 m, set by Peter on 2026-08-27, and the comment beside it
argues the case: an elevation is a stricter claim than a locality string, so a
record can be precise enough to print and too vague to be given a height.
qc_rule_coordinate_uncertainty blocks printing at 250 m.

The proposal is to collapse them to one number. Not measured here as a
preference between two defensible thresholds, but for the argument underneath
it: one number meaning "precise enough to be a record" is a rule the store can
state once, and two thresholds an ADR 0001-style single statement cannot cover
are two thresholds that will drift.

MEASURED on the dev store (2026-08-28 reseed, after elevation derivation had
run), which is NOT what CLAUDE.md's elevation paragraph says - that cites
1,558 unsupportable rows from 2026-08-27, before the reseed, and is stale:

  located samples                                          66,291
  coordinate uncertainty unknown (NULL)                    17,357
  elevations unsupportable at the current 100 m limit         403
  elevations unsupportable at a 250 m limit                    98
  samples with no elevation, uncertainty in (100, 250]        439

So moving the limit to 250 m would:
  - stop calling 305 existing elevations unsupportable
  - make 439 samples newly eligible for derivation

A CONSEQUENCE WORTH THE CHANGE ON ITS OWN. At 250 m the two thresholds
coincide, so sample_elevation_unsupportable becomes a subset of the samples
qc_rule_coordinate_uncertainty already blocks from printing: every
unsupportable elevation is then on a record that cannot print anyway. That
removes the awkward middle class the current split creates - beeline-6vc
recorded 744 unsupportable elevations sitting on records that still print,
which is a state nobody wants to have to explain. Under one threshold it
cannot arise.

THE COUNTER-ARGUMENT, which is the one the 2026-08-27 comment makes and which
this bead should not pretend away: a 250 m horizontal slop in steep terrain
hides a real vertical error, and a DEM answers with a confident integer
regardless. The two claims genuinely are not equally strong. Whether that
matters depends on what an elevation on a label is FOR, which nobody has
written down.

WHAT WOULD SETTLE IT, and is not done here: for the 439 samples in the
(100, 250] band, sample the DEM across the uncertainty radius and report the
spread. If the elevation varies by a few metres across the circle the
distinction is academic; if it varies by hundreds, the tighter limit is
earning its keep and the right answer may be neither number but a
terrain-dependent one. That is a half-day of work and it turns a preference
into a measurement.

IF IT GOES AHEAD: schema/170 (the view is one row, so this is a one-line
change), a migration per ADR 0006, and CLAUDE.md's elevation paragraph, whose
numbers are stale regardless of the outcome. The derive job needs no change -
it reads sample_elevation_pending, which reads the limit.
close_reason: Filed in the wrong tracker. Question issues go on GitHub (Peter, 2026-08-29; docs/agents/issue-tracker.md says so and I reasoned past it). Moved to https://github.com/rainhead/beeline/issues/20 and rewritten for that audience.

title: docs/questions.md: narrow the label-attribution question and record three answers
description:
Four edits to docs/questions.md that this session established but did not
land, since the doc change was never asked for.

1. **Printing Q7 is confused and should be narrowed or dropped.** It asks
   "whose name goes on their labels — the program, or the atlas that happens
   to process them?" A label has six fields (location, coordinates, date,
   collector, method, field number) and carries no atlas or program name at
   all, so there is no slot for the question; the collector's name is on it
   because they collected it. CONTEXT.md already states the handling half
   positively. The only residue is an eventual Ecdysis/GBIF institutionCode,
   which follows physical custody rather than membership. Filed as gh-16 and
   closed there with the reasoning; the doc still carries the bad framing and
   will mislead the next reader. See beeline-1kb.1.2.

2. **Printing Q3 is answered** (Peter, 2026-08-28): no other atlas currently
   prints or mails. Future scope. Delete the question.

3. **Taxonomy Q1-Q3 are answered** (Peter, 2026-08-28): all atlases use the
   current taxonomy until we build something different, after cutover. So
   there is no divergence to model and no contested name reaching GBIF.
   beeline-0zb's stance — defer until a second opinion is actually being read
   — is confirmed rather than changed. Q4 (whether determiners want
   qualifiers beyond cf./aff./nr.) stays open and is Lincoln's.

4. **Add the questions' audience where it is now known.** GitHub issues reach
   Andony and Arthur, who are repo collaborators; Lincoln, Olivia and Karen
   are not, so nothing addressed to them can be an issue. Worth stating in
   the doc's preamble, since it decides the form each question takes.

Also worth recording: gh-13 (geoprivacy), gh-15 (accounts) and gh-17
(printing) now carry the questions they were raised from, so those sections
should point at the issues the way this doc already points at beads.
notes:
Items 1 and 2 landed in PR #44 (merged 2026-09-09), as part of relocating Arthur's walkthrough answers.

1. Printing Q7 (attribution for records belonging to no member atlas) — DROPPED, not narrowed. The section intro now says why in one clause and links gh-16, which holds the reasoning: a label has six fields and carries no atlas or program name, so there was no slot for what the question asked. The taxonomy section's cross-reference, which pointed at 'Printing and mailing 7' and after renumbering landed on a question about duplicate field numbers, now points at gh-16 instead.
2. Printing Q3 (how other atlases plan to print and mail) — DELETED, with the reason recorded: no other atlas currently prints or mails (Peter, 2026-08-28), so it is future scope.
4. Audience — done for the Printing section only, which now splits it: questions 1-3 and 6-7 to Arthur, 4-5 a decision for Peter and Andony.

STILL OPEN, and why this bead stays open: item 3 (Taxonomy Q1-Q3 are answered — all atlases use the current taxonomy until we build something different, after cutover, so there is no divergence to model and no contested name reaching GBIF; Q4 stays open and is Lincoln's), and the rest of item 4 (audience annotations on the sections other than Printing). Both are in the Taxonomy and People sections, which PR #44 deliberately did not touch.

title: Ask Andony: which collectors need iNaturalist accounts of their own
description:
docs/questions.md "People and accounts" Q2 and Q4, which are one conversation
with Andony: who among the collectors needs an iNaturalist account of their
own, and who already has one we have not found.

EMILY CARLSON (Q4). Her 254 samples carry `amelathopoulos` because Andony
typed the records in, not because it is hers. She needs her own account
resolved, not a share of his. Andony is the one person who can say for
certain, since he is the one who entered them. (She was briefly mislinked to

THE HOUSEHOLDS (Q2). Gretchen holds `pandg`; Robert (1,087 samples) cannot
sign in. Same shape for Steve Sheehy under Sarah Malaby's `smalaby` (420) and
Julie Biddle under Tom Robertson's `tom_julie` (363). This no longer blocks
anything — delegation (beeline-oyl) is built and all three grants are
recorded, so the account holder can reach their partner's records. The

Worth knowing before the call: the legacy register already lists separate

Tom Robertson, `pepederson` for Pete Pederson. NONE of the four resolves on
iNaturalist (checked 2026-08-28, api.inaturalist.org/v1/users/<login> — all
404). They are legacy-system account names, not iNat logins, so they are
evidence that the old system treated these people as separate participants,
and no help at all in finding them an account.

WHO CANNOT SIGN IN AT ALL. The legacy system minted synthetic ids in the
9991xxx range for collectors with no iNaturalist account. Twelve of them are
in staging, by record count:

  Pat Wheeler 622, Maureen Beezhold 185, Randy Costello 132,
  Steve Sheehy|Sarah Malaby 102+31, Myrna Anderson 101, Jane Pope 83,
  Steven Olson 78, Alyssa Tollefson 63, Shannon Mayfield 36,
  Jeana Schorr 34, Max Havlik 2

Every one of these is a person with records and no way into the app. Ask

Related: beeline-e85 (unclaimed samples) is the same question from the
