title: DEM fallback beyond the legacy archive (Copernicus GLO-30)
description: The nightly's elevation step reports ~24 tiles that neither data/dem nor the legacy server's archive holds — all for out-of-atlas records (TX, CO/UT, NJ/PA, ON, SK, AB, YT/AK, NZ; ~120 sample locations, 0.2%). Two are unobtainable from SRTM at all (n60/n61 — SRTM stops at 60°N). Elevation is never a QC finding and doesn't block printing, so NULL is acceptable; this bead is the better answer when wanted: fetch missing tiles from Copernicus GLO-30 (public no-auth S3, global coverage incl. >60°N), converted/renamed to the nXX_wYYY naming derive-elevation reads, recorded as their own elevation_source rows. Sandbox currently has the same 74-tile set as dev (rsynced 2026-08-22).
notes:
Implemented (code + tests green, typecheck clean); NOT yet run for the full tile set.

Verified facts about Copernicus GLO-30 on the public no-auth mirror
https://copernicus-dem-30m.s3.amazonaws.com:
- All 23 missing tiles exist there, including the two SRTM cannot supply (n60/n61) and the NZ one. ~700 MB total; 2 tiles fetched in ~10s.
- Object name is Copernicus_DSM_COG_10_N44_00_W124_00_DEM/<same>.tif, keyed off the SAME southwest corner the SRTM nXX_wYYY name is — confirmed against tile bounding boxes in both hemispheres (S39_00_E176_00 covers lat -39..-38, exactly what s39 means).
- No conversion needed. They are float32 COGs geotiff.js reads directly, so derive-elevation's existing reader works unchanged and no gdal dependency was added.
- Longitude sampling thins toward the poles: 3600 px wide below 50°N, 2400 to 60°, 1800 above. Height is always 3600. derive-elevation already reads each tile's own raster dimensions, so this needed no math change; spot-checked Whitehorse (638.8 m vs actual ~640).

Shape of the change:
- Tiles are keyed (tileKeyFor -> 'n44_w124') and the dataset supplies the suffix: SRTM '_1arc_v3.tif' preferred, GLO-30 '_glo30.tif' fallback. NOT renamed onto SRTM's filename — elevation_source.description would then lie about provenance, a later rsync could collide, and '1arc' is wrong for the thinned tiles. Each GLO-30 tile gets its own elevation_source row described 'Copernicus DEM GLO-30, nearest pixel'.
- ElevationResult.missingTiles now reports tile KEYS (no dataset has them), not one dataset's filename.
- fetchGlo30 downloads to <name>.partial and renames, so an interrupted transfer never leaves a truncated tile for derivation to hash and trust.
- Float samples can be NaN, which no < -10 comparison catches; added a Number.isFinite guard so a NaN counts as a void instead of writing NaN into an INTEGER column.
- No schema change, so no migration.

Remaining: run 'pnpm elevation:fetch' for real (dev, then sandbox) to pull the other 21 tiles.
Code review (two-axis) applied:
- tileKeyFor now zero-pads latitude to 2 digits (n05, not n5). Confirmed against the live service: Copernicus_DSM_COG_10_N05_00_E036_00_DEM -> 200, N5_00 -> 404. Latent for SRTM too; no current data is within 10 deg of the equator, but the fallback's premise is global coverage.
- src/app/messages/en.ts nightly-pipeline description said 'fills missing elevations from the SRTM tiles on disk' — now 'the DEM tiles'.
- Added tileFileName(key, dataset); locateTile returns { dataset, fileName } so callers stop re-deriving the path it just proved exists.
- Documented the registration difference: GLO-30 COGs carry GTRasterTypeGeoKey=2 (point-registered) and span the degree in 3600 rows where SRTM uses 3601, so the reference formula lands one row (~30 m) north on GLO-30. Kept the legacy ElevationService arithmetic — matching it is the point for SRTM, and 30 m is immaterial for an elevation.
- Test no longer depends on a void left by an earlier test (asserts a delta around its own row); verified it passes in isolation.
Not done, deliberately: no schema COMMENT ON change (comment-only, and it would owe the sandbox a migration for nothing); no unit test that downloads a real 20 MB COG.

Re-verified after refactor at real scale on a throwaway DB copy: 203 SRTM tiles + 2 GLO-30 tiles, 53741 elevations, each elevation_source described by the dataset it actually came from. Anchorage 53 m and Atiamuri NZ 228 m unchanged.
Dev fetch + derive DONE (2026-08-24).

The gap set had grown since this bead was filed: 130 tiles needed, not 23. 103 came from the legacy archive, 26 from GLO-30, 1 from neither. 12552/12553 gaps filled; data/dem is now 4.4 GB (26 glo30 tiles).

122 sample locations now carry GLO-30 elevations (3–3359 m), matching this bead's '~120 sample locations, 0.2%' estimate exactly. elevation_source now holds 177 SRTM + 26 GLO-30 + 1 legacy-import rows.

The latitude-padding fix earned its keep on the first real run: one of the needed tiles is s08_w122, which the unpadded code would have asked for as s8_w122.

The single remaining NULL is sample 21290 ('USA/OR/Corvallis', sample_number 562) at -7.079786,-121.581916 — open Pacific, ~1200 km of coordinate_uncertainty_m (1196135) on an inat_public record. No DEM covers open ocean, so NULL is the right answer and s08_w122 is correctly reported unavailable. The existing coordinate_uncertainty QC rule already flags it; 77 locations exceed 10 km uncertainty. Nothing to do here.

SANDBOX STILL PENDING, and it is not simply 'run the same command':
- scripts/deploy-maderas.sh deploys origin/main, so the sandbox cannot read _glo30.tif tiles until this change is committed, pushed and deployed — old code only looks for _1arc_v3.tif.
- Per ADR 0005 exactly one process holds beeline.duckdb, and the app holds it, so 'pnpm elevation:fetch' cannot open the sandbox store while beeline is running. Fetching there means either downtime or, better, rsyncing the 26 tiles onto maderas:dev/beeline/data/dem/ and letting the nightly's in-process 'derive elevations' step pick them up with no downtime and no DB contention.
Shipped to the sandbox 2026-08-24. Deployed d5d840d to maderas (that deploy also carried e7474a5 and applied migration 0007, which was unpushed and rode along on the push). Then rsynced tiles into maderas:dev/beeline/data/dem/: 26 GLO-30 (833 MB) plus the 103 SRTM tiles the sandbox was missing (2.5 GB). Sandbox now has full tile parity with dev: 203 tiles, 26 of them GLO-30, 4.5 GB, 32 GB free.

Verified by sha256 on both ends (identical hashes matter here — elevation_source.file_hash is a sha256 of the file, so the sandbox produces byte-identical provenance rows rather than a divergent set).

No downtime and no DB contention was needed: the tiles just have to be on disk, and the nightly's in-process 'derive elevations' step picks them up. Confirms the approach noted above — never run elevation:fetch against a deployed store, since it opens beeline.duckdb directly and the app holds it (ADR 0005).

Follow-up filed: beeline-6vc (refuse to derive elevation above a coordinate-uncertainty threshold).
Done. Tiles fetched for real in dev and on the sandbox (26 *_glo30.tif alongside the 177 SRTM tiles, 203 total, both hosts on d5d840d).

The sandbox nightly-pipeline at 2026-08-24 02:00 confirms it end to end: 'elevation 182/182 filled' with an EMPTY missing-tiles list — every gap closed, including the n60/n61 tiles SRTM cannot supply.

Dev has exactly one gap left, and it is not a DEM problem: sample 21290 at -7.079786/-121.581916 with coordinate_uncertainty_m = 1196135. That is open South Pacific ocean 1,196 km wide — no DEM publishes ocean tiles, so tile s08_w122 will never exist in any dataset. The sample already trips the blocking qc_rule_coordinate_uncertainty finding, which is the right place for it; elevation stays NULL, which the bead already accepts.
close_reason: GLO-30 fallback shipped and proven: sandbox nightly filled 182/182 elevations with no missing tiles.

title: In-app sample creation (trap-sample entry interface)
description: Creating a sample in the app — today iNat sync and the legacy import are the only data entry points, and the in-app editor (beeline-2c3.8) only edits samples that already exist. The roadmap defers this past cutover because the design is unknowable until the staff registry questions come back (docs/roadmap.md). When it arrives it also changes the correction story: app-created samples have no staging row to anchor corrections on, so they'd be app-owned rows edited directly (no overlay needed) — a third population alongside iNat-backed and legacy-staged. Related: beeline-2c3.9 (specimen row add/remove) has the same row-creation shape.
notes: 2026-09-10 (Peter, prepping for the Andony meeting): confirmed as a requirement — UI for DESIGNATED collectors to create trap samples. 'Designated' implies a per-person permission the model does not have yet (there is person_admin and nothing finer; per-atlas roles are beeline-7c1). Trap protocol / site / servicing questions in docs/questions.md are still open with Lincoln, Olivia and Karen and still shape the form. Whether this is needed before the December cutover or after is not yet stated; the roadmap currently defers it past cutover.

title: Post-launch: per-collector OAuth pulls instead of (or alongside) project pulls
description: Open question (Peter, 2026-08-20): migrate to pulling collectors' observations only after they have logged into Beeline once, using their own OAuth token. What it buys: a user's own token always sees their own private coordinates (the obscured-untrusted QC category vanishes for logged-in collectors — no project-trust opt-in campaign); OAuth login IS the person↔iNat-account mapping (replaces register heuristics; note it claims shared accounts like molfamily for whichever human logs in, it cannot split them); authorization aligns exactly with iNat's permission model rather than leaning on curator powers; per-user syncs are small. Costs to weigh: coverage gap for never-logged-in or lapsed collectors (specimens could arrive physically with no Beeline record — today's project pulls catch everything); label printing gated on collector onboarding (feature or bottleneck?); token lifecycle at scale (hundreds of stored secrets, revocation, per-user refresh failures re-introducing the silent-downgrade hazard distributed across users — iNat OAuth access tokens are long-lived, which helps). Likely landing: hybrid — project pulls keep the public projection for awareness/completeness (and deletion detection), per-user tokens upgrade provenance where present. Relates: beeline-zcf.6 (trusted access), beeline-gju (person↔account mapping).

title: Pronouns: multiple sets on profiles, vocabulary, i18n
description: Noodle & confirm later (Peter, 2026-08-20): profiles may display multiple pronoun sets, but a machine always uses one — suggests stored value stays single-valued (the machine's choice) even if profile display widens. Constraint: the site should be multilingual (English, Spanish, Canadian French), so prefer a closed vocabulary of options we can translate — grammatical-gender rendering differs per language (Spanish elle/elle-a endings, French iel + accord). State of the art unresearched. Current: person.pronouns CHECK ('he','she','they'), null = unstated, render neutrally.
close_reason: Superseded by beeline-6bw: Peter decided 2026-08-27 to remove pronouns from the system entirely — sensitive and unnecessary, and anyone who wants to state theirs can use a free-text profile page. The vocabulary, multiple-sets and i18n question this bead held dissolves rather than being answered; the reason it was hard is the reason not to hold the data.
